REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(Identification of Sectoral Opportunities in Regions of Georgia – Least Cost Selection)

Country: Georgia

Project Name: The Relief and Recovery for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs)

Project No: P173975

Loan No. 9239-GE

Assignment Title:  Identification of Sectoral Opportunities in Regions of Georgia

Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): GE-GEDC-CS-LCS-03

Implementing Agency: JSC Georgian Economic Development Corporation

Date: 07.10.2026

The Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development of Georgia (MoESD), within the Relief and Recovery for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) Project supported by the World Bank, intends to apply part of the loan proceeds to support the identification and assessment of sectoral and business opportunities across the regions of Georgia, with a focus on regional and municipal competitive advantages, value-chain potential, and actionable investment and business opportunities.

The Project, Relief and Recovery for MSMEs, will be implemented nationwide and will consist of four components:

Component 1 – Financial relief and recovery for MSMEs

Component 2 – Digital payments & financial infrastructure upgrading

Component 3 – Project management and monitoring

Component 4 – Contingent Emergency Response Component

A substantial portion of the Project activities fall under Component 1. Component 1 is implemented by JSC Georgian Economic Development Corporation (GEDC) (hereinafter – Client). It comprises of the following sub-components:

  • Sub-component 1.1 provide micro-grants to finance working capital and fixed assets for micro and small firms.
  • Sub-component 1.2 co-finance interest payments on loans underwritten by participating financial institutions (PFIs).
  • Sub-component 1.3 provide partial credit guarantees for loans issued by PFIs.
  • Sub-component 1.4 provide technical assistance to MSMEs in COVID-proofing, strengthening managerial skills, and digitalization through establishing Consulting Centers in the regions of Georgia (Growth Hubs - hereinafter GHs) to deliver specific services to MSMEs locally.

This Assignment:

The assignment consists of conducting a study to identify and prioritize sectoral opportunities across the municipalities and regions of Georgia.

The study shall:

  • Analyze Georgia’s existing and potential sectoral strengths at the national level, including established and emerging sectors, infrastructure, market trends, and other factors relevant to identifying economic and investment opportunities in the regions of Georgia;
  • Assess competitive advantages and sectoral opportunities at the municipal level across the regions of Georgia, identifying existing specializations, underutilized assets and capabilities, and opportunities for expansion, upgrading, diversification, and new sector development;
  • Map existing and potential value-chain linkages across municipalities and regions, identifying how production, processing, services, logistics, distribution, export, and other value-chain functions are currently distributed or could be developed across different locations;
  • Validate and refine the analytical findings through consultations with relevant institutions, businesses, and other stakeholders at the national, regional, and municipal levels;
  • Identify specific investment and business opportunities within the shortlisted priority sectors and locations, and prepare preliminary investment-readiness assessments for a prioritized shortlist of opportunities, covering the principal market, location, infrastructure, workforce, financing, regulatory and other enabling conditions and constraints;
  • Develop conclusions, recommendations, and a prioritized action plan for advancing the identified opportunities, including recommended next steps, required institutional and policy actions, potential business-support measures, further studies where required, and indicative short-, medium-, and longer-term priorities.

The outcome of the assignment shall enable the relevant stakeholders to direct investment promotion, regional development, and business support efforts toward the municipalities, regions, and sectors where competitive advantage and readiness are strongest.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following link:

https://docs.google.com/document/d/1xfvaZ4O82S6uumDtD2wDbG5aBNd0jEVb/edit usp=sharing&ouid=114433811295150382465&rtpof=true&sd=true

GEDC now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The minimum selection criteria are:

  • Be a legal entity registered under the law of Georgia on Entrepreneurs, with no outstanding tax liabilities (unless deferred or exempt by law);
  • General Experience – The Consultant shall have at least six (6) years of demonstrated professional experience in economic research and advisory services, regional or local economic development, sectoral analysis, competitiveness assessment, investment-related advisory services, or other fields directly relevant to the Assignment.
  • Specific Experience - The Consultant shall have successfully completed, within the last six (6) years, at least three (3) regional economic development studies, sectoral opportunity assessments, and/or economic assessments, at least one (1) of which involved municipal- or regional-level analysis in Georgia or a comparable country.

To be considered for the selection, the interested consulting firm must submit the following documents:

  1. A brief description of the company’s background and organizational structure, including the year of legal registration/incorporation and an extract from the Registry of Entrepreneurial and Non-entrepreneurial (Non-commercial) Legal Entities. In the case of a Joint Venture (JV), this information shall be provided for each JV member.
  2. To demonstrate compliance with the experience requirement above, the Consultant shall provide a list of completed assignments under the contracts which shall include: 
  • Assignment name,
  • Scope (brief description of the deliverables/outputs),
  • name of clients and country of assignment,
  • duration (start and end dates), 
  • Contract Value (if was done in a form of a Joint Venture (JV) or sub-consultancy, the amount paid to the consultant), if was done in a form of a joint venture or a sub-consultancy, the Consultant’s role/involvement.

Note: To support the preparation of Expressions of Interest (EOIs) and facilitate the assessment process, interested Consultants are provided with an experience form. Consultants are requested to complete this form in line with the requirements outlined above.

The Form is available at the link below:

https://drive.google.com/file/d/1efb3T6xdt7EvotIWpGeFBN7tPpXU0-Cb/view?usp=drive_link

        3. Proof of completion of similar contracts (contracts and respective delivery and acceptance certificates); Where confidentiality obligations apply, the firm may provide other information or documents that enable the relevant experience to be confirmed without breaching such obligations.

When evaluating jointly performed projects, only the experience and scope of work actually performed by the relevant firm and capable of being confirmed by the information submitted shall be taken into account.

Joint Venture (JV) Requirements – Consultants may form a Joint Venture consisting of a maximum of two (2) member firms. The JV members shall jointly demonstrate compliance with the General and Specific Experience requirements specified above.

The JV shall demonstrate at least six (6) years of relevant professional experience and at least three (3) successfully completed regional economic development studies, sectoral opportunity assessments, and/or economic assessments within the last six (6) years. At least one (1) of these studies shall have involved municipal- or regional-level analysis in Georgia or in a comparable country.

The Lead Member of the JV shall have successfully completed at least one (1) of the three (3) required studies.

The experience and qualifications of sub-consultants shall not be taken into consideration for the purpose of meeting the above qualification requirements.

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Least-Cost Based Selection (LCS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations. Shortlisted Consultants will be invited to submit technical and financial proposals. Only the Consultants whose technical proposals achieve at least the minimum technical score specified in the RFP will have their financial proposals opened, and the Consultant offering the lowest evaluated price will be selected and invited for negotiations.

The attention of interested consulting firm is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” July 2016, revised November 2017, revised August 2018 and revised November 2020 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

Interested consulting firm may obtain further information by email: gmaisuradze@gedc.ge.

Expressions of Interest in English language must be submitted electronically to the address below not later than October 22, 2026, at 17:00 (Tbilisi Time). The required documents (attached to the EOI) may be submitted in Georgian.

To: JSC Georgian Economic Development Corporation

Attn: Guranda Maisuradze, Procurement Specialist

E-mail To: gmaisuradze@gedc.ge

Please include the title of the announced selection in subject line of the email.

The information should demonstrate experience relevant to the assignment, including project financial reporting, expenditure eligibility, Designated Accounts, withdrawal applications, internal controls, and preparation of audit opinions and Management Letters.

Experience shall be attributed to the legal entity that performed the services. Where an assignment was undertaken through a joint venture or another association, identify the firm’s actual role and the services it performed.

D. Management and Quality Assurance Capacity

Describe:

- The firm’s organizational structure and capacity to manage periodic audits over the assignment period;

- Its procedures for maintaining auditor independence, identifying conflicts of interest, and safeguarding confidential information;

- Its audit quality management, supervision and internal review arrangements;

- Its procedures for addressing client complaints concerning professional performance or report quality; and

- Its capacity to deliver reports in English, Uzbek and Russian within the required deadlines.

- Information on relevant professional affiliations or quality certifications may be included, where applicable.

E. Relevant Assignment References

F. Eligibility and Independence Declaration

The Expression of Interest shall include a declaration signed by an authorized representative confirming that:

- The firm has reviewed this notice and the Terms of Reference;

- The firm is included in the applicable World Bank – ECA – List of Eligible Audit Firms;

- The information and assignment references submitted accurately reflect the firm’s qualifications and experience;

For a joint venture, the declaration shall cover each member.

 

6. Shortlisting Criteria

Subject to compliance with the eligibility requirements in Section 4, Expressions of Interest will be assessed against the following firm-level criteria:

- Relevant experience in providing financial statement audit services in accordance with ISA;

- Relevant experience in auditing projects financed by the World Bank or other international financial institutions;

- Technical capacity relevant to the audit scope, including examination of project expenditure, financial reporting, Designated Accounts and internal controls; and

- Managerial and organizational capacity, including audit quality management arrangements and capacity to undertake the periodic audits and reporting requirements throughout the assignment.

 

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage. Their qualifications and experience will be assessed during evaluation of the technical proposals in accordance with the Request for Proposals.

No Financial Proposal is required at the Expression of Interest stage.

 

7. Selection Method and Conflict of Interest

A Consultant will be selected using the Least-Cost Selection (LCS) method in accordance with the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”).

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the Procurement Regulations, which set out the World Bank’s requirements concerning conflicts of interest.

data.notice_text:
SOLICITUD DE EXPRESIONES DE INTERÉS

(SERVICIOS DE CONSULTORÍA – SELECCIÓN DE CONSULTORES INDIVIDUALES)

Costa Rica

Proyecto EnABLE Costa Rica – Proyecto Nacional de Apoyo a la Inclusión Social en el Programa de Reducción de Emisiones del FCPF

Número de Donación: P179757 / TFOC9130-CR

Títulos de los Servicios:

Contratación CR-FUNBAM-574465-CS-INDV Consultor/a Social: Género y Salvaguardas del Proyecto ENABLE

Contratación CR-FUNBAM-574466-CS-INDV Técnico/a en Procesos Educativos del Proyecto ENABLE

 

La Fundación Banco Ambiental (FUNBAM), en su calidad de Agencia Administradora del Proyecto EnABLE Costa Rica, ha recibido recursos financieros del Banco Mundial a través de la Donación P179757 / TFOC9130-CR (Proyecto Nacional de Apoyo a la Inclusión Social en el Programa de Reducción de Emisiones del FCPF), e intenta utilizar parte de esos recursos para la contratación de servicios de consultoría.

Los servicios de consultoría (“los Servicios”) comprenden la contratación de dos (2) consultores/as individuales, cada uno/a con alta dedicación, por un período inicial de doce (12) y diez (10) meses, renovable sujeto a evaluación de desempeño y a la no objeción del Banco Mundial. Los servicios se iniciarán a partir de la firma del contrato y se desarrollarán en la sede de FUNBAM, San José, Costa Rica, con desplazamientos a territorios indígenas según las necesidades del Proyecto. Las contrataciones son las siguientes:

a) CR-FUNBAM-574465-CS-INDV – Consultor/a Social apoyo en temas de Género y Salvaguardas. Apoyará a la Especialista Social y Coordinadora del Proyecto en la verificación del cumplimiento de los instrumentos de salvaguardas ambientales y sociales del Proyecto (MGAS, PCAS y Estándares Ambientales y Sociales EAS 1, 2, 7 y 10 del Banco Mundial) durante la formulación y ejecución de los subproyectos de las Entidades Beneficiarias Principales (EBP) en los 24 territorios indígenas, incorporando el enfoque de género. El monto anual estimado de contratación con el IVA incluido es de US$28.800,00.

b) CR-FUNBAM-574466-CS-INDV – Técnico/a en Procesos Educativos. Liderará la adecuación metodológica de los contenidos técnicos generados por el equipo del Proyecto y su traducción en procesos de formación culturalmente pertinentes dirigidos a las EBP en los territorios indígenas. El monto estimado de contratación con el IVA incluido es de US$22.000,00 para los 10 meses considerados.

Los Términos de Referencia (TDR) detallados de cada contratación se adjuntan a la presente Solicitud de Expresiones de Interés, la cual se publica en el sitio oficial del sistema de compras públicas de Costa Rica, dirección www.sicop.go.cr, opción de avisos institucionales.

FUNBAM invita ahora a consultores individuales elegibles a manifestar su interés en prestar los Servicios. Los/as consultores/as interesados/as deberán proporcionar información que demuestre que poseen las calificaciones requeridas y la experiencia pertinente para la ejecución de los Servicios. Los criterios de preselección para cada contratación son:

a) CR-FUNBAM-574465-CS-INDV – Consultor/a Social en temas de Género y Salvaguardas

  • Bachiller universitario en Trabajo Social, Sociología, Antropología, Psicología, Ciencias Sociales o disciplinas afines.
  • Experiencia previa en al menos una de las siguientes áreas: trabajo con comunidades o pueblos indígenas, enfoque de género, procesos de participación comunitaria o consulta, o acompañamiento social a proyectos de desarrollo.
  • Deseable conocimiento básico de los Estándares Ambientales y Sociales (EAS) del Banco Mundial y/o experiencia de campo en zonas rurales o territorios indígenas.

b) CR-FUNBAM-574466-CS-INDV – Técnico/a en Procesos Educativos

  • Estudiante avanzado con al menos el cuarto año de bachillerato aprobado o Bachiller universitario en Educación, Andragogía, Ciencias Sociales o carrera afín.
  • Experiencia previa en el diseño o facilitación de procesos de capacitación, talleres o materiales educativos, idealmente dirigidos a comunidades o poblaciones con diversidad cultural.
  • Deseable experiencia o formación en adaptación metodológica de contenidos técnicos para su comprensión por públicos no especializados.

Se llama la atención de los/as consultores/as interesados/as sobre la Sección III, párrafos 3.14, 3.16 y 3.17 de las “Regulaciones de Adquisiciones para Prestatarios de FPI del Banco Mundial”, sexta edición de febrero de 2025 (“Regulaciones de Adquisiciones”), que establecen la política del Banco Mundial sobre conflicto de interés. El Banco exige que los individuos que participan en actividades de adquisiciones correspondientes a operaciones de financiamiento para proyectos de inversión (FPI) no tengan conflictos de interés.

La expresión de interés de los servicios de consultoría es requerida bajo el párrafo 7.36 de las Regulaciones de Adquisiciones para los Prestatarios de Financiamiento para Proyectos de Inversión, elaboradas por el Banco Mundial (de febrero de 2025). Los Consultores serán seleccionados con base al método de Selección Abierta y Competitiva de Consultores Individuales, descrito en las Regulaciones antes mencionadas.

Se puede obtener información adicional en la dirección indicada a continuación, en días hábiles de lunes a viernes, de 8:00 a 16:00 horas.

Las Expresiones de Interés deben ser enviadas por correo electrónico a más tardar el día 23 de octubre de 2026 en formato pdf a las 8:00 horas al correo adquisicionesycontratos@funbam.org/ ezuniga@funbam.org. Toda comunicación recibida después de la fecha y hora indicadas no será tomada en cuenta.

Los/as interesados/as deberán indicar en el asunto del correo el número y nombre de la contratación a la que postulan. En caso de postular a ambas contrataciones, deberán enviar una expresión de interés independiente para cada una.

data.notice_text:
GOVERNMENT OF THE REPUBLIC OF MALAWI

 

 

 

Ministry of Health and Sanitation

 

 

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

 

CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL SELECTION

 

 

Country                          : Malawi

Name of Project              : Malawi Health Emergency Preparedness, Response and

                                            Resilience Program

Project ID No                   : P505187

Assignment Title              Senior Project Procurement Specialist

Reference No.                  : MW-MOH-573835-CS-INDV

Date of Issue                     : 12th October, 2026

 

 

 

 

 

 

  1. Background

The government of Malawi is implementing the Malawi Health Emergency Preparedness, Response and Resilience Program (MHEPRRP) funded by the World Bank (IDA). This is a five-year project. The Project aims at strengthening health system resilience and multisectoral preparedness and response to health emergencies in Malawi.

The Ministry of Health intends to source consultancy services for the Senior Project Procurement Specialist to work for the project. The position is tenable at the Ministry of Health Headquarters, Capital Hill, Lilongwe, Malawi.

 

1.1 Project Development Objective (PDO)

The Project Development Objective (PDO) is to strengthen health system resilience and multisectoral preparedness and response to health emergencies in Malawi. The Project will strengthen the preparedness and resilience of the health system and improve early detection and response to Health Emergencies (HEs) through multisectoral approach,

 

Objective of the Assignment

The objective of the assignment is to provide strategic leadership, technical oversight, and performance management of the Project's procurement and contract management function in order to accelerate implementation and ensure the timely conversion of Project resources into goods, works, services, and measurable development results.

The Specialist will ensure:

  • An integrated and realistic procurement pipeline;
  • Effective monitoring of critical procurement activities;
  • Timely identification and resolution of procurement and contract management risks; and
  • Full compliance with the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, the Financing Agreement, the approved Procurement Plan, and applicable Government of Malawi procurement legislation.

3. Duties And Accountabilities 

The Senior Procurement Specialist, under the direction of the Project Coordinator, shall supervise the implementation of all procurement related activities of the Project. This includes ensuring that project activities are implemented in accordance with the World Bank (WB) and Government of Malawi (GoM) Procurement Policies and Guidelines, Project Documents and Agreements and Procureme0nt Operational Manual. The Senior Procurement Specialist shall ensure the timely delivery of goods and services to the Projecting Implementing Entities (PIEs) by supporting the development and maintenance of an effective monitoring, administrative and reporting procurement environment that facilitates and contributes to the achievement of the Project’s goals and objectives.

The specific duties of the Senior Procurement Specialist shall include but not limited to the following:

  1. Strategic Procurement Leadership and Acceleration
  • Provide the supervision and quality check on preparing procurement documentation for goods, works and non-consulting services including Specific Procurement Notices (SPNs), Invitation for Bids, advertisements, Request for Quotation documents, organizing and conducting bid openings, evaluation reports, obtaining the necessary approvals and No Objection Letters from the World Bank where required, arranging for the contract signing, and distribution to the appropriate authorities;
  • Provide executive-level leadership and oversight for procurement and contract management functions.
  • Maintain an integrated procurement pipeline and implementation schedule.
  • Identify procurement bottlenecks and coordinate corrective actions.
  • Advise Project Management on procurement priorities, sequencing, and implementation risks.
  1. . Procurement Governance, Compliance and Quality Assurance
  • Ensure compliance with World Bank regulations and Government procurement requirements.
  • Review major procurement documents and procurement strategies.
  • Promote competition, transparency, integrity, accountability, and value for money.
  1.  Oversight of Complex and High-Value Procurement
  • Review procurement documentation for consulting services including liaising with the technical teams on preparing Terms of Reference (TORs), Requests for Expressions of Interest (EOI), advertisements, evaluating EOIs and creating shortlists, preparing Request for Proposal documents, evaluating proposals, obtaining the necessary clearances from the World Bank where required, assisting in contract negotiations, minutes of negotiations, draw-up draft contracts and making arrangements for contract signing, and distributing to the appropriate authorities;
  • Lead or oversee high-value and strategically important procurement activities.
  • Support evaluations, negotiations, contract awards, and resolution of complex procurement matters.
  1. . World Bank and Procurement Oversight Coordination
  • Serve as the principal procurement focal point for the World Bank and oversight institutions.
  • Coordinate submissions requiring Prior Review and No Objection.
  • Support implementation support missions, audits, and procurement reviews.
  • Facilitate implementation of agreed corrective actions.
  • Lead ensuring compliance with procurement methods and prior review thresholds applicable to the project;
  • Ensure all procurement activities are carried out in accordance with the agreed procedures, including the Financing Agreement; the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations; and Government of Malawi Public Procurement and Disposal of Public Assets Act;
  1. Contract Management and Delivery Oversight
  • Establish and oversee a robust contract management framework.
  • Lead in coordinating responses to inquiries and communicate the results of the evaluation process to bidders or consultants, in keeping with World bank’s Procurement Regulations;
  • Lead in handling bidders and consultants’ complaints and debriefings by ensuring that they are all addressed adequately and in a timely manner and to maintain a complaints database;
  • Monitor contract milestones, deliverables, guarantees, warranties, insurance, and payments.
  • Advise management on contract variations, claims, disputes, and extensions.
  1.  Procurement Risk, Integrity and Complaints Management
  • Maintain a comprehensive procurement risk register and tracker.
  • Identify and mitigate procurement and market risks.
  • Oversee procurement complaints handling.
  • Promote compliance with ethical and anti-corruption standards.
  1. . Procurement Performance Monitoring and Reporting
  • Monitor procurement processing times and implementation milestones.
  • Ensure timely updating of STEP and other approved systems.
  • Prepare quarterly procurement performance reports.
  • Provide procurement inputs to project progress reports and management reviews.
  1. . Supervision, Mentoring and Capacity Building
  • Supervise and mentor procurement staff assigned to the Project.
  • Support resolution of complex procurement issues.
  • Identify capacity gaps and implement capacity-building initiatives.
  • Strengthen sustainable procurement systems within the Ministry of Health.
  • Carry out any other duties as may be assigned by the Project Coordinator from time to time.

4.0 Contract Duration 

The position is available until December 2029, with potential extensions. This a one-year contract and will be renewed annually based on satisfactory performance, availability of resources, and project needs.

 

5.0 Performance Criteria

The following performance criteria will be used to assess the performance of the Senior Procurement Specialist at regular intervals and based upon these assessments the contract with the Ministry of Health may be continued or terminated:

  • > 90 % of Planned Annual procurement activities completed within the approved procurement schedule
  • 100% of procurement processes conducted in accordance with the applicable World Bank Procurement Regulations and approved Procurement Plan.
  • Procurement risks reviewed and updated at least quarterly or whenever significant project circumstances change.
  • 100% of contracts actively monitored, with key deliverables, expiry dates, payment milestones and performance issues tracked.
  • Procurement complaints responded to and resolved/escalated within the applicable timeframe.
  • Procurement files are complete and readily available for supervision missions, audits and post-procurement reviews.
  • Demonstrable savings/value-for-money improvements where appropriate, without compromising quality, competition or compliance.
  • All required procurement documents uploaded/updated in STEP within the prescribed timeframe.

6.0 Deliverables

The Senior Procurement Specialist shall be responsible for the following key deliverables

  • Procurement Acceleration plan within 30 days of commencement, quarterly procurement performance reports, a contract management framework by a specified date
  • Project annual Procurement Plan and periodic updates of the same.
  • Timely Procurement of Goods, Works and Services
  • Bid/Proposal Evaluation and Contract Award (Bidding documents, Request for Proposals, Evaluation Reports, Draft Contracts, etc)
  • Minutes of meetings held throughout the procurement process, including short-listing, Evaluation, interview and negotiation and bid openings all duly signed by panel members/participating parties.
  • Accurate procurement reporting, STEP updates and support to audits/World Bank reviews.
  • Effective management and monitoring of all active contracts.
  • Effective procurement risk management and timely resolution of procurement issues.
  • Monthly, Quarterly, Semi-Annual and Annual procurement reports as inputs into the Project Management
  • Weekly, monthly updates on Procurement Plan tracker to be shared with Project Management

7.1 Qualifications and Experience

The candidate for the assignment shall have the following attributes:

  • The candidate must have a minimum of Master’s Degree in Procurement, Engineering, Economics, Business Administration, Public Administration, Law, or a related field.
  • At least Fifteen (15) years of post-qualification professional experience, of which at least ten (10) years must comprise progressive experience managing procurement and contract management under World Bank-financed project projects involving complex procurement of works, goods, equipment, and consulting services.
  • Experience with Donor funded Projects including the World Bank and Professional membership of a recognized procurement body such as MIPS or CIPS will be an added advantage.
  • Strong organizational, communication and ethical skills in conducting duties in procurement experience
  • Prior familiarity with procurement policies, regulation and the preparation of specific standard procurement documents on World Bank and knowledge of preparation of bid evaluation reports and new procurement reporting in Systematic Tracking of Exchanges in Procurement (STEP)
  • Experience in emergency procurement, health-sector procurement, medical equipment procurement, infrastructure procurement, or other complex public-sector procurement assignments.
  • Sound working knowledge of Government of Malawi public procurement laws and procedures.
  • Demonstrated knowledge of World Bank procurement guidelines, policies, evaluation procedures, and reporting requirements
  • Extensive experience (at least 5 years) using the World Bank STEP system.
  • Proven experience in management of large and complex works contracts
  • Experience in multidisciplinary project environments.

 

 

 

 

7.2   Required competencies

  • Relevant specialized procurement training, including procurement under donor-funded projects and procurement of large works and equipment.
  • Excellent analytical, communication, interpersonal, report-writing, and decision-making skills
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Applications including Excel, PowerPoint and Word.
  • Excellent ability to communicate clearly, accurately and concisely in English, both verbally and in writing.
  • Ability to work in a team and independently with minimal supervision.
  • Ability to work with tight deadlines and deliver exceptional results.
  • Strategic procurement planning and leadership;
  • Strong professional judgement and decision-making ability;
  • Procurement and contract management expertise;
  • Procurement risk assessment and mitigation;
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills;
  • Negotiation and dispute-resolution capability;
  • Effective stakeholder engagement and relationship management;
  • Ability to manage complex procurement portfolios under demanding timelines;
  • Excellent communication and report-writing skills;
  • High standards of integrity, accountability, and ethical conduct;
  • Sound understanding of value for money, competition, transparency, and procurement governance; and
  • Proficiency in STEP and other procurement and contract management

8.0 Reporting

The Senior Project Procurement Specialist will report directly to the Project Coordinator and serve as the principal advisor to Project Management on procurement, contract management, and procurement risk matters.

The Specialist will provide leadership to procurement personnel assigned to the Project and work closely with Technical Teams, Financial Management Specialists, Monitoring and Evaluation personnel, Environmental and Social Specialists, the Public Procurement and Disposal of Assets Authority (PPDA), the World Bank, and other key stakeholders.

 

 

9.0 Location of Employment

The Senior Procurement Specialist will be based at the Ministry of Health and Sanitation, Capitol Hill. The following shall be provided by the Client: office space, furniture, and office equipment, and internet facilities.

10. REMUNERATION

Remuneration will be determined in accordance with the applicable Ministry of Health and Project remuneration framework and will be commensurate with the qualifications, experience, and responsibilities of the position.

 

8. SELECTION METHOD

 

The Consultants will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant Selection

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section I, paragraphs 1.9 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations” Selection and Employment of Consultant under IBRD Loans and IDA Credits and Grants by World Bank Borrowers, July 2016 Revised November 2017 and August 2018 (“Procurement Regulations”- Consultant Guidelines), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

 

Further information can be obtained at the address 9 (a) below during office hours from 08.00 to 12.00 and 13.00 to 16.30 hours local time, except on Weekends and Public Holidays

 

    1. SUBMISSION OF EXPRESSION OF INTEREST

Expression of Interest, clearly marked on the outer envelope with EoI name and reference number must be delivered to the address at 9 (b) below and deposited in the tender box located at Ministry of Heath, 2nd Floor at or before 10:00 hours local time on 23rd October, 2026

The Montenegro has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of CLIMATE RESILIENT FISHERIES AND AGRIFOOD SECTOR DEVELOPMENT PROJECT (CRFASD), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services for PORT MANAGEMENT MODEL & BUSINESS PLAN - MONTENEGRO FISHERY PORT (MFP).    

 

The overall objective of this consultant service (“the Service”) is to develop a practical, financially sustainable and legally compliant Port Management Model and Business Plan for the Montenegro Fishery Port (MFP) in Ulcinj.

 

The assignment shall identify and assess alternative governance and operational arrangements for the management of the port and recommend the most appropriate model taking into consideration the specific characteristics of the fisheries sector in Montenegro, the mixed-use nature of the port, the applicable legal and institutional framework, and long-term financial sustainability requirements.

50

35

15

Posisi : JASA KONSULTAN INDIVIDUAL PENYUSUNAN KONSEP DAN ANALISIS URBAN BIODIVERSITY

Nomor Referensi : ID-KKSDA BAPPENAS-547884-CS-INDV


 

Tugas Utama

Tugas utama Jasa Konsultan Individual Penyusunan Konsep Urban Biodiversity (Urban Biodiversity Analyst) ini adalah untuk melakukan melakukan menyusun landasan teori, konsep pengelolaan Urban Biodiversity beserta praktek baiknya yang dapat digunakan sebagai acuan pada skala tapak, kawasan, hingga kota/wilayah dalam rangka mendukung pembangunan ekosistem, peningkatan kualitas lingkungan hidup, dan mendukung ketahanan kota terhadap perubahan iklim.

Durasi kontrak diharapkan selesai dalam waktu 8 bulan. Kerangka Acuan Kerja untuk ruang lingkup kegiatan secara rinci dapat dilihat pada tautan berikut ini:

https://link.bappenas.go.id/URBAN_BIODIVERSITY 


 

Kriteria Pemilihan

Kualifikasi untuk Jasa Konsultan Individual Penyusunan Konsep Urban Biodiversity (Urban Biodiversity Analyst) adalah sebagai berikut:

  • Memiliki pendidikan minimal S2 jurusan Ekologi/Biologi/Ilmu Lingkungan/ Ekologi Perkotaan/Konservasi Keanekaragaman Hayati yang dibuktikan dengan ijazah pendidikan.
  • Memiliki pengalaman paling kurang 1 (satu) pekerjaan dalam kurun waktu 4 (empat) tahun terakhir baik di lingkungan pemerintah maupun swasta, termasuk pengalaman subkontrak dibuktikan dengan kontrak kerja/ surat referensi pekerjaan/surat keterangan bekerja
  • Memiliki pengalaman kerja minimal 5 (lima) tahun dalam studi biodiversitas/ konservasi dan penyusunan dokumen keanekaragaman hayati, yang dibuktikan dengan kontrak kerja/ surat referensi pekerjaan/surat keterangan bekerja
  • Memiliki pengalaman kerja dalam proyek yang berkaitan dengan penyusunan konsep, pedoman, dan strategi pengelolaan keanekaragaman hayati di tingkat nasional dan atau daerah, serta proyek lainnya yang relevan yang dibuktikan dibuktikan dengan kontrak kerja/ surat referensi pekerjaan/surat keterangan bekerja.
  • Memiliki kemampuan dalam berbahasa Inggris baik lisan maupun tulisan yang dibuktikan dengan sertifikat kemampuan Bahasa Inggris yang masih berlaku/publikasi/laporan dari studi/kajian/hasil pekerjaan yang telah dilakukan.
  • Menguasai perangkat GIS yang digunakan dalam analisis spasial dan inventarisasi biodiversitas perkotaan dibuktikan dengan Portofolio atau hasil pekerjaan sebelumnya.
  • Nilai pekerjaan sejenis tertinggi dalam kurun waktu 10 (sepuluh) tahun terakhir paling kurang sama dengan 50% (lima puluh persen) nilai HPS/Pagu Anggaran yang dibuktikan dengan kontrak kerja/surat referensi pekerjaan/surat keterangan bekerja.






 

Syarat dan Ketentuan Pelamaran:

Pelamar yang berminat harus menyerahkan dokumen-dokumen berikut:

  • Surat pernyataan minat
  • CV lengkap calon konsultan individu

 

Kandidat yang berminat harus menyerahkan dokumen yang dipersyaratkan sebelum 23 Oktober 2026, pukul 12.00 WIB ke alamat Email berikut : ulp@bappenas.go.id 

 

Pokja Jasa Konsultan Individual Penyusunan Konsep Dan Analisis Urban Biodiversity

Kementerian PPN/Bappenas


 

Jakarta,  13 Oktober 2026

data.project_name: Dominican Republic Emergency Response and Resilience Project
data.notice_text:
SOLICITUD DE EXPRESIONES DE INTERÉS. SERVICIOS DE CONSULTORÍA

República Dominicana

Proyecto de Respuesta a Emergencias y Resiliencia de la República Dominicana

Préstamo No.: 9473-DO

Título del Trabajo:  Formulación de Instrumentos Regionales y Municipales de Ordenamiento Territorial y Gestión del Riesgo de Desastres. Región Valdesia y Región Higuamo.

No. de Referencia: DO-MEPYD-475964-CS-QCBS

El Gobierno de la República Dominicana ha recibido financiamiento del Banco Mundial para cubrir el costo del Proyecto de Respuesta a Emergencias y Resiliencia de la República Dominicana a través del Ministerio de la Presidencia y tiene la intención de aplicar parte de los fondos a la contratación de servicios de consultoría.

Los servicios de consultoría ("los Servicios") comprenden la formulación de los Planes Regionales de Ordenamiento y Desarrollo Territorial (PRODT) de las regiones Valdesia y Higuamo; siete (7) Planes Municipales de Ordenamiento Territorial (PMOT) de nueva formulación: tres (3) en Valdesia, correspondientes a Bajos de Haina, Baní y San Gregorio de Nigua; y cuatro (4) en Higuamo, correspondientes a Guayacanes, Hato Mayor, Sabana de la Mar y Monte Plata.

Además, comprenden la revisión, actualización, complementación, apoyo o armonización de cuatro (4) instrumentos municipales existentes o en formulación: dos (2) en Valdesia, correspondientes a San Cristóbal y San José de Ocoa, y dos (2) en Higuamo, correspondientes a San Pedro de Macorís y Yamasá; la formulación de cinco (5) Instrumentos de Delimitación de Suelo Urbano (IDSU), tres (3) en Valdesia, para Villa Altagracia, Yaguate y Nizao, y dos (2) en Higuamo, para Bayaguana y Sabana Grande de Boyá; nueve (9) Estrategias Territoriales de Reducción del Riesgo de Desastres y Adaptación al Cambio Climático, cinco (5) en Valdesia y cuatro (4) en Higuamo; y dos (2) Normas Subsidiarias Regionales de Planificación, una para cada región, con determinaciones territorializadas para doce (12) municipios, en un período de catorce (14) meses calendario, conforme al alcance establecido en los Términos de Referencia. Esta descripción es de carácter general; el detalle de los alcances y especificaciones técnicas se encuentra en los Términos de Referencia (TDR).

El Ministerio de la Presidencia ahora invita a las firmas consultoras elegibles ("Consultores") a indicar su interés en proporcionar los Servicios. Los Consultores interesados deben proporcionar información que demuestre que tienen las calificaciones requeridas y la experiencia relevante para prestar los Servicios. Los criterios de preselección son:

  • Actividad principal, experiencia y trayectoria de la firma. Se requiere una firma con al menos cinco (5) años de experiencia comprobable en el desarrollo de proyectos, planes o políticas relacionados con el ordenamiento y desarrollo territorial en las escalas nacional, regional, municipal y/o de desarrollo urbano. Asimismo, deberá acreditar experiencia específica en la formulación de instrumentos regionales o supramunicipales y de instrumentos municipales de ordenamiento territorial que incorporen zonificación, regulación del uso del suelo, cartografía, normativa y mecanismos de implementación, incluyendo experiencia en la ejecución simultánea de instrumentos correspondientes a distintos niveles de gobierno. Asimismo, deberá demostrar experiencia reciente, adquirida durante los últimos diez (10) años, en gestión del riesgo de desastres y adaptación al cambio climático, acreditada mediante al menos tres (3) contratos o proyectos relevantes o siete (7) años de experiencia institucional acumulada, incluyendo análisis multiamenaza, modelación hidrológico-hidráulica y sísmica, integración de escenarios climáticos y articulación de resultados con instrumentos de ordenamiento territorial e inversión pública.
  • Experiencia específica y comparabilidad de proyectos. La firma deberá acreditar al menos tres (3) proyectos similares en alcance, complejidad, niveles de gobierno y extensión geográfica, ejecutados satisfactoriamente. En conjunto, los proyectos deberán incluir: (i) al menos una experiencia en planificación regional, supramunicipal o de escala territorial equivalente; (ii) al menos una experiencia en formulación o actualización de instrumentos municipales con zonificación, cartografía y normativa de uso del suelo; y (iii) al menos una experiencia que integre gestión del riesgo de desastres, adaptación al cambio climático o Evaluación Ambiental Estratégica. Un mismo contrato podrá ser utilizado para acreditar simultáneamente más de uno de los requisitos de experiencia específica descritos anteriormente, siempre que la documentación presentada permita verificar claramente cada aspecto requerido. Las experiencias deberán permitir verificar, según corresponda, planificación regional y municipal, instrumentos normativos de uso del suelo, información geoespacial, participación territorial, fortalecimiento institucional, portafolios de inversión y estrategias de implementación.
  • Capacidad técnica, organizativa y operativa. La firma deberá demostrar capacidad técnica y de gestión para trabajar de forma simultánea en dos regiones con dinámicas territoriales diferenciadas, manteniendo coordinación técnica, control de calidad, presencia en territorio, gestión documental, producción cartográfica, participación y revisión de productos en paralelo, detallando las capacidades institucionales y herramientas utilizadas por la firma para la gestión de proyectos, producción cartográfica y administración de información.
  • Correspondencia con el alcance de la consultoría. La correspondencia será valorada mediante el análisis integrado de la experiencia y las capacidades institucionales acreditadas frente a la complejidad, escala y condiciones de ejecución de los servicios requeridos. Se considerará la capacidad demostrada para desarrollar de manera simultánea y articulada instrumentos regionales, supramunicipales y municipales de naturaleza y alcance equivalentes a los PRODT, PMOT, IDSU y Normas Subsidiarias Regionales de Planificación previstos en esta consultoría, así como Estrategias Territoriales de Reducción del Riesgo de Desastres y Adaptación al Cambio Climático; procesos participativos y de coordinación multiactor; formulación normativa; gestión de información territorial y cartográfica; Evaluación Ambiental Estratégica; fortalecimiento institucional; y productos de implementación.

Los servicios se prestarán en idioma español e implican presencia activa en el territorio de las regiones Valdesia e Higuamo y en el Distrito Nacional, República Dominicana.

Nota: Los Expertos Clave no serán evaluados en la etapa de preselección.

Para estos fines la firma consultora deberá remitir la documentación de forma clara, estructurada, verificable y directamente vinculada con los criterios de preselección establecidos en la presente Solicitud de Expresiones de Interés (SEI). El documento principal no deberá exceder de cuarenta (40) páginas. Los documentos legales y los soportes documentales presentados para acreditar la experiencia y capacidad declaradas no se computarán dentro de este límite y deberán incorporarse como anexos debidamente identificados, paginados y referenciados. La documentación técnica de soporte no deberá exceder de ciento cincuenta (150) páginas para una firma consultora individual. En caso de APCA, consorcio, joint venture o asociación equivalente, el límite será de ciento cincuenta (150) páginas por cada integrante que acredite experiencia o capacidad técnica, organizativa u operativa relevante para los criterios de preselección. El registro mercantil, la nómina de accionistas y los documentos legales equivalentes no se computarán dentro de estos límites de páginas.

La documentación requerida es la siguiente:

  • Carta de expresión de interés, con datos generales de la firma consultora (firmada y sellada).
  • Detalle de experiencia directa de la firma consultora donde se evidencie: actividad principal y años en el negocio, experiencia relevante, capacidad técnica y de gestión de la firma consultora de acuerdo con los requerimientos arriba mencionados. Para cada experiencia declarada deberá indicarse de manera organizada, como mínimo, el nombre del contrato o proyecto, cliente y país, fechas de ejecución, monto contractual, alcance, rol desempeñado por la firma o integrante de la APCA, productos o actividades efectivamente ejecutados, escala territorial, criterio o criterios de preselección que acredita y referencia exacta del soporte documental presentado.
  • Estructura organizativa general de la Firma Consultora o APCA, con una breve descripción de sus áreas técnicas, capacidades institucionales y recursos permanentes relevantes para la consultoría. En esta etapa no deberán presentarse CV ni se evaluarán las calificaciones de expertos individuales.
  • Registro mercantil actualizado o equivalente en su país de origen.
  • Nómina de accionistas o documento equivalente en su país de origen.

Nota: Toda la documentación que se presente deberá estar en idioma español.

La lista corta estará integrada por un mínimo de cinco (5) y un máximo de ocho (8) firmas consultoras.

Se llama la atención de los Consultores interesados sobre la Sección III, párrafos 3.14, 3.16 y 3.17 de las “Regulaciones de Adquisiciones para Prestatarios en Proyectos de Inversión del Banco Mundial, actualizadas a noviembre de 2020 (“Regulaciones de Adquisiciones”), que establece la política del Banco Mundial sobre conflictos de intereses.

Los Consultores podrán asociarse con otras firmas para mejorar sus calificaciones y deberán indicar claramente si la asociación se presenta como APCA (joint venture, consorcio o asociación equivalente) o como subconsultoría. En caso de APCA, todos sus integrantes serán conjunta y solidariamente responsables de la totalidad del contrato, si resultan seleccionados.

Se puede obtener más información durante el horario de oficina de 08:00 a 16:00 horas, en las oficinas de este Viceministerio ubicadas en la calle César Nicolás Penson núm. 48, Distrito Nacional, Santo Domingo, República Dominicana, o mediante comunicación escrita dirigida al correo electrónico adquisicioneseyr@minpre.gob.do.

Los TDR podrán solicitarse, sin costo, mediante comunicación dirigida al correo electrónico antes indicado, haciendo constar en el asunto la referencia del proceso, o descargarse desde el enlace correspondiente a este proceso, publicado en el Portal de Transparencia del Ministerio de la Presidencia: https://minpre.gob.do/transparencia/compras-y-contrataciones/contratacion-de-firma-de-consultoria-para-la-formulacion-de-instrumentos-regionales-y-municipales-de-ordenamiento-territorial-y-gestion-del-riesgo-de-desastre-valdesia-regional-5-municipales-e-hi/.

Las expresiones de interés deben enviarse por escrito a la siguiente dirección (en persona, por correo o por correo electrónico) hasta el viernes 23 de octubre de 2026, a las 16:00 horas (hora oficial de la República Dominicana).

Viceministerio de Ordenamiento Territorial y Desarrollo Regional

  • A la atención de: Domingo Matías. Viceministro de Ordenamiento Territorial y Desarrollo Regional. Ministerio de la Presidencia
  • Dirección: Calle César Nicolás Penson núm. 48. Distrito Nacional, Santo Domingo, República Dominicana
  • Tel: +1 (829) 213 2707
  • Correo electrónico: adquisicioneseyr@minpre.gob.do

Cuando la Expresión de Interés sea remitida por correo electrónico, deberá enviarse en formato PDF. El tamaño máximo por archivo adjunto será de veinte (20) MB. Si el expediente supera dicha capacidad, podrá remitirse mediante varios correos, indicando en cada envío el número de envío y el total de envíos.

La firma deberá demostrar capacidad técnica y de gestión para trabajar de forma simultánea en dos regiones con dinámicas territoriales diferenciadas, manteniendo coordinación técnica, control de calidad, presencia en territorio, gestión documental, producción cartográfica, participación y revisión de productos en paralelo, detallando las capacidades institucionales y herramientas utilizadas por la firma para la gestión de proyectos, producción cartográfica y administración de información.
  • Correspondencia con el alcance de la consultoría. La correspondencia será valorada mediante el análisis integrado de la experiencia y las capacidades institucionales acreditadas frente a la complejidad, escala y condiciones de ejecución de los servicios requeridos. Se considerará la capacidad demostrada para desarrollar de manera simultánea y articulada instrumentos regionales, supramunicipales y municipales de naturaleza y alcance equivalentes a los PRODT, PMOT, IDSU y Normas Subsidiarias Regionales de Planificación previstos en esta consultoría, así como Estrategias Territoriales de Reducción del Riesgo de Desastres y Adaptación al Cambio Climático; procesos participativos y de coordinación multiactor; formulación normativa; gestión de información territorial y cartográfica; Evaluación Ambiental Estratégica; fortalecimiento institucional; y productos de implementación.

Los servicios se prestarán en idioma español e implican presencia activa en el territorio de las regiones Cibao Noroeste y Cibao Sur y en el Distrito Nacional, República Dominicana.

Nota: Los Expertos Clave no serán evaluados en la etapa de preselección.

Para estos fines la firma consultora deberá remitir la documentación de forma clara, estructurada, verificable y directamente vinculada con los criterios de preselección establecidos en la presente Solicitud de Expresiones de Interés (SEI). El documento principal no deberá exceder de cuarenta (40) páginas. Los documentos legales y los soportes documentales presentados para acreditar la experiencia y capacidad declaradas no se computarán dentro de este límite y deberán incorporarse como anexos debidamente identificados, paginados y referenciados. La documentación técnica de soporte no deberá exceder de ciento cincuenta (150) páginas para una firma consultora individual. En caso de APCA, consorcio, joint venture o asociación equivalente, el límite será de ciento cincuenta (150) páginas por cada integrante que acredite experiencia o capacidad técnica, organizativa u operativa relevante para los criterios de preselección. El registro mercantil, la nómina de accionistas y los documentos legales equivalentes no se computarán dentro de estos límites de páginas.

La documentación requerida es la siguiente:

  • Carta de expresión de interés, con datos generales de la firma consultora (firmada y sellada).
  • Detalle de experiencia directa de la firma consultora donde se evidencie: actividad principal y años en el negocio, experiencia relevante, capacidad técnica y de gestión de la firma consultora de acuerdo con los requerimientos arriba mencionados. Para cada experiencia declarada deberá indicarse de manera organizada, como mínimo, el nombre del contrato o proyecto, cliente y país, fechas de ejecución, monto contractual, alcance, rol desempeñado por la firma o integrante de la APCA, productos o actividades efectivamente ejecutados, escala territorial, criterio o criterios de preselección que acredita y referencia exacta del soporte documental presentado.
  • Estructura organizativa general de la Firma Consultora o APCA, con una breve descripción de sus áreas técnicas, capacidades institucionales y recursos permanentes relevantes para la consultoría. En esta etapa no deberán presentarse CV ni se evaluarán las calificaciones de expertos individuales.
  • Registro mercantil actualizado o equivalente en su país de origen.
  • Nómina de accionistas o documento equivalente en su país de origen.

Nota: Toda la documentación que se presente deberá estar en idioma español.

La lista corta estará integrada por un mínimo de cinco (5) y un máximo de ocho (8) firmas consultoras.

Se llama la atención de los Consultores interesados sobre la Sección III, párrafos 3.14, 3.16 y 3.17 de las “Regulaciones de Adquisiciones para Prestatarios en Proyectos de Inversión del Banco Mundial, actualizadas a noviembre de 2020 (“Regulaciones de Adquisiciones”), que establece la política del Banco Mundial sobre conflictos de intereses.

Los Consultores podrán asociarse con otras firmas para mejorar sus calificaciones y deberán indicar claramente si la asociación se presenta como APCA (joint venture, consorcio o asociación equivalente) o como subconsultoría. En caso de APCA, todos sus integrantes serán conjunta y solidariamente responsables de la totalidad del contrato, si resultan seleccionados.

Se puede obtener más información durante el horario de oficina de 08:00 a 16:00 horas, en las oficinas de este Viceministerio ubicadas en la calle César Nicolás Penson núm. 48, Distrito Nacional, Santo Domingo, República Dominicana, o mediante comunicación escrita dirigida al correo electrónico adquisicioneseyr@minpre.gob.do.

MINISTRY OF ROADS AND HIGHWAYS

DEPARTMENT OF FEEDER ROADS

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

CONSULTANT’S QUALIFICATIONS BASED SELECTION (CQS)

Name of Project

Ghana Market Access and Connectivity Project (GMACP)-Project Preparatory Grant

Loan No/Credit No/ Grant Number

IDA-E6230

Assignment Title

Consulting Services for Preparation of Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) and Resettlement Action Plan (RAP) for Cluster 2 and 4

Procurement Plan Ref Number

GH-MRH- 572781-CS-CQS

Country of Delivery

Ghana

Project ID No.:

P514903

 

  1.  The Government of the Republic of Ghana has received a Grant from the World Bank toward the cost of the Project Preparatory activities for the Ghana Market Access and Connectivity Project (GMACP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for the following consulting services.

 

The primary objective of this assignment is to procure a Consultant to prepare and deliver separate cluster-wide ESIA/ESMP and RAP instruments for Cluster 2 and Cluster 4 reflecting the distinct Environmental and Social (E&S) screening status, risk profile and delivery sequencing of each cluster.

 

2. The Consulting Services (“the Services”) include the following among others:

i) Define the scope of the ESIA and RAP studies covering all roads in the validated road list for the relevant cluster (Clusters 2 and 4) through scoping and stakeholder engagement, informed by the applicable E&S screening findings.

ii) Establish baseline environmental, social, and livelihood conditions and assess applicable legal and institutional requirements

iii) Prepare a cluster-wide ESIA/ESMP and a cluster-wide RAP for Cluster 2 and 4, each supported by road-specific and district-specific annexes, schedules, maps, mitigation measures and implementation arrangements, in accordance with the outcome of the E&S screening and scoping process for the relevant cluster and in alignment with national requirements and the World Bank ESF.

iv) Provide practical measures for mitigation, compensation, livelihood restoration, implementation, monitoring, and integration into project design and execution.

v) Establish an inventory for all assets to be affected and determine the replacement cost in accordance with applicable requirements.

 

The estimated level of effort (professional staff-months) for Key Staff is 19.20 Person-months.

The implementation period for the assignment is expected to be Twenty (20) weeks from the commencement of the Assignment. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained by sending an official request to the email addresses given below

data.institution: Eswatini Water and Agricultural Development Enterprise
data.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES - PROVISION OF END-TO-END BUSINESS DEVELOPMENT SERVICES- FIRMS SELECTION)

Ref No: EWADE /0796

COUNTRY: Kingdom of Eswatini

NAME OF PROJECT: Eswatini Youth Employment Opportunities project (P507360)

Loan No./Credit No./ Grant No.: IDA Credit No. 77910 (IDA Credit) 

Assignment Title: Procurement of consulting services for end-to-end business development services (BDS) Providers to Support Youth Employment under the Eswatini Youth Employment Opportunities Project (EYEOP)

Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): SZ-EWADE-549413-CS-QCBS 

1. The Government of the Kingdom of Eswatini, has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of the implementation of the Eswatini Youth Employment Opportunities Project (EYEOP), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The Eswatini Youth Employment Opportunities Project is a five-year, national, multi-sectoral initiative that seeks to expand income-earning opportunities for Eswatini youth by strengthening employability, promoting entrepreneurship and supporting inclusive, resilient livelihoods. The Project delivers an economic inclusion package comprising market-relevant skills training, business development support, access to finance and integration into value chains, and is implemented through three components, including Component 1: Youth Income-Earning Opportunities, under which Sub-component 1.1 (Income-Earning Opportunities for Youth in Agriculture), led by the Eswatini Water and Agricultural Development Enterprise (EWADE), targets 20,000 youth (at least 50% female, 5% disabled) in agriculture and related value chains.

The consulting services comprise of the provision of end-to-end Business Development Service Providers to support youth participation in priority agricultural and agribusiness value chains under Sub-component 1.1 (Youth Income-Earning Opportunities) of EYEOP. The Services will support eligible youth through an integrated pathway covering value chain intelligence and market analysis; beneficiary profiling and pathway allocation; socio-emotional, entrepreneurship, technical and business skills development; business planning and enterprise establishment; finance readiness and access productive finance; market linkages and value chain facilitation; mentorship, coaching and aftercare support; and monitoring, quality assurance and performance monitoring.

The services will focus on prioritized value chain including selected commodities across vegetables, field crops, small ruminants, poultry and aquaculture sub-sectors.

The assignment is expected to commence upon contract signature and will be implemented throughout the EYEOP implementation period, in accordance with approved Annual Work Plan and Budgets (AWPB). The engagement will initially be for one (1) year, with the possibility of annual renewal, subject to satisfactory performance, achievement of agreed deliverables and performance targets, availability of funding and continue need for the services.

2. The Terms of Reference for the primary procurement stage for the assignment are attached to this request for expressions of interest in Annex 1.

3. The Eswatini Water and agricultural development Enterprise invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

  • Core business and institutional experience: Demonstrated core business in business development services, enterprise development, business advisory services, entrepreneurship development, skills development, training, mentorship, market linkage facilitation or related areas relevant to the assignment.
  • Relevant assignment experience: Successful completion of at least one (1) assignment of similar nature, scope and complexity within the last five (5) years, demonstrating experience in the delivery of BDS, enterprise development, youth entrepreneurship, business advisory services, training, mentorship, market linkages or related services.
  • Experience in youth and enterprise development: Demonstrated experience in implementing youth entrepreneurship, employment, skills development or economic inclusion programmes, including support to emerging and/or existing enterprises.
  • Agriculture, agribusiness and value-chain experience: Demonstrated experience in agriculture, agribusiness or related value-chain development, including facilitating linkages between smallholder farmers or enterprises and buyers, aggregators, processors, financial institutions, input suppliers or other private-sector actors.
  • Financial and business development experience: Demonstrated institutional experience in financial literacy, finance readiness, business planning, enterprise financing and/or agriculture and value-chain financing.
  • Geographic and contextual experience: Demonstrated experience working in Eswatini and/or Southern Africa, with an understanding of the regional agricultural, youth employment, entrepreneurship and enterprise-development context.
  • Technical and operational capacity: Demonstrated institutional capacity, systems and operational reach to deliver integrated BDS at the scale envisaged under EYEOP, including the ability to mobilize and manage appropriate technical resources, delivery personnel, logistics, data-management systems and quality-assurance arrangements.
  • Experience in inclusive and sustainable development approaches: Demonstrated experience integrating gender, youth inclusion, disability inclusion, climate resilience, climate-smart agriculture, environmental sustainability or related cross-cutting considerations into programme delivery.
  • Development programme experience: Experience implementing donor-funded, government-funded or multi-stakeholder development programmes will be considered an advantage.

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage. Their qualifications and experience will be assessed at the Request for Proposals (RfP) stage in accordance with the applicable evaluation criteria.

4. The shortlist will contain 5 to 8 firms.

5. Consultants are required to further submit the following eligibility documents:

  • Valid Tax Compliance Certificate
  • Valid Trading License
  • Certificate of Incorporation
  • Forms J and C
  • Audited Financial statements
  • Valid ENPF Compliance Certificate
  • Copies of Company Director IDs certified
  • Affidavit or Police Clearance for Company Directors
  • Expression of interest form (Form 1)
  • Company Profile
  • Relevant Experience
  • CVs of Key Personnel

6. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.15 and 3.16 of the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. In addition, please refer to the following specific information on conflict of interest related to this assignment:

 

Consultants shall not be hired for any assignment that would be in conflict with their prior or current obligations to other clients, or that may place them in a position of being unable to carry out the assignment in the best interests of the Borrower. Without limitation on the generality of the foregoing, Consultants shall not be hired under the circumstances set forth below:

a) a firm that has been engaged by the Borrower to provide Goods, Works, or Non-Consulting Services for a project (or an affiliate that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with that firm), shall be disqualified from providing Consulting Services resulting from, or directly related to, those Goods, Works, or Non-Consulting Services. This provision does not apply to the various firms (Consultants, contractors, or suppliers), which together are performing the contractor’s obligations under a turnkey or design and build contract;

b) a firm that has been engaged by the Borrower to provide Consulting Services for the preparation or implementation of a project (or an affiliate that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with that Consulting firm), shall be disqualified from subsequently providing Goods, Works, or Non-Consulting Services resulting from, or directly related to those Consulting Services. This provision does not apply to the various firms (Consultants, contractors, or suppliers), which together are performing the contractor’s obligations under a turnkey or design and build contract;
