ANNEX 1: Terms of Reference

TERMS OF REFERENCE

Provision of End-to-End Business Development Services

(Business Development Management Support TA)

Eswatini Youth Employment Opportunities Project (EYEOP)

1. Background

The Kingdom of Eswatini faces persistent challenges of high youth unemployment, limited formal-sector job creation and widespread poverty, particularly in rural areas. Women, youth with disabilities, youth who are not in education, employment or training, and youth engaged in low-productivity activities face additional barriers to productive opportunities.

The Eswatini Youth Employment Opportunities Project (EYEOP) is a five-year national, multisectoral initiative supported by the World Bank to expand income-earning opportunities for youth. The Project combines market-relevant skills, entrepreneurship and business development support, productive start-up support, access to finance, mentorship, and integration into agricultural and related value chains.

Under Subcomponent 1.1, EWADE will support 20,000 youth in agriculture and related value chains, with at least 50 percent women. The beneficiary pathway covers socio-emotional and mindset-change support, technical and business skills, business planning, productive grants where applicable, enterprise development, market or employment linkages, mentorship and post-support monitoring.

The assignment will focus on Government-prioritized value chains: vegetables (onions, potatoes, tomatoes and baby vegetables), dry beans, small ruminants, poultry and aquaculture. Youth opportunities may cover on-farm production and off-farm activities such as input supply, nurseries and hatcheries, aggregation, logistics, processing, mechanization, e-extension, e-commerce and related business services.

2. Objective of the Assignment

The overall objective is to engage a qualified BDS Provider to deliver a comprehensive, demand-driven and results-oriented package that enables eligible youth to establish, improve, sustain and grow viable enterprises or access wage-employment opportunities, while contributing to measurable improvements in employment, income, productivity, market participation and resilience.

The specific objectives are to:

  • Profile beneficiaries and allocate them to suitable employment, enterprise, on-farm or off-farm pathways.
  • Strengthen technical, socio-emotional, entrepreneurship, business-management, financial and digital capabilities.
  • Support viable business planning, enterprise establishment, operational improvement and growth.
  • Improve finance readiness and facilitate appropriate access to productive grants or other finance.
  • Facilitate sustainable market, value-chain and employment linkages.
  • Provide structured mentorship and generate reliable beneficiary-level performance evidence.

3. Scope of Services

Under Subcomponent 1.1, the BDS Provider shall provide training, capacity building and mentoring services to support EWADE in the design and implementation of economic inclusion interventions. The Consulting Firm shall undertake the following major tasks:

3.1 BDS Package Design, Curriculum Review and Pilot Testing

The Provider shall establish an EYEOP-approved BDS package that is practical, interactive, youth-centred and tailored to beneficiary needs and priority value chains. Existing local and international good-practice content shall be used as the starting point for customization rather than developing all content from first principles.

  • Review existing BDS, entrepreneurship, business-management, socio-emotional, financial-literacy, digital-skills, technical-training and mentorship materials.
  • Assess suitability for NEET youth, vulnerable informal workers, women and youth with disabilities, and identify gaps requiring adaptation or additional modules.
  • Customize content to EYEOP pathways, priority value chains, the Eswatini market context, beneficiary literacy levels and language needs.
  • Develop clear learning objectives, session plans, practical exercises, participant outputs, assessment methods, facilitator manuals, participant materials and a structured mentorship guide.
  • Pilot the package with an agreed beneficiary group; assess content, language, timing, accessibility and practicality; document findings and revise the package before EWADE approval.

3.2 Youth Mobilization, Communication, Profiling and Pathway Allocation

  • Support awareness, beneficiary communication, registration and screening in accordance with Project eligibility and targeting requirements.
  • Assess skills, interests, aspirations, productive assets, constraints, readiness, entrepreneurial potential and relevant labour-market or value-chain characteristics.
  • Match beneficiaries to wage-employment, self-employment, on-farm or off-farm pathways and identify required technical training, enterprise support and reasonable accommodations.
  • Communicate schedules, participation requirements and logistics through appropriate approved channels.
  • Maintain accurate profiles, selection records and pathway-allocation data in formats compatible with the EYEOP MIS.

3.3 Socio-Emotional, Mindset, Life and Business Skills Training

  • Deliver practical training in initiative, confidence, resilience, goal-setting, problem-solving, communication, adaptability and decision-making.
  • Address gender-related, household, cultural, disability-related or other barriers affecting participation and enterprise performance.
  • Deliver business-model development, customer identification, marketing, costing, pricing, record keeping, cash-flow management and financial literacy.
  • Use experiential methods, including demonstrations, case studies, role play, group work and application to a beneficiary’s own business or employment pathway.
  • Ensure training is accessible and adapted to education, literacy, language and disability needs.

3.4 Technical and Competency-Based Training

  • Deliver technical training relevant to the selected priority value chain and pathway, aligned with applicable DIVT or other competent standards.
  • Provide practical and experiential learning suited to the selected commodity, occupation or business opportunity.
  • Integrate climate-smart agriculture, green business practices, food safety, quality standards and appropriate digital agriculture solutions.
  • Support competency assessment and certification in coordination with relevant institutions.
  • Align delivery with production calendars, market cycles and employment demand where applicable.

3.5 Enterprise Development and Business Start-Up Support

  • Validate enterprise opportunities against market demand, competition, costs, risks and beneficiary capabilities.
  • Support business models, enterprise profiles, business plans, production and marketing plans, budgets, cash-flow forecasts and growth plans.
  • Provide incubation, business advisory, coaching and technical support during establishment and early operations.
  • Support formalization, governance, compliance, record keeping, productivity, innovation, digital adoption and climate resilience where relevant.
  • Assess enterprise-specific technical, operational, financial and market constraints and coordinate referrals to suitable specialist services.
  • Support enterprises to improve operational continuity, sales, customer retention, market access, income and employment creation.

3.6 Finance Readiness and Productive Resource Management

  • Conduct finance-readiness assessments and support grant applications, budgets, cash-flow projections, investment cases and financing plans.
  • Explain eligibility and application requirements for Project grants and other relevant financing.
  • Facilitate linkages with financial institutions, investors and financing providers without influencing third-party decisions or representing finance as guaranteed.
  • Strengthen responsible use of grants and other finance through budgeting, basic financial management and record keeping.
  • Track referrals, applications, approvals, financing accessed, reasons for rejection and use of finance where required.

3.7 Market, Value-Chain and Employment Linkages

  • Identify viable commercial and employment opportunities based on market demand, value-chain requirements and beneficiary capabilities.
  • Maintain an engagement pipeline of buyers, employers, processors, aggregators, exporters, retailers, lead firms and other relevant market actors.
  • Facilitate supplier relationships, off-take arrangements, aggregation, contract farming, buyer-seller engagement, trade events and employment placement.
  • Support beneficiaries to meet quality, volume, reliability, packaging, certification, pricing and delivery requirements.
  • Facilitate access to inputs, equipment, logistics, extension, mechanization, digital market access and other services needed for sustainable participation.

3.8 Mentorship, Coaching and Post-Support Follow-Up

  • Establish a structured mentorship and coaching system appropriate to beneficiary pathways and enterprise stages.
  • Recruit, assess and train mentors under EWADE-approved requirements and maintain a qualified mentor roster.
  • Match beneficiaries with suitable entrepreneurs, business owners, technical specialists, extension officers, employers or private-sector mentors.
  • Provide individual and group coaching during critical production, operational, marketing and business-growth stages.
  • Use a structured guide, session plans, action plans, attendance records and follow-up logs; monitor mentor performance and replace underperforming personnel.
  • Conduct agreed tracer and follow-up activities to assess enterprise operation, employment, income, sales, productivity and sustainability.

3.9 Monitoring, Quality Assurance, Learning and Adaptive Management

  • Maintain complete beneficiary and service-delivery records interoperable with the EYEOP MIS and submit data in prescribed formats and frequencies.
  • Track agreed output and outcome indicators, including completion, enterprise establishment and survival, market participation, finance, employment, income, sales, productivity and jobs.
  • Undertake quality assurance of curricula, trainers, mentors, venues, materials, attendance, accessibility and beneficiary experience.
  • Collect beneficiary feedback and satisfaction data; maintain supporting evidence; perform data-quality checks; and implement corrective actions.
  • Document implementation lessons, innovations, constraints and emerging risks for each cohort or service cycle and submit evidence-based recommendations.
  • Record and refer complaints through the Project grievance mechanism and comply with environmental and social, safeguarding, anticorruption, confidentiality and data-protection requirements.

4. Methodology & Workplan

The TOR defines the mandatory service requirements, minimum standards, outputs and intended results. The Provider shall propose the detailed methodology, staffing deployment, sequencing, tools, logistics and quality-assurance arrangements in its technical proposal. The approach shall demonstrate how all service areas will be integrated into a coherent beneficiary journey rather than delivered as disconnected activities.

Delivery shall be organized around defined beneficiary cohorts or service cycles. The contract will specify the number and profile of beneficiaries, geographic coverage, value chains, pathway mix, delivery period, required modules, mentorship frequency, service standards, deliverables, indicators and verification requirements. Training, enterprise support and mentoring shall be aligned with agricultural production calendars, market cycles and relevant employment demand.

The detailed methodology shall be finalized during inception with EWADE. Adjustments may be proposed during implementation in response to beneficiary needs and evidence, but shall require written approval and shall not reduce agreed coverage, service quality, outputs, results, safeguards or contractual accountability.

4.1. Delivery and Contracting Model

An applicant may participate as:

  • A single firm possessing the required end-to-end capabilities; or
  • A joint venture or consortium with complementary capabilities, with a clearly defined Lead Firm supported by formally identified specialist subcontractors or technical partners.

The Lead Firm shall enter into the contract with EWADE and assume full responsibility for end-to-end delivery, coordination, quality assurance, reporting, fiduciary compliance, risk management, safeguarding, data quality and achievement of all contracted outputs and results. The proposal shall identify each participating entity, its legal relationship to the Lead Firm, its role, the services it will provide, key personnel, coordination arrangements and the mechanism for managing performance and risks across the delivery chain.

EWADE will hold the Lead Firm accountable and will not separately manage consortium members, subcontractors or specialist partners. The Lead Firm shall consolidate all work plans, reports, invoices, evidence and communications; monitor the performance of participating entities; address delivery failures; and ensure consistent service standards. Any material change in consortium membership, specialist arrangements, key responsibilities or proposed personnel shall require prior written approval by EWADE.

4.2 Performance Review and Adaptive Management

Performance shall be reviewed for each cohort or service cycle against agreed service standards, output quality, beneficiary satisfaction, data quality, safeguarding compliance, market or employment linkage performance and outcome indicators measurable within the review period.

A broader implementation review shall be undertaken after the initial six months, or at another point specified in the contract, to assess the effectiveness of the integrated delivery model, coordination arrangements, beneficiary progression and the Lead Firm’s management of participating entities. EWADE may require a corrective action plan, enhanced supervision, replacement of personnel, revised sequencing or other reasonable adjustments within the contract. Any adjustment shall preserve the agreed objectives and the Lead Firm’s unified accountability.

5. Expected Outputs and Performance Framework

The assignment shall use results-based performance management. Performance will be assessed on delivery of contracted outputs and measurable contributions to agreed employment, enterprise, income and market outcomes. The Provider shall not be evaluated solely on the number of activities conducted. The contract shall distinguish between outputs within the Provider’s direct control and outcome indicators to which the Provider contributes.

6. Deliverables and Reporting Requirements

The Consulting Firm shall produce the following outputs to deliver business development services for the enrolled youth beneficiaries:

7. Schedule and Duration

The services will commence upon contract signature and will be delivered throughout the implementation period of the Eswatini Youth Employment Opportunities Project (EYEOP), in accordance with approved Annual Work Plans and Budgets, applicable project implementation arrangements and the performance requirements specified in the contract.

The engagement will be structured as a performance-based contract, initially covering one year and renewable annually, subject to satisfactory performance, achievement of agreed deliverables and performance targets, availability of funding and the continued need for the services. Subject to these conditions, the contract may be renewed on an annual basis for the duration of the EYEOP implementation period

The BDS Provider will be expected to provide services on a demand-driven and continuous basis, responding to the evolving needs of participating youth and the implementation schedule of the project. Key areas of service delivery will include:

  1. Mobilization and onboarding: Support the profiling, assessment and onboarding of participating youth into the relevant EYEOP economic inclusion and entrepreneurship interventions.
  2. Business assessment and planning: Conduct business diagnostics, develop or strengthen business plans and profiles, and support beneficiaries to develop viable and market-oriented enterprises.
  3. Capacity building and incubation: Deliver tailored business development training, coaching, mentorship, incubation and other technical assistance required to strengthen youth-owned enterprises.
  4. Enterprise development and growth support: Provide ongoing technical assistance to supported enterprises, including support for implementation, business formalization, financial management, productivity improvement and enterprise growth.
  5. Market and value-chain linkages: Facilitate linkages with buyers, lead firms, financial institutions, input suppliers, service providers and other relevant market actors to enhance access to markets and sustainable business opportunities.
  6. Performance monitoring and reporting: Monitor beneficiary and enterprise performance against agreed indicators and targets, and submit periodic reports demonstrating progress, results, challenges, corrective actions and lessons learned.
  7. Continuous improvement and adaptive support: Adjust the nature and intensity of BDS support based on beneficiary performance, emerging needs, project priorities, market conditions and lessons from implementation.

The specific annual deliverables, targets, timelines and performance indicators will be agreed with the EYEOP implementing agency at the commencement of each contract year and may be reviewed periodically to reflect the project's implementation priorities.

Continuation or renewal of the services will be subject to satisfactory performance against the agreed performance indicators and deliverables, compliance with contractual and project requirements, availability of funds, and approval in accordance with applicable procurement and project procedures. The sequence and timing of individual BDS activities may therefore vary during the project period depending on beneficiary needs, project implementation progress and approved annual work plans.

8. Team Composition

The Consultant shall propose suitably qualified key experts, including a Task Team Leader/BDS Team Leader; Agriculture Production, Agribusiness and Value Chain Expert, Training, Skills and Youth Development Expert; Market Systems and Private Sector Linkages Expert; Finance and Investment Readiness Expert, MEL/Data Management Expert, Digital Agriculture and Innovation Expert as well as Gender, Social Inclusion and Environment Safeguards Expert. For each proposed expert, the Consultant shall provide the key responsibilities, academic and professional qualifications, relevant professional experience, experience in assignments of similar nature and complexity, proposed level of effort expressed in person-months and/or percentage of time, and availability for the assignment.

9. Firm Qualifications and Experience

The applicant shall demonstrate relevant institutional experience, technical expertise, operational capacity and systems relevant to deliver EYEOP Business Development Services. As a minimum mandatory requirement, the applicant shall have successfully completed at least one (1) assignment of similar nature, scope and complexity within the last five (5) years. The assignment shall demonstrate relevant experience in the delivery of BDS, enterprise development, youth entrepreneurship, business advisory services, training, mentorship, market linkages or related services.  In addition to the mandatory minimum requirement above, the applicant shall demonstrate the following relevant institutional experience, technical expertise and operational capacity:

  • Proven experience in delivering BDS, enterprise development, business advisory services, mentoring and coaching, including supporting emerging and existing entrepreneurs to establish, grow and sustain viable businesses across multiple sectors
  • Demonstrated experience implementing youth entrepreneurship, employment or skills development programmes.
  • Demonstrated experience in facilitating partnerships and establishing market linkages between smallholder farmers and buyers, aggregators and other private sector actors.
  • Demonstrated Experience in financial literacy, financial readiness and agriculture/value chain financing.
  • Proven experience implementing donor-funded, government-funded, or multi-stakeholder development programmes will be considered an advantage.
  • Demonstrated experience working in Eswatini and/or Southern Africa, with a sound understanding of the local agricultural, youth and enterprise development context.
  • Demonstrated experience integrating gender, youth, disability inclusion, climate-smart agriculture and green business practices.
  • Demonstrated adequate technical, financial and operational capacity to deliver BDS at the scale envisaged under EYEOP.

10. Environmental, Social Framework (ESF) Requirements

The assignment shall comply with the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) and applicable national requirements as referenced in the Project Appraisal Document (PAD), with responsibilities proportionate to the Training, Capacity Building, and Mentoring category for delivery of business development services supporting income earning opportunities for youth under the EYEOP.

  • Comply with the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework, applicable national requirements and relevant Project instruments.
  • Apply gender-responsive and disability-inclusive approaches and provide agreed reasonable accommodations.
  • Integrate climate resilience, occupational health and safety, stakeholder engagement and beneficiary feedback into service delivery.
  • Record, refer and report grievances through the Project grievance mechanism and ensure personnel comply with safeguarding requirements and codes of conduct.
  • Protect beneficiary information, maintain required disaggregation and ensure confidentiality and data-protection obligations extend to consortium members and subcontractors.

11. Reporting Lines

The Lead Firm shall enter into the contract with EWADE and report to EWADE for all activities under this assignment, assuming full responsibility for end-to-end delivery, coordination, reporting and achievement of contracted outputs and results.

  • Accountability: EWADE will hold the Lead Firm accountable and will not separately manage consortium members, subcontractors or specialist partners. The Lead Firm shall consolidate all work plans, reports, invoices, evidence and communications; monitor the performance of participating entities; address delivery failures; and ensure consistent service standards.
  • EWADE responsibilities: EWADE will confirm beneficiary cohorts and targets; provide or facilitate access to applicable Project documents, beneficiary information and systems; designate technical and contract-management focal points; coordinate relevant Government stakeholders; review deliverables; monitor service quality; and verify performance.
  • Provider responsibilities: The Lead Firm shall provide all personnel, specialist inputs, logistics, equipment, materials, communication and management systems required for delivery unless otherwise stated in the contract. It shall maintain complete technical, financial and beneficiary records and make them available for supervision, audit and verification. It shall promptly report material delays, safeguarding issues, fiduciary concerns or other risks requiring management attention.
  • Escalation and corrective action: Where a broader implementation review identifies performance concerns, EWADE may require a corrective action plan, enhanced supervision, replacement of personnel, revised sequencing or other reasonable adjustments within the contract, preserving the agreed objectives and the Lead Firm's unified accountability.

11. Proposal and Evaluation Requirements

The technical proposal shall explain the applicant’s understanding of the assignment; integrated methodology; beneficiary profiling and pathway allocation; training, enterprise, finance, market, mentorship and M&E approaches; staffing and deployment; consortium governance; geographic capacity; quality assurance; risks and safeguards; output verification; and relevant past performance.

Evaluation shall consider capacity to manage the full beneficiary journey, the credibility and complementarity of any consortium arrangement, methodology, qualifications of key personnel, delivery and monitoring systems, relevant experience, financial and operational capacity, and value for money.

12. Payment Terms 

Payments shall be output-based and linked, as appropriate, to accepted deliverables, verified service delivery and verified performance results. The payment structure shall clearly distinguish inputs, outputs and outcomes and shall not reimburse consultant time without a corresponding accepted deliverable or contracted service result unless expressly provided in the contract.

The RfP and contract shall define each payment milestone, indicator definition, target, acceptance criterion, evidence requirement, verification method, payment trigger and treatment of incomplete or non-conforming outputs. Where payment is calculated per beneficiary, it shall be based on the verified number receiving the contracted package and satisfying applicable service-verification requirements. Submission of a report alone will not constitute acceptance where the underlying service or beneficiary-level evidence cannot be verified.

EWADE may verify reported outputs and results through document review, MIS checks, site visits, beneficiary confirmation, attendance validation, data-quality assessments, financial review or independent verification. All payments will be subject to written acceptance by the authorized EWADE representative and applicable contractual and fiduciary requirements.

13. Items to be Finalized in the RfP and Contract

  • Final beneficiary volumes, geographic coverage, cohorts, value chains, duration and delivery calendar.
  • Detailed outputs, targets, indicators, acceptance criteria, verification arrangements and reporting schedule.
  • Final payment milestones and any performance-linked share.
  • Key experts, minimum inputs, service standards, logistics and implementation milestones.
  • MIS protocols, applicable environmental and social instruments, data requirements and client inputs.
  • Provisions governing the Lead Firm, consortium members, specialist subcontractors, substitutions, remedies and termination.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

Consultancy Services for the Feasibility Study and Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) for the Proposed Underwater Museum

Reference No.: SVGUBEC-C-QCBS-13

Date of Issue: 7 October 2026

Saint Vincent and the Grenadines has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Unleashing the Blue Economy of the Caribbean (UBEC) Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) comprise the preparation of a Feasibility Study and an Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) for the proposed Underwater Museum, together with an Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP), a site-specific Stakeholder Consultation Plan and the related consultations, subproject grievance mechanism arrangements, and the associated environmental and social management instruments. The Services will determine whether the Client’s 2025 preliminary concept, “The Submerged Museum: A Museum of Slavery & Resistance”, including its proposed repurposed-vessel configuration, is technically, environmentally, socially, economically, financially, legally and institutionally feasible, and will compare it with lower-impact or non-vessel alternatives.

The assignment is expected to be completed within approximately twenty-six (26) weeks from contract signing. The expected start date is February 2026.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment may be downloaded at the following website: https://procurement.gov.vc/eprocure/index.php/current-bids.

The Ministry of Tourism, Civil Aviation and Sustainable Development, through the UBEC Project Implementation Unit, now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services

The shortlisting criteria are:

1. At least ten (10) years of corporate experience in feasibility studies and/or environmental and social impact assessments for marine, coastal, tourism, blue economy or biodiversity-sensitive projects.

2. Completion, within the last ten (10) years, of at least three (3) comparable assignments involving coastal or marine infrastructure, marine tourism, underwater attractions, artificial reefs or vessel-related marine installations, or biodiversity-sensitive coastal and marine sites, of which at least one (1) shall have been an ESIA (or equivalent environmental and social assessment) for a marine or coastal investment.

3. Demonstrated experience in coastal and marine assignments in Small Island Developing States (SIDS) or comparable developing coastal nations; experience in the Caribbean will be an advantage.

4. Demonstrated experience in applying the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (in particular ESS1, ESS6, ESS8 and ESS10), or comparable environmental and social requirements of another multilateral development bank, including marine habitat assessment and stakeholder engagement with coastal communities, fisherfolk and marine users.

5. Technical and managerial capability of the firm to deliver an integrated multidisciplinary assignment, covering marine ecology and biodiversity, coastal engineering and vessel suitability, tourism and financial analysis, social development and livelihoods, cultural heritage, occupational health and diving safety, and GIS/mapping, including capacity to plan and supervise marine field surveys and to apply quality control across deliverables.

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

To facilitate the assessment, Expressions of Interest should include, at a minimum:

(a) a covering letter signed by an authorized representative of the firm;

(b) evidence of the firm’s legal registration or incorporation;

(c) a firm profile describing its core business, years in business, organization and permanent technical staff;

(d) a list of comparable assignments, indicating for each the client and contact details, country and location, contract value, start and completion dates, the firm’s role (lead firm, joint venture partner or sub-consultant) and a brief description of the services provided; and

(e) where applicable, details of any proposed association, identifying the lead firm and the role of each member, and stating whether the association is a joint venture or a sub-consultancy.

Consultants should submit their Expressions of Interest in English and are requested to limit their submission to a maximum of twenty-five (25) pages excluding covering letter and certificates.  Shortlisted Consultants will be invited to submit technical and financial proposals.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” July 2016 [revised November 2017, August 2018 and November 2020, September 2023, February 2025] (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Given that the Feasibility Study and ESIA must provide impartial advice on site selection and on the vessel-based concept, Consultants should disclose in their Expression of Interest any prior or current involvement in the preparation of the Underwater Museum concept, and any commercial interest in dive, tourism, salvage or marine operations at or near the candidate sites, so that any potential conflict of interest can be assessed.

Request for Expressions of Interest (REOI)

Ministry of Public Works and Transport (MPWT)

Southeast Asia Regional Economic Corridor and Connectivity Project – Additional Financing (SEARECC - AF)

Consulting Services for Implementation Support and Works Supervision (ISWS)

for OPBR Contract (OPBRC) for Rehabilitation of National Road No.2 West, Section 4

(Pak Beng to Muang Ngeun, Thai Border) and Local Road in Samphanh District, Phongsaly Province

(Consulting Service - Firms Selection, Reference No. SEARECC-QCBS-001- FS001-AF)

The Government of Lao People’s Democratic Republic (GoL) has applied financing support from the International Development Association (IDA) to implement the Lao PDR Southeast Asia Regional Economic Corridor and Connectivity Project – Additional Financing (SEARECC-AF) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services are required to support the Employer in the detailed design review, implementation and supervision of the rehabilitation and improvement works to be financed under the SEARECC Additional Financing (AF), including NR2W Section 4 under the Output- and Performance-Based Road Contract (OPBRC) and the Khua–Samphan Local Road in Phongsaly Province under the Hybrid Performance-Based Contract (HPBC).

The services include but are not limited to: (i) reviewing the detailed designs prepared by the Contractors for NR2W Section 4 under the OPBRC and the Khua–Samphan Local Road under the HPBC, and providing recommendations to the Employer; (ii) supervising the rehabilitation and improvement works and monitoring compliance with the applicable technical specifications, performance requirements and contractual obligations; (iii) reviewing the Contractors’ site-specific Environmental and Social Management Plans and associated plans, including the Traffic Management Plan, Community Health and Safety Plan, Labor Management Plan and Occupational Health and Safety Plan; (iv) supporting the Employer in monitoring compliance with the Project’s environmental and social requirements and approved instruments; (v) advising and supporting the Employer on relevant aspects of Project implementation; and (vi) engaging a certified laboratory, where required, to undertake environmental monitoring, including air-quality, noise and water-quality monitoring. All environmental and social activities shall be consistent with the applicable Site-Specific Environmental and Social Management Plans, ARAP/RAP, EGEP, SEP and other approved Project environmental and social instruments, and shall comply with the applicable Environmental and Social Standards and Government of Lao PDR requirements. The Services shall be carried out in accordance with applicable Project requirements and Good International Industry Practice.

The ISWS Consultant is expected to commence the assignment in parallel with the OPBRC and HPBC Contractors, whose contracts are expected to be awarded by May 2027. The assignment comprises two parts: (i) supervision of the rehabilitation of NR2W Section 4 under the OPBRC; and (ii) supervision of the improvement of the Khua–Samphan Local Road under the HPBC. The services are expected to cover the 36-month rehabilitation and improvement works period, commencing in the second quarter of 2027. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be request from the address given below or download from link: https://1drv.ms/w/c/4b4fca78445f7e3e/IQD6xUUXRNy0T5JCNSzoBGezASfwFa3cY6MZitkSEtlBW1E?e=ztqWJd.

The Ministry of Public Works and Transport, through the Department of Roads now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

Criterion 1 - Supervision of road works:  At least ten (10) years of experience in Works Supervision of national road improvement or rehabilitation contracts of equivalent or comparable value, scope of nature in the capacity of prime contractor (i.e. individually or as lead member of JV); such experience in South/ Southeast Asia is a strong asset;

Criterion 3 - Monitoring of ESF in road works and services: Minimum 3 contracts of similar scope and nature performed in the past 10 years in the capacity of prime contractor (i.e. individually or as lead member of JV), including implementation and/or monitoring of RAP, ESIA, ESMP for road construction, improvement or rehabilitation.

Expressions of Interest (EOIs) shall be submitted in English. Consultants shall include maximum 15 contracts per criterion listed above and will arrange the “past contract information forms” separately for each criterion. Failure to provide the required detail in the past contract information forms shall be under full Consultant’s responsibility – there will be no clarifications carried out during evaluation. In case the Consultant shall provide more than 15 contracts for each criterion, only the first 15 references shall be considered for evaluation. Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

Attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Regulations - Procurement in Investment Project Financing - Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services (September 2025 edition), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES)

Republic of the Marshall Islands

Strengthening Public Financial Management II

Loan No. /Credit No. / Grant No.: IDA – E5100

Assignment Title International US GASB Advisory Firm

Reference No. (as per procurement plan):  MH-PFM PMO-576102-CS-CQS

 

The Government of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI) faces structural and institutional capacity constraints in sustaining effective public financial management and service delivery. Strengthening accounting, financial reporting, and audit readiness remains a national priority to improve fiscal transparency and accountability.

With financial support from the World Bank, the Government of RMI is implementing the Strengthening Public Financial Management II (PFM II) Project. The Project Development Objective is to strengthen the reliability, quality, and timeliness of public financial reporting, supported by modernized systems and sustained institutional capacity.

Under Component 1: Improving PFM Practices in Budget Execution and Financial Reporting, Sub-component 1.1 focuses on developing sustainable in-house capability within the Ministry of Finance, Banking & Postal Services (MOFBPS), Budgetary Central Units (BCUs), and selected Component Units (CUs) to prepare Annual Financial Statements (AFS) compliant with U.S. Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) accounting standards.

MOFBPS has made progress in strengthening its financial reporting capacity and has engaged an embedded GASB Specialist and accounting personnel to progressively support strengthening of financial management and reporting practices. Additional specialized advisory support is required to assist the Ministry during the annual financial statement preparation cycle, address complex accounting and consolidation matters, enhance the current Chart of Accounts (CoA) to a unified CoA covering all government budget entities, strengthen Component Unit financial reporting and its integration with the Government FMIS to support consolidated reporting and audit readiness, and provide technical quality assurance.

RMI has implemented the BISAN Financial Management Information System (FMIS) as the primary platform for budget execution, accounting, and financial reporting. RMI is also in the process of enhancing the FMIS with additional functionalities that will include budget planning, FMIS interface with external systems, and improvements in financial reporting. While the FMIS is operational, preparation of the Annual Financial Statements continues to require manual processes and adjustments outside the system. MOFBPS intends to progressively strengthen and automate the generation of GASB-compliant financial statements and supporting reports directly from the FMIS.

Scope of Services

Under the general guidance of the PFM II Project Manager and in close coordination with MOFBPS, the Firm shall provide specialized technical assistance in the following areas:

3.1 Annual Financial Statement Preparation and Technical Support

The Firm shall lead and provide hands on technical support to MOFBPS for the timely preparation and completion of the GASB compliant Annual Financial Statements for the Primary Government and agreed material Component Units, including:

•            Compilation and preparation of the government wide and fund financial statements, notes, disclosures, supporting schedules, reconciliations, consolidation adjustments and elimination entries for Fiscal Year 2026;

•            Assist the RMI to develop a detailed year end close and financial statement preparation calendar, including identification of milestones, roles and responsibilities, and required adjusting and conversion entries;

•            Technical advice and quality assurance on complex accounting treatments, adjustments, applicable GASB requirements, prior-period matters, and accounting-related audit findings;

•            Review and strengthening of year-end close procedures, financial statement templates, working papers, and supporting schedules where material gaps are identified;

•            Targeted surge support during agreed critical periods of financial statement preparation and external audit;

•            Provide technical advice on Chart of Accounts enhancements and related financial reporting requirements, as required by MOFBPS.

The Firm shall work alongside the PFM II GASB Specialist, the Reform Coordination Unit, and MOFBPS accounting staff and shall use existing work products wherever appropriate. MOFBPS shall retain ownership and formal approval of the Annual Financial Statements. The Firm shall document the compilation process and transfer knowledge and practical tools to enable MOFBPS and relevant Component Units to lead subsequent reporting cycles.

3.2 Component Unit Financial Reporting and Audit Readiness

The Firm shall provide hands on technical support to agreed material Component Units for the compilation and completion of GASB compliant financial statements and preparation of information required for consolidated government wide reporting, including:

•            Support the preparation of GASB-compliant financial statements, reconciliations, disclosures, supporting schedules, and consolidation information for Fiscal Year 2026 and other outstanding prior years;

•            Provide technical advice on mapping Component Unit trial balances and reporting information to the Primary Government reporting structure and Bisan FMIS, where relevant;

•            Assessment of CU financial reporting and audit readiness, including accounting records, reconciliations, year-end close, audit documentation, recurring audit findings, systems, and relevant staff capacity;

•            Establishment of an audit readiness baseline and a Prioritized Component Unit Financial Reporting Improvement Plan;

•            Targeted technical assistance to priority CUs to address identified accounting and audit-preparation gaps; and

•            Development of standardized reporting templates, checklists, procedures, and timelines to progressively enable CUs to harmonize their financial reporting and provide information required for consolidated government wide reporting and audit preparation.

The assessment and support shall remain focused on financial accounting, financial reporting, year-end close, and external audit readiness and shall not extend to broader operational, procurement, grants-management, or general compliance matters.

3.3 FMIS Financial Statement Automation and Enhanced Chart of Accounts Support

The Firm shall provide accounting and functional advisory support for the progressive automation of GASB-compliant financial statements and supporting reports through the FMIS, including:

•            Review, testing, and validation of FMIS-generated financial statements and supporting reports against GASB requirements and approved reporting formats;

•            Support for implementation of the enhanced CoA, including technical discussions/workshops, an implementation strategy, training, and rollout support across relevant RMI budgeting entities;

•            Accounting and functional guidance to the FMIS Specialist, Graduate GASB Trainees, MOFBPS accounting staff, FMIS service provider, and other relevant technical teams on financial reporting configurations and enhancements; and

•            Recommendations to progressively reduce manual financial statement preparation and increase reliance on validated FMIS-generated reports.

The Firm's role shall focus on accounting requirements, functional specifications, testing, validation, and quality assurance of the ongoing FMIS Enhancements. Technical programming, software development, and system administration shall remain the responsibility of the FMIS technical team and/or service provider.

3.4 Audit Support, Capacity Building and Knowledge Transfer

Throughout the assignment, the Firm shall:

•            Support MOFBPS and priority CUs in preparing audit-ready working papers and responding to accounting and financial reporting matters raised by external auditors where feasible;

•            Provide specialized training and technical coaching on complex GASB requirements, Component Unit consolidation, audit readiness, and validation of FMIS-generated reports, building on the ongoing mentoring provided by the GASB Specialist;

•            Develop practical financial reporting guidance, templates, procedures, and reference materials for areas covered by the firm's assignment; and

•            Transfer knowledge and responsibilities to strengthen sustainable in-house financial statement and audit-preparation capacity.

Duration, Location and Conditions of the Assignment

•            Duration: Eighteen (18) months, with the possibility of extension subject to satisfactory performance, continued project requirements, availability of financing, and applicable procurement and contractual requirements.

•            Mode: Primarily virtual, supplemented by in-country missions proposed by the Firm and agreed with MOFBPS in the approved work plan.

•            The technical and financial proposals shall state the proposed number, duration, timing, and cost assumptions for in-country missions. Missions should, where practicable, coincide with critical periods of the annual financial reporting cycle, Component Unit engagement, FMIS reporting work, year-end close, audit preparation, and targeted training.

•            MOFBPS will facilitate reasonable access to relevant financial information, FMIS reports, audit documentation, and designated counterpart personnel required for performance of the assignment.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) and REOI with Annexes for the assignment can be obtained at the email address given below.

Ministry of Finance, Banking and Postal Services, MIR room 219

or E-mail: rf.rmipfm@gmail.com

Individual Consultant Selection (National)

Ministry of Livestock and Fisheries, Juba, South Sudan

 

  • Background: Ministry of Livestock and Fisheries (MLF) has received funding from the World Bank towards the cost of implementing the 5-years South Sudan Resilient Livestock Sector Project (RLSP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. The project development objective is to enhance animal health, improve range-land management, and strengthen resilience of livestock production in selected project areas. The project will directly benefit 166,000 households in the targeted eight (8) Counties in the following five (5) States, namely: Jonglei, Warrap, Upper Nile, Central Equatoria and Western Equatoria. The project aims to lay the foundation for a climate-resilient, competitive, and gender sensitive productive livestock sector in South Sudan to enable socioeconomic and inclusive growth. The main components of the project are; (i) strengthening animal health and welfare systems, (ii) sustainable and integrated rangeland development and management for livestock production, with focus on feed and water management, (iii) technical assistance, institutional strengthening, and project management, coordination, monitoring, and communication.
  • Objective: The consulting services (“the Services”) is for Project Executive Secretary who will work within the Ministry’s Project Coordination Unit (PCU), report to the Project Administrative Assistant and be responsible for providing support to the Project Management Team and executing the project secretarial duties and responsibilities as well as the daily operations of the project. The incumbent is expected to work in synergy with other Donor funded projects being coordinated through PCU under MLF.
  • Key Responsibilities: These include but are not limited to the following:
  1. Front desk management and reception of visitors to the Project in liaison with the security guard at the office's entrance of the Project Manager;
  2. Receiving and dispatching all office communication by e-mail, fax, post, diplomatic bag, etc. Distributes incoming traffic to the relevant recipients for action or information (assures copying and further distribution);
  3. Assist the Project Manager and Administrative Assistant in fleet management and supervision of the cleaners, messengers, drivers and security guards;
  4. Assist in implementing and maintaining office systems and maintaining filing systems;
  5. Maintaining an updated address and phone lists of MLF key staff, and all key project stakeholders;
  6. Assist the Project Manager and Administrative Assistant in organizing, coordinating meetings, conference and travel arrangements and writing minutes of the meetings;
  7. Providing secretarial services as required by project personnel (i.e. write correspondence, phone calls, photocopies, scanning etc.); and
  8. Carrying out any other duties assigned by the Project Management Team.

 

  • Terms of Reference: The detailed Terms of Reference (ToR) containing roles and scope for the assignment as well as the evaluation criteria for this consultancy can be obtained upon written request to the e-mail address: ss.rlsp2025@gmail.com clearly indicating the subject matter as “ToR for Administrative Assistant”.

  • Qualification
  • Hold a minimum Diploma in any of the following: Management, Business and Administration, International Development, Project Management, and Social Work from a recognized institution.
  • Bachelor’s degree will be an added advantage.

  • Fluent in English both written and spoken.
  • Experience
  • At least two (2) years of work experience in a similar or related role with Government or any other reputable non-government organisation.
  • Office administration skills - experience managing front office.
  • Other Requirement
  • Initiative and practical resourcefulness together with exceptional group dynamics and people skills.
  • Good communication skills, both oral and written

 

  • Selection Criteria: The Consultant(s) will be selected in accordance with the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, dated July 2016 and revised 7th Edition of September 2025 which can be found at the following website: www.worldbank.org/procurement. This will then be followed by oral interviews for the shortlisted candidates and will be assessed using scored criteria on qualification, specific experience and desirable skills.

Ref: 18.13.0000.000.000.07.0020.25

The indicative scope of work includes, but is not limited to, the following:

  1. Review existing ESIA documents, technical studies, and design updates related to marine works of the Bay Terminal Project.
  2. Update environmental and social baseline conditions, including marine water quality, sediment, ecology, and socio-economic aspects.
  3. Assess potential environmental and social impacts of dredging, reclamation, breakwater, and associated marine construction activities.
  4. Evaluate compliance with national regulations and World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF), including gap analysis.
  5. Conduct stakeholder identification, consultation and disclosure in accordance with regulatory and donor requirements.
  6. Assess impacts on fisheries, livelihoods, occupational health and safety, and vulnerable groups and prepare subsequent Resettlement Action Plan & Livelihood Restoration plan.
  7. Analyze climate change risks, disaster resilience, and cumulative environmental impacts.
  8. Update Environmental and Social Management Plans (ESMP), including monitoring, mitigation, and emergency response measures.

All studies and designs shall be in accordance with the highest standards of international engineering profession.

Eligible consulting firms are to indicate their interest in providing the above-mentioned services. Interested consultants must provide information indicating that they are qualified to perform the services (such as: brochures, description of similar assignments, experience in similar conditions, availability of appropriate skills among staff etc.).

Assignment Title

Consulting Services for Institutional Capability Development and Operational Strengthening for iTaukei Land Trust Board

Reference Number

Country of Delivery

Republic of Fiji

 

The Government of Fiji through the Ministry of Finance, Strategic Planning, National Development and Statistics has received financing from the World Bank (“WB”) for the Fiji Tourism Development Program in Vanua Levu or ‘Na Vualiku’ and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) will support the Ministry of Tourism and Civil Aviation (“MTCA”) as the lead Implementing Agency, in technical partnership with the iTaukei Land Trust Board (“TLTB”) as the beneficiary institution, to undertake comprehensive institutional capability development and operational strengthening.

The primary purpose of the assignment is to strengthen the institutional capacity, operational readiness, and technical effectiveness of TLTB in those areas most relevant to tourism-related iTaukei land development in the Northern Division so that TLTB is equipped to manage the increased volume and complexity of work the project will generate, and to do so in a way that is efficient, transparent, and genuinely beneficial to iTaukei landowners.

The Services are expected to commence in February 2027 for an assignment duration of Sixteen (16) Months. The lump-sum contract will be signed with payment against acceptance of clearly defined milestones/ deliverables.

The detailed Terms of Reference (“TOR”) for the assignment is available by contacting Mr. Akshay Chand on Akshay.chand01@mtca.gov.fj or clicking the below link.

https://docs.google.com/document/d/1vyoixSfW-Yi13ddZIJGaJ0m3J8NGoNFM/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=116864177158872071295&rtpof=true&sd=true 

The MTCA now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraph 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers dated September 2025 (“the Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

The shortlisting criteria are:   

1. Technical experience in institutional/organizational development, functional reviews, capability development and operational strengthening - The firm shall demonstrate at least eight years of relevant corporate experience in carrying out institutional/organizational assessments or functional reviews, capacity development, institutional strengthening or closely related advisory work. The firm shall also demonstrate successful completion of at least three assignments of comparable complexity during the last ten years, incorporating a combination of capacity development, institutional diagnostic work, and preparation of practical operational tools.

2. Experience in land administration and customary land governance - Demonstrated experience in land administration support, land agencies, lease systems, land records, cadastral or spatial data functions, customary or communal land institutions, or similar land governance environments.

3. GIS, land information systems, and systems planning experience - Relevant advisory experience in reviewing spatial data environments, preparing systems roadmaps, and developing technical requirements for future systems enhancement.

4. Stakeholder engagement and context-sensitive delivery - Evidence of effective work in settings requiring structured consultation with Government, statutory bodies, community stakeholders, customary institutions, women, vulnerable groups, and other actors, preferably in Fiji, the Pacific, or similar small-island contexts.

5. Local Delivery - Firms must demonstrate a credible approach to local delivery, whether through a permanent presence in Fiji, locally-based experts, or formal arrangements with local partners that ensure sustained field engagement in Suva and Vanua Levu throughout the assignment.

6. Project management, quality assurance, and multidisciplinary delivery capability - Firms shall demonstrate internal quality assurance arrangements adequate to support multidisciplinary delivery, timely reporting, and consistent technical standards across all outputs.

1. The Government of Samoa has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the SFSRDP P181456 and intends to apply part of the proceeds to consulting services for the procurement of a Consultant to carry out a diagnostic assessment for a core banking solution for the Central Bank of Samoa.

 

2. The primary objective of the assignment is to conduct a comprehensive diagnostic assessment of the Central Bank’s current operational environment, identify capability gaps, define future-state requirements, and provide a strategic recommendation and roadmap for introducing a Core Banking Solution that aligns with international good practices and future needs of the Central Bank.

 

3. The estimated assignment duration is for 8 weeks. The consulting firm is expected to begin work by January  2027.

 

4. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website: www.cbs.gov.ws and www.mof.gov.ws or can be obtained at the address given below:

2 Apia City Boulevard

5. The Bank now invites eligible all Individual (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing services. All interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualification and relevant experience to perform the Services (attach curriculum vitae with the description of experience in similar assignments, similar conditions, responsiveness to the TOR etc.). Firms; staff may express interest through the employing firm for the assignment and, under such situation, only the experience and qualifications of individuals shall be considered in the selection process.

 

 

6. The evaluation criteria are:

Mandatory

  • A Master’s degree in Information Systems, Computer Science, Finance, Banking, Business Administration, or a related field.
  • A minimum of 10 years of professional experience in financial sector IT strategy and enterprise architecture.
  • Central Banking Domain Expertise, including but not limited to:
    • Core Functions: Proven experience working with or consulting for central banks, specifically regarding monetary policy execution, currency management (vault/mint operations), and government banking.
    • Treasury & Settlement: Deep understanding of Treasury Single Account (TSA) management, Real-Time Gross Settlement (RTGS) system integrations, and Automated Clearing House (ACH) frameworks.
    • Accounting Standards: Familiarity with central bank financial reporting, statutory accounting rules, and international frameworks (e.g., IFRS).

 

  • Enterprise Architecture & Diagnostic Capability, including but not limited to:
    • System Diagnostics: Demonstrated track record of conducting IT gap analyses, legacy system audits, and business process re-engineering (BPR) for complex financial institutions.
    • Core Banking Systems: Strong technical knowledge of modern Core Banking Solutions (CBS), modular service-oriented architectures (SOA), cloud vs. on-premise trade-offs, and data migration complexities.
    • Security & Resilience: Knowledge of financial sector cybersecurity frameworks, business continuity planning (BCP), and disaster recovery (DR) protocols.

 

  • Strategy, Procurement & Roadmap Design, including but not limited to:
    • Strategic Planning: Experience drafting high-level IT roadmaps, cost-benefit analyses, and Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) models for large-scale software implementations.
    • Procurement Knowledge: Experience writing technical specifications, Functional/Technical Requirements documents, and Terms of Reference (TOR) or Requests for Proposals (RFP) for international vendor bidding.

 

  • Communication & Stakeholder Management, including but not limited to:
    • Executive Advisory: Proven capability to interview, advise, and present strategic technical assessments to high-level executives
    • Reporting Skills: Portfolio of high-quality, clear, and structured technical diagnostic reports written in English

 

Desirable

  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.
  • Excellent speaking, writing and interpersonal skills

data.notice_text:
REPUBLIC OF MALAWI
MINISTRY OF ENERGY
 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRM SELECTION)

Country

Malawi

Project Name

ASCENT Malawi Project

Project Number

P502464

Assignment Title

Consultancy for Provision of Fund Management Services for the Ngwee Ngwee Ngwee Fund

Reference No.

MW-MOE.-574017-CS-QCBS

EOI Issue Date

28th September 2026

This request for expression of interest follows the General Procurement Notice for this Project that appeared in the United Nations Development Business (UNDB) on 31st January 2025.

The Government of the Republic of Malawi through the Ministry of Energy (MoE) has received financing from the International Development Association (IDA) and the Energy Sector Management Assistance Program (ESMAP) towards the cost of implementing the Accelerating Sustainable and Clean Energy Access Transformation in Malawi (ASCENT Malawi) Project. It is intended that part of the proceeds of the financing will be used to cover eligible payments under the contract for these consultancy services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) are intended to engage a qualified consulting firm or consortium to provide Fund Management Services for the Ngwee Ngwee Ngwee Fund (NNNF). The Fund Manager will support the Ministry of Energy in delivering ASCENT Malawi Project Components 2, 3 and 4; managing legacy Malawi Electricity Access Project (MEAP) loan collections and residual obligations; and supporting the transition and institutionalisation of the NNNF as a sustainable standalone revolving fund.

The assignment is expected to be implemented over forty-eight (48) Calendar months, from 1st January 2027 to 31st December 2030, subject to contract signature and availability of financing.

The objective of the assignment is to provide specialised fund management services that enable timely, compliant and well-secured financing to eligible Participating Organisations; ensure sound portfolio, fiduciary, safeguards, data and risk management; protect the Fund’s creditor rights; support achievement of ASCENT energy-access and market-development results; and strengthen systems, national capacity and arrangements for the long-term sustainability of the NNNF.

The scope of work under this assignment shall include, but not be limited to:

a) Inception, portfolio takeover, reconciliation and structured handover of existing NNNF facilities, commitments, systems, records and outstanding actions;

b) Cross-cutting fund administration, including drawdown and payment review, portfolio monitoring, forecasting, records management, risk management and reporting;

c) Administration of Component 2 debt and Results-Based Financing (RBF) facilities for off-grid solar companies, including disbursements, repayments, verification interfaces, portfolio quality and recovery actions;

d) Administration of Component 3 financing and performance-linked payments for electrification of public schools and health facilities, in coordination with the ASCENT PIU technical team;

e) Administration of Component 4 clean cooking financing, including loans, repayments, security, portfolio monitoring and carbon-finance interfaces;

f) Management of loan collateral, security perfection, covenant monitoring, enforcement and recoveries, subject to Ministry approvals;

g) Management and collection of the legacy MEAP loan portfolio, including arrears, restructuring, recoveries and close-out actions;

h) Data management, monitoring, dashboards, financial and operational reconciliation, fraud and corruption controls, cybersecurity and data protection;

i) Implementation and monitoring of environmental and social requirements in accordance with the NNNF ESMS, applicable Malawi law and World Bank requirements;

j) Coordination with the Independent Verification Agent, Legal Advisor, Carbon Consultant, technical specialists and other consultants engaged by the Ministry; and

k) Support to institutionalisation of the NNNF, including governance arrangements, capitalisation options, sustainable business model, capacity development, systems transfer and final handover.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TORs) for the assignment can be found at the following websites: Ministry of Energy (https://energy.gov.mw/resources/), Ngwee Ngwee Ngwee Fund (https://www.nnnf.energy.gov.mw/resources/) and ASCENT Malawi Project (https://www.ascent.mw/resources/), or upon request through amopiha@ascent.mw copied to info@ascent.mw and austin.theu@energy.gov.mw. All requests for clarification should be sent through the above email addresses.

The MoE now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are as follows:

1. Core business of the firm(s) and years in business of not less than 5 years organizational capability and relevant experience in fund management, investment, lending, RBF/grant facilities or comparable financing programmes.

2. Relevant similar experience, which should specifically include the below:

a) Off-grid solar and clean cooking sector expertise: experience in, and understanding of, the off-grid solar and clean cooking market in Sub-Saharan Africa, including Energy-as-a-Service and PAYGo solar business models (minimum of five years), together with specific experience in, and understanding of, the Malawi off-grid solar and clean cooking market and the success factors of for-profit businesses in this sector;

b) Results-Based Financing (RBF) and grant facility management: a minimum of three years track record of structuring and managing RBF grant facilities aimed at market stimulation, ideally facilities funded by multilateral development banks, development finance institutions and/or bilateral development assistance agencies;

c) Debt and consumer financing track record: a minimum of three years track record of providing debt financing to off-grid solar and clean cooking distribution businesses and/or consumer finance businesses, including microfinance institutions;

d) Malawi presence and government/development-partner engagement: an established or committed local footprint in Malawi sufficient to manage relationships and reporting with the Government of Malawi and with RBF Grant Window and Debt Window applicants and investees and experience managing reporting relationships with government stakeholders and large development finance organisations;

e) Integration & Institutional Capability: Capacity to integrate sector expertise, financing mechanisms, and local presence, with into a coherent delivery model, supported by evidence of technical and managerial systems for coordinating RBF, debt financing, and stakeholder reporting, and scalable energy-access ability to sustain and scale operations in Malawi’s energy access sector.

3. Technical and managerial capability of the firm (provide only the structure of the organization, general qualifications, and number of key staff. Do not provide CVs of the staff. Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

This Request for Expressions of Interest is open to all eligible firms as defined in the World Bank's Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (July 2016, as revised November 2017, August 2018, September 2023 and February 2025). Firms declared ineligible by the World Bank Group in accordance with the Bank's guidelines on Preventing and Combating Fraud and Corruption in Projects Financed by IBRD Loans and IDA Credits and Grants are not eligible to participate.

Consultants may associate with other firms in the form of a Joint Venture (JV) or sub-consultancy to enhance their qualifications. In the case of a JV, the firms should clearly identify the lead firm and the nature of the association. All partners in a joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality- and Cost-Based (QCBS) Selection method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers.

Interested firms are requested to submit an Expression of Interest containing the following information:

  • Firm Profile: organisation name, legal status, country of registration, year of establishment, core business and contact details.
  • Relevant Experience: description of similar assignments, including client, assignment title, duration, contract value, scope and role of the firm; reference contacts should be provided.
  • Approach Statement: a brief statement responding to the shortlisting criteria outlined above. 
  • Statement of Availability and Commitment: Signed declaration of the firm's availability and commitment to execute the assignment.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours from 8:00 to 12:00 and 13:00 to 16:00 hours local time, Monday to Friday, except National Holidays.

Project ID Nº: P179154

 ASSIGNMENT TITLE: TRAINING OF TEACHERS AND STAFF OF HEIS IN DIGITAL SKILLS

Reference No.: 33/CS/C2SC3.A13.3/25

The Government of the Republic of Angola has received a loan of US$ 150 million from the World Bank (WB) and a donation of US$ 50 million from the Global Partnership for Education (GPE) to implement the TERTIARY EDUCATION, SCIENCE, AND TECHNOLOGY PROJECT (TEST). The Project is budgeted at and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services for the Training of Teachers and Staff of HEIs in Digital Skills.

The referred Project has the following objectives: (i) to improve the quality of student preparation to increase the total number of enrollments and expand opportunities for more equitable access; (ii) to improve the quality and alignment of curricula with the labor market and instruction in priority training areas; and (iii) to improve governance and management of the education sector.

The consulting services ("the Services") include in an integrated and sequential manner, all activities necessary for operationalizing the National Strategy for Digital Skills Development in higher education, ensuring technical rigor, institutional participation, adaptation to the Angolan context, and long-term sustainability.

The consulting service will have a maximum duration of six (6) months.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained at the address given below.

The TERTIARY EDUCATION, SCIENCE, AND TECHNOLOGY PROJECT (TEST) now invites eligible consultancy companies (“Consultants”) to express their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants must provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The shortlisting criteria are:

The consultant can be a company or a consortium of companies and must demonstrate that it has:

  • Specialized expertise in the field of digital skills;
  • Prior experience in assessing and building digital skills within public and private sector organizations;
  • Knowledge of the higher education landscape in Sub-Saharan Africa and PALOP countries is highly desirable.
  • The firm must demonstrate proven experience in the execution of at least three contracts of a similar nature within the last five years, related to digital skills, digital transformation in education, the development of competency frameworks, or large-scale capacity-building programs.

The consulting firm must propose a highly qualified multidisciplinary team with proven experience in digital skills, digital education, and institutional transformation in higher education.

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” on September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest: The aforementioned document can be consulted at the following link: http://pubdocs.worldbank.org/en/813421487104372186/Procurement-Regulations-for-IPF-Borrowers-portuguese.pdf 

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours 08:00 to 3:30 from Monday to Friday.

Expressions of interest must be delivered in writing to the address below by email on October 26th, 2026 by 3:30 pm (Angola local time):

Attention: Ndilu Makenda Nkula

Project Manager

Ministry of Education Higher, Science and Technology and Innovation

Rua do MAT, Complexo Administrativo Clássicos do Talatona, Edifício n.º 2,5º Andar
