data.notice_text:
SOLICITUD DE EXPRESIONES DE INTERÉS

SERVICIOS DE CONSULTORÍA

República Dominicana

Proyecto de Respuesta a Emergencias y Resiliencia de la República Dominicana

Préstamo No.: 9473-DO

Título del Trabajo:  Consultoría para aplicar control de calidad de vuelos fotogramétricos, MDS y MDT y ortoimágenes.

No. de Referencia: DO-MEPyD-470659-CS-QCBS

El Gobierno de la República Dominicana ha recibido financiamiento del Banco Mundial para cubrir el costo del Proyecto de Respuesta a Emergencias y Resiliencia de la República Dominicana a través del Ministerio de la Presidencia y tiene la intención de aplicar parte de los fondos a la contratación de servicios de consultoría.

Los servicios de consultoría ("los Servicios") comprenden la supervisión, verificación progresiva, control de calidad externo y validación técnica de los productos cartográficos básicos generados por el contrato de producción cartográfica del Proyecto. La firma consultora deberá revisar la correcta aplicación del aseguramiento de calidad del Proveedor del Servicio de producción y realizar las comprobaciones independientes adicionales que resulten necesarias, en gabinete y, cuando corresponda, en campo, para verificar la conformidad de los insumos, procesos, productos intermedios y productos finales con las especificaciones técnicas, estándares y criterios de aceptación aplicables.

El alcance comprende, principalmente, los vuelos fotogramétricos con captura de imágenes aéreas y datos LiDAR; puntos de fotocontrol y comprobación; orientación de imágenes y aerotriangulación; ajuste, filtrado y clasificación de nubes de puntos LiDAR; Modelos Digitales de Superficie (MDS) y Modelos Digitales del Terreno (MDT); y mosaicos de ortoimágenes digitales verdaderas (true-orthos), así como la documentación técnica, metadatos, formatos, certificados de calidad y demás respaldos asociados. La producción objeto de supervisión cubre aproximadamente 48,196.00 km² del territorio nacional, diferenciados en zona urbana (2,896.70 km²) y zona rural (45,299.30 km²). Los Servicios tendrán una duración de doce (12) meses calendario, conforme al alcance y condiciones establecidos en los Términos de Referencia (TDR). Esta descripción es de carácter general; el detalle de los alcances y especificaciones técnicas se encuentra en los TDR.

El Ministerio de la Presidencia ahora invita a las firmas consultoras elegibles ("Consultores") a indicar su interés en proporcionar los Servicios. Los Consultores interesados deben proporcionar información que demuestre que tienen las calificaciones requeridas y la experiencia relevante para prestar los Servicios. Los criterios de preselección son:

  • Actividad principal, experiencia y trayectoria de la firma. La firma consultora deberá acreditar trayectoria institucional en servicios relacionados con información geoespacial, cartografía, geodesia, fotogrametría aérea, teledetección, LiDAR, modelos digitales de elevaciones, ortoimágenes, control de calidad cartográfica, supervisión técnica o validación de productos geoespaciales. Deberá demostrar una experiencia general mínima de ocho (8) años y haber ejecutado satisfactoriamente al menos cinco (5) contratos relacionados con estos servicios durante los últimos ocho (8) años.
  • Experiencia específica y comparabilidad de proyectos. La firma deberá acreditar al menos tres (3) contratos de naturaleza comparable ejecutados satisfactoriamente durante los últimos ocho (8) años. En conjunto, dichas experiencias deberán incluir: (i) al menos dos (2) contratos con actividades de supervisión, auditoría técnica, QA/QC, validación o aceptación de productos fotogramétricos y/o LiDAR; (ii) al menos un (1) proyecto de cobertura nacional, subnacional extensa, regional o territorialmente continua; y (iii) al menos un (1) proyecto que haya comprendido productos LiDAR y modelos digitales de elevaciones, además de ortoimágenes u ortofotos. Un mismo contrato podrá acreditar más de una condición cuando su alcance lo demuestre de manera verificable. La experiencia en producción cartográfica será considerada únicamente cuando evidencie funciones sustantivas de aseguramiento o control de calidad sobre los productos generados.
  • Capacidad técnica, organizativa y operativa. La firma deberá demostrar capacidad para ejecutar revisiones concurrentes y especializadas por bloques, productos o frentes de trabajo; aplicar procedimientos de QA/QC; gestionar grandes volúmenes de imágenes aéreas, nubes de puntos LiDAR, MDS, MDT y ortoimágenes; y mantener trazabilidad documental, control de versiones y seguimiento de observaciones y subsanaciones. Deberá acreditar disponibilidad de recursos computacionales, software, licencias, infraestructura de procesamiento y almacenamiento, herramientas especializadas y mecanismos seguros de intercambio y respaldo de información, así como capacidad organizativa para iniciar oportunamente la consultoría y cumplir los tiempos de revisión previstos.
  • Correspondencia con el alcance de la consultoría. La correspondencia será valorada mediante el análisis integrado de la experiencia y las capacidades institucionales acreditadas frente a la escala y complejidad de los Servicios. Se considerará especialmente la experiencia en revisión y validación de planes de vuelo, cobertura y GSD, GNSS/IMU, control terrestre, aerotriangulación, ajuste y clasificación LiDAR, MDS/MDT, ortorrectificación, ortoimágenes verdaderas, exactitud posicional, completitud, consistencia radiométrica, formatos, metadatos y trazabilidad documental, así como la capacidad para coordinar técnicamente con el Contratante y el Proveedor del Servicio de producción preservando la independencia del control de calidad externo.

La firma consultora deberá actuar con independencia técnica respecto del Proveedor del Servicio de producción y declarar cualquier vínculo contractual, societario, comercial, técnico o profesional que pueda comprometer la objetividad de la supervisión. Los Servicios se prestarán en idioma español, en modalidad combinada de gabinete y, cuando corresponda, actividades presenciales o verificaciones de campo. La firma adjudicataria deberá disponer o establecer una oficina local en Santo Domingo durante la ejecución de la consultoría.

Nota: Los Expertos Clave no serán evaluados en la etapa de preselección y no deberán presentarse CV en esta etapa.

Para estos fines la firma consultora deberá remitir la documentación de forma clara, estructurada, verificable y directamente vinculada con los criterios de preselección establecidos en la presente Solicitud de Expresiones de Interés (SEI). El documento principal no deberá exceder de cuarenta (40) páginas. Los documentos legales y los soportes documentales presentados para acreditar la experiencia y capacidad declaradas no se computarán dentro de este límite y deberán incorporarse como anexos debidamente identificados, paginados y referenciados. La documentación técnica de soporte no deberá exceder de ciento cincuenta (150) páginas para una firma consultora individual. En caso de APCA, consorcio, joint venture o asociación equivalente, el límite será de ciento cincuenta (150) páginas por cada integrante que acredite experiencia o capacidad técnica, organizativa u operativa relevante para los criterios de preselección. El registro mercantil, la nómina de accionistas y los documentos legales equivalentes no se computarán dentro de estos límites de páginas.

La documentación requerida es la siguiente:

  • Carta de expresión de interés, con datos generales de la firma consultora (firmada y sellada).
  • Detalle de experiencia directa de la firma consultora donde se evidencie: actividad principal y años en el negocio, experiencia general y específica, capacidad técnica y de gestión de acuerdo con los criterios indicados. Para cada experiencia declarada deberá indicarse, como mínimo, el nombre del contrato o proyecto, cliente y país, fechas de ejecución, monto contractual, alcance, rol desempeñado por la firma o integrante de la APCA, productos o actividades efectivamente ejecutados, superficie o cobertura territorial, componentes fotogramétricos y/o LiDAR comprendidos, funciones de QA/QC, supervisión o validación realizadas, criterios o estándares de calidad aplicados, criterio o criterios de preselección que acredita y referencia exacta del soporte documental presentado. Para acreditar las experiencias no será necesario presentar el contrato completo; podrán aportarse únicamente las páginas pertinentes del contrato, certificaciones, actas de recepción, constancias de conformidad, informes finales aprobados u otra documentación equivalente emitida o validada por el cliente o contratante que permita verificar la experiencia declarada.
  • Estructura organizativa general de la Firma Consultora o APCA, con una breve descripción de sus áreas técnicas, capacidades institucionales, recursos permanentes, infraestructura computacional, software y mecanismos de gestión y control de calidad relevantes para la consultoría. En esta etapa no deberán presentarse CV ni se evaluarán las calificaciones de expertos individuales.
  • Declaración de independencia técnica y ausencia de conflictos de interés que puedan afectar la objetividad de la consultoría, con el compromiso de informar al Contratante cualquier posible conflicto que se identifique durante el proceso de selección o la ejecución del contrato.
  • Registro mercantil actualizado o equivalente en su país de origen.
  • Nómina de accionistas o documento equivalente en su país de origen.

Nota: Toda la documentación que se presente deberá estar en idioma español.

La lista corta estará integrada por un mínimo de cinco (5) y un máximo de ocho (8) firmas consultoras.

Se llama la atención de los Consultores interesados sobre la Sección III, párrafos 3.14, 3.16 y 3.17 de las “Regulaciones de Adquisiciones para Prestatarios en Proyectos de Inversión del Banco Mundial”, actualizadas a noviembre de 2020 (“Regulaciones de Adquisiciones”), en las que se establece la política del Banco Mundial sobre conflictos de intereses.

Los Consultores podrán asociarse con otras firmas para mejorar sus calificaciones y deberán indicar claramente si la asociación se presenta como APCA (joint venture, consorcio o asociación equivalente) o como subconsultoría. En caso de APCA, todos sus integrantes serán conjunta y solidariamente responsables de la totalidad del contrato, si resultan seleccionados.

El Consultor será seleccionado conforme al método de Selección Basada en Calidad y Costo (SBCC/QCBS), de acuerdo con las Regulaciones de Adquisiciones.

Se puede obtener más información durante el horario de oficina de 08:00 a 16:00 horas, en las oficinas de este Viceministerio ubicadas en la calle César Nicolás Penson núm. 48, Distrito Nacional, Santo Domingo, República Dominicana, o mediante comunicación escrita dirigida al correo electrónico adquisicioneseyr@minpre.gob.do.

Los TDR podrán solicitarse, sin costo, mediante comunicación dirigida al correo electrónico antes indicado, haciendo constar en el asunto la referencia del proceso, o descargarse desde el enlace correspondiente a este proceso, publicado en el Portal de Transparencia del Ministerio de la Presidencia: https://minpre.gob.do/transparencia/compras-y-contrataciones/contratacion-de-consultoria-para-aplicar-control-de-calidad-de-vuelos-fotogrametricos-mds-y-mdt-y-ortoimagenes-ref-do-mepyd-470659-cs-qcbs/.

Las expresiones de interés deben enviarse por escrito a la siguiente dirección (en persona, por correo o por correo electrónico) hasta el 26 de octubre de 2026, a las 4:00 p. m. (hora de la República Dominicana).

Republic of Tajikistan

Title: Chief Livelihoods Specialist

Reference No.: TWEEP-CS-IC-11

The State Committee on Investment and State Property Management of the Republic of Tajikistan (SCISPM) has received financing from the World Bank toward the preparation and implementation of the Tajikistan Women’s Economic Empowerment Project (TWEEP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for the engagement of an individual consultant for the full-time position of Chief Livelihoods Specialist.

The assignment is to provide PIG-side technical oversight and quality assurance for Component 1, “Support to Women and Women’s Groups for Improved Livelihoods,” including Subcomponents 1.1, 1.2, and 1.3. The Specialist will serve as the PIG’s primary technical counterpart for the Technical Partner for Component 1 (TP1) and, under the Project Coordinator, will monitor the quality, timeliness, and results of TP1 implementation; review key methodologies, work plans, training approaches and materials, beneficiary-support tools, and technical deliverables; assess livelihood and grant-supported activities for commercial viability and market linkages; conduct risk-based field monitoring and spot checks; and advise the Project Coordinator on technical acceptability and corrective measures. Under Subcomponent 1.1, 3,200 women will be trained in business and technical skills, of whom 1,600 will be selected to receive in-kind grants followed by mentoring and coaching. The Specialist will work full-time at the Project Implementation Group (PIG) office at SCISPM in Dushanbe, with regular field visits to the Project’s target districts. The initial contract will be for twelve (12) months, including a three (3)-month probationary period, and may be extended subject to satisfactory performance, availability of funding, and Project needs, tentatively until April 2029.

Education

data.notice_text:
TERMS OF REFERENCE

National Individual Consultant

Site Engineer (Two Positions)

Title

Site Engineer (two (2) positions)

Contractual Arrangement

Local Recruitment

Expected Start Date

November 9th 2026

Contract Duration

Eight (8) months (November 2026 – July 2027), with possibility of extension subject to satisfactory performance, project needs, and availability of funding.

Level of Input

Full-time

Project

Nurturing Early Skills through Technology (NEST) Project

Financing Partner

The World Bank

Hiring Organization

Shanti Volunteer Association (SVA)

Duty Station

Position 1:

Battambang Province (covering project sites in Kos Kralar, Ek Phnom and Thmar Kaul Districts)

Position 2: Banteay Meanchey Province (covering project sites in Phnom Srok District)

Contract Type

Time Based

1.  Background

The Nurturing Early Skills through Technology (NEST) Project is funded by the Japan Social Development Fund (JSDF) and administered by the World Bank. The Project is implemented by Shanti Volunteer Association (SVA) in close collaboration with the Ministry of Education, Youth and Sport (MoEYS) of Cambodia.

The Project aims to enhance access to and quality of Early Childhood Education (ECE) through the promotion of learning through play and the integration of digital technology in target districts in Cambodia. The Project supports teacher professional development, establishment of an ECE digital resource platform, parental and community engagement, improvement of preschool learning environments through construction and renovation, and implementation of pilot school meal programs.

The Project is implemented in selected districts in Battambang, Banteay Meanchey, and Pailin provinces, targeting public preschools with the objective of strengthening equitable access to quality ECE services for young children aged 3–5 years.

Under Component 2 of the Project, SVA will implement phase 1 of civil works activities, comprising: (i) construction of 8 new preschool buildings, toilets, water tanks and 6 kitchen facilities.; (ii) renovation of 17 existing preschool buildings; and (iii) outdoor environment improvements at  25 targeted preschools. These works are spread across three districts in Battambang province and one district in Banteay Meanchey Province., and procured through Request for Bids (RFB) and Request for Quotations (RFQ) methods

To strengthen day-to-day site supervision during the main construction period, SVA seeks to recruit two (2) National Individual Consultants – Site Engineers, one (1) based in Battambang Province and one (1) based in Banteay Meanchey Province. The Site Engineers will provide full-time, on-site supervision over the prime contractor(s) at project sites in their assigned provinces, under the technical guidance of the Civil Engineer Consultant and the SVA Engineer.

2.  Objectives

The objective of this assignment is to ensure that the prime contractor’s civil works at project sites are executed in accordance with the approved drawings, technical specifications, Bills of Quantities (BoQ), and contract requirements, through on-site supervision by the Site Engineer.

Specifically, the Site Engineer will:

  • Provide full-time, day-to-day on-site supervision of the prime contractor’s works at project sites in the assigned province.
  • Ensure quality of materials and workmanship are complied with specification, approved drawing, method statement and schedules.
  • Ensure that the prime contractor executed all work in compliance with approved Environmental and Social(E&S) document
  • Maintain accurate and complete site records, including site diaries, inspection checklists, measurement records, and photo documentation.
  • Provide verified site-level information (progress, quantities, defects) to the Civil Engineer Consultant and SVA Engineer to support progress monitoring, payment certification, and completion.

3.  Scope of Work

Under the technical guidance of the Civil Engineer Consultant and the SVA Engineer, the Consultant shall undertake the following tasks at project sites in the assigned province:

a.  Site Mobilization and Pre-Construction

  • Become familiar with the approved drawings, technical specifications, BoQs, contract documents, and contractors’ work programs for each assigned site, and report any discrepancies to the Civil Engineer and SVA Engineer.
  • Participate in site handover to contractors and in pre-mobilization meetings with contractors, school representatives, and the SVA project team.
  • Sites readiness: coordinate with contractor’s supervisor and relevant stakeholders at target schools during contractor mobilization.
  • Prepare and submit updated sites plan including photos
  • Confirm that contractors have mobilized the required personnel, equipment, materials, site signage, and safety arrangements before works begin.

b.  Day-to-Day Site Supervision and Quality Control

  • Conduct full-time, day-to-day supervision of civil works at assigned sites, prioritizing site visits according to construction schedules and critical activities.
  • Inspect and verify key construction stages before contractors proceed (e.g., reinforcement and formwork inspection prior to concreting), using standard inspection checklists.
  • Verify that materials delivered to site comply with approved samples and technical specifications, and reject and record non-compliant materials.
  • Witness and record field and material tests (e.g., concrete slump tests, sampling of concrete test cubes, compaction checks), and follow up on test results.
  • Issue site instructions to contractors on quality and workmanship issues within delegated authority, and refer matters beyond this authority, including design changes and variations, to the Civil Engineer Consultant and SVA Engineer.

c.  Site Records, Progress Monitoring and Reporting

  • Maintain a site diary for each site, recording daily activities, workforce and equipment, weather conditions, materials delivered, inspections, instructions issued, visitors, and issues.
  • Maintain photo documentation (before, during, and after works) and inspection records for each site.
  • Monitor actual progress against contractors’ approved work programs, and report delays together with proposed corrective measures.
  • Prepare weekly site progress reports and monthly reports, and submit them to the Civil Engineer Consultant and SVA Engineer.
  • Participate in regular site meetings and record minutes and agreed actions, as required.

d.  Measurement and Payment Support

  • Verify at sites the actual completed works in Activity Schedule submitted by contractors
  • Prepare measurement sheets and supporting documentation for contractors’ payment applications, for review by the Civil Engineer Consultant and SVA Engineer.
  • Record and report site conditions or instructions that may give rise to variations or claims, with supporting evidence, for review by the Civil Engineer Consultant and SVA Engineer.

e.  Environmental, Social, and Safety Compliance

  • Monitor contractors’ daily implementation of occupational health and safety (OHS) measures, including use of personal protective equipment (PPE), site fencing and barricading, safety signage, safe working at height, and first aid, with particular attention to the safety of children, teachers, and community members at operating preschools.
  • Monitor implementation of E&S mitigation measures at construction sites, including dust and noise control, waste management, drainage, and agreed working hours, in coordination with the E&S Specialist.
  • Monitor contractor compliance with labor management requirements, including workers’ code of conduct and prevention of child labor.
  • Report E&S incidents, accidents, and non-compliance to the E&S Specialist and SVA Project Manager immediately, and in any case within 24 hours, and follow up on corrective actions.
  • Liaise with school directors, School Management Committees (SMCs), and local authorities on site-level matters, and refer community concerns and grievances to the Project Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM).

f.  Completion and Handover

  • Participate in pre-completion and final inspections, and prepare defect (snagging) lists for each site.
  • Monitor rectification of defects by contractors and confirm completion of rectification works.
  • Compile site-level completion documentation, including as-built mark-ups, photo records, test records, and site diaries.
  • Support the handover of completed facilities to schools, School Management Committees (SMCs), and relevant government counterparts.

4.  Expected Outputs and Deliverables

The following deliverables are expected over the course of the assignment. Timelines are indicative and subject to adjustment based on project implementation progress and construction schedules.

#

Deliverable

Timeline

1

Inception Work Plan and site supervision schedule for assigned sites

Within two (2) weeks of contract signing

2

Site diaries and inspection checklists for each site

Daily (submitted with weekly reports)

3

Weekly site progress report (progress, quality issues, instructions issued, E&S/OHS observations, and photos)

 

Weekly

4

Monthly report, including progress against work programs and E&S compliance

Monthly

5

Material inspection and test records, and measurement sheets supporting contractors’ payment applications

 

As required, in line with contractors’ payment schedules

6

E&S and OHS incident reports

Within 24 hours of occurrence

7

Defect lists and pre-completion inspection reports for each site

Prior to practical completion at each site

8

Site completion documentation package and Final Report

Upon practical completion of each site; Final Report at end of contract

5.  Work Supervision

The Consultant will work under the overall supervision of the SVA Project Manager and will receive day-to-day technical guidance from the Civil Engineer Consultant and the SVA Engineer.

The Consultant will coordinate and liaise with:

  • The Civil Engineer, the SVA Engineer, and the other Site Engineer, to ensure a consistent supervision approach across provinces;
  • PMU members and field staff;
  • The E&S Specialist and other technical consultants engaged under the Project;
  • Contractors, site supervisors, and construction personnel at project sites;
  • School directors, School Management Committees (SMCs), community representatives, and sub-national authorities at project sites.

The Consultant shall submit site records and weekly reports to the Civil Engineer Consultant and SVA Engineer, and monthly reports to the SVA Project Manager through the SVA Engineer, for review and approval. The Consultant shall participate in regular coordination meetings, site meetings, and World Bank supervision missions, as required.

6.  Contract Term and Location of Assignment

The contract period is eight (8) months, from November 2026 to July 2027, with possibility of extension subject to satisfactory performance, project needs, and availability of funding.

The Consultant will be engaged as a full-time Individual Consultant (IC) under the NEST Project and is expected to be present at project sites on a daily basis throughout the assignment period.

Key arrangements are as follows:

  • Duty Station: Position 1 – Battambang Province (covering project sites in Kos Kralar, Ek Phnom and Thmar Kaul Districts) Position 2 – Banteay Meanchey Province (covering project sites in Phnom Srok District)
  • Contract Modality: The contract will be time-based, with remuneration at a fixed monthly rate for the duration of the assignment.
  • Working Arrangements: Full-time, in accordance with SVA working hours. Work outside regular working hours may be required in line with construction activities, subject to SVA policy.
  • The Consultant is expected to work primarily at project sites and to make their own arrangements for workspace. No office space will be provided by SVA; however, the Consultant may use the SVA Battambang Office for meetings or as required. The Consultant is expected to provide their own computer, smartphone for photo documentation, and personal working equipment.
  • Payment Modality: Payment shall be made on a monthly basis upon submission and approval of monthly reports and agreed deliverables.
  • Travel costs directly related to project implementation and approved by SVA, including daily travel to project sites, will be covered in accordance with SVA travel policy.

7.  Consultant Qualifications

Education

  • Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering, Construction Engineering, Architecture, or other relevant technical field. A technical diploma with additional relevant site experience may be considered.

Experience

  • Minimum two (2) years of relevant professional experience in site supervision of building construction and/or renovation works.
  • Hands-on experience in site-level quality control, including stage inspections, material checks, and quantity measurement.
  • Experience in maintaining site diaries, inspection records, and progress reports.
  • Experience in construction of schools or other public or community buildings is an advantage.
  • Experience working on World Bank-financed or other internationally funded projects is an advantage.

Technical Competencies

  • Sound practical knowledge of building construction methods, materials, and quality control at site.
  • Ability to read and interpret construction drawings, technical specifications, and Bills of Quantities.
  • Ability to carry out site measurements and quantity verification.
  • Familiarity with occupational health and safety (OHS) requirements and environmental and social compliance in construction settings.
  • Ability to keep accurate records and prepare clear and timely reports.
  • Proficiency in MS Office (Word and Excel); knowledge of AutoCAD is an advantage.

data.title: Technical Assistance to operationalize the Road Asset Management System (RAMS)
data.project_name: Moldova Rural Connectivity Project
data.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

 

 

Country: Moldova

Name of Project: Moldova Rural Connectivity Project

Project ID: P180153

 

Assignment Title: Technical assistance for the further development of Road Asset Management System in Moldova

 

Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): MRCP/CS/08

 

The Government of the Republic of Moldova has received financing from the World Bank (the “Bank” or the “WB”) in the form of a loan/credit toward the cost of the Moldova Rural Connectivity Project. The S.A. ”Administraia Naional a Drumurilor” (“NRA” or JSC “National Road Administration”), an implementing agency (the “Client”), intends to apply part of the proceeds of this loan/credit to eligible payments under the contract for which this Request for Expressions of Interest is issued.

NRA has developed and operates a Road Asset Management System (RAMS). However, there are still many unresolved issues that prevent the proper use of the RAMS as a key pillar for the further effective road investment and maintenance planning processes, such as: lack of integration/interoperability of sub systems; manual intensive data collection; fragmentation of roles in RAMS related data collection and utilization; non-clear future alignment with the road register; lack of the sufficient legal regulation.

NRA intends to retain a consultant to lay the strategic, technical, institutional, and legal groundwork for the modernization of NRA's Road Asset Management System, so that Moldova's national road network can be managed efficiently, cost-effectively, and in line with European standards. Specifically, consultant will be required to review business processes and recommend improvements; review of existing IT based tools, software, databases, etc. architecture and integration and recommendations for further improvement preparation; develop a future RAMS Roadmap; define the asset inventory scope and data governance framework required for the future RAMS; Policy Framework Development; develop a training program and conduct a number of in-person workshops covering mentioned above topics.

 

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained following a formal request to the Client to procurement.wb@andsa.md.

 

The NRA now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Consulting Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The Consultant will be a firm or a group of firms (JVCA[1]) with previous project experience related to Construction Supervision Services.

 

The shortlisting criteria:

The following shortlisting criteria will be applied to all consulting firms (individual company or joint venture overall) that have submitted EoI:

1. Criterion: General Firm Experience

Proven general experience and verifiable track record in providing consultancy/technical assistance related to Road Asset Management Systems (RAMSs), completed within the past ten (10) years. RAMS-related consultancy/technical assistance may cover studies; strategies; policy frameworks; institutional support; or preparation of methodologies, guidelines, and standards.

Scoring:

The Consultant shall be awarded up to 20 points based on the quality and relevance of project references.

 

2. Criterion: Development or implementation of RAMS solutions

Proven specific expertise and verifiable track record in the assignments related to development or implementation of the existing RAMS solutions, deployed on local and/or national road networks with paved and unpaved roads, completed within the past ten (10) years. For the purpose of this criterion, an assignment shall be considered completed if the RAMS solution has been fully developed and/or deployed and formally accepted by the client, regardless of subsequent maintenance or update activities.

Preference will be given to projects related to the local road networks.

Scoring:

The Consultant shall be awarded up to 40 points based on the quality and relevance of project references.

 

3. Criterion: Road network data

Proven specific expertise and verifiable track record in the assignments related to road network data survey, collection, and verification to be incorporated in a developed road database, completed within the past ten (10) years.

Scoring:

The Consultant shall be awarded up to 30 points based on the quality and relevance of project references.

 

4. Criterion: Training

Proven specific expertise and verifiable track record in delivering training related to RAMS completed within the last ten (10) years, with preference given to projects related to the local road networks.

Scoring:

  1. The Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa (COMESA) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Accelerating Sustainable and Clean Energy Access Transformation (ASCENT) Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services

 

2. The objective of the consulting services (“the Services”) is to support the development and application of geospatial least-cost electrification planning approaches, including the identification of optimal combinations of grid extension, mini-grid, and standalone systems to achieve universal access objectives, and to be grounded in internationally recognized methodologies that ensure transparency, consistency, and reproducibility of analytical approaches, as well as the development or strengthening of related geospatial data systems, data governance arrangements, interoperability mechanisms, and digital decision-support tools

 

3. Scope of service”; The services to be provided under the Framework Agreement are organized into indicative service components, which describe the range of technical support that may be required

 

Individual assignments issued under the Framework Agreement may involve one or several service components, depending on the needs of the requesting Project Implementation Unit (PIU).

 

The combination and scope of services to be provided under each assignment will depend on the specific needs of the requesting PIU and the nature of the Service Request submitted to COMESA.

Service component 1:

 Development of National Electrification Analyses (NEAs).

 

Consulting firms may support participating PIUs in preparing or updating National Electrification Analyses using geospatial least-cost electrification modelling methodologies. Activities may include the collection and validation of spatial datasets, development or updating of geospatial least-cost electrification models, analysis of grid extension, mini-grid and standalone electrification options, and preparation of electrification investment planning scenarios.

 

Service component 2:

Updating Existing Electrification Plans and Models.

 

Consulting firms may assist PIUs in reviewing and updating existing electrification plans and modelling tools. Activities may include updating modelling assumptions and datasets, recalibrating electrification planning models, incorporating updated demand forecasts or policy targets, and producing revised electrification planning outputs.

Service component 3:

Spatial Data Infrastructure (SDI), Data Governance and Interoperability.

 

Consulting firms may assist PIUs in establishing or strengthening national spatial data infrastructure (SDI) systems, data governance arrangements and interoperable geospatial data platforms to support energy access planning. Activities may include assessing SDI readiness, identifying data architecture and interoperability gaps, developing data governance frameworks and standards, and establishing or enhancing geospatial data platforms, metadata catalogues and data-sharing mechanisms, including, where relevant, open-source or interoperable platforms such as GeoNode, CKAN, or equivalent tools.

 

Service component 4:

Development of Visualization and Decision-Support Platforms.

 

Consulting firms may support the development of digital platforms and tools that facilitate the analysis and dissemination of electrification planning outputs. Activities may include development of geospatial dashboards, creation of data portals for electrification planning outputs, and integration with national energy information systems.

Service component 5:

Capacity Building and Institutional Support.

 

Consulting firms may provide technical assistance and training to strengthen national capacities in geospatial electrification planning. Activities may include training on modelling methodologies and planning tools, support for data management processes, and preparation of technical guidelines and operational manuals.

 

The consulting services “Framework Agreement for Geospatial Electrification Planning and Analytical Services” include establishment for an initial period of three (3) years and may, subject to satisfactory performance, continued need, availability of financing, and any applicable approvals, be extended for up to two (2) additional one-year periods.

The Ministry of Public Works and Transport (MPWT) of the Royal Government of Cambodia (RGC) has applied for financing support from the World Bank's (WB) International Development Association (IDA) to implement the Cambodia Regional Connectivity Improvement Project (CRCI) with and duration of six (6.5) years starting in early 2027. Component 2: Institutional Capacity Strengthening in Logistics and Trade Facilitation

Component 3: Phase 1 Project Management and Phase 2 Preparation

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES - INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT - INTERNATIONAL)

Republic of North Macedonia

Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Water Economy

Zletovica Productivity through Irrigation and Renewable Energy Project (PIREP)

Grant No.: TF0D2152

Assignment Title: Senior Hydraulic and Water Resources Engineer (International Consultant)

Reference No.: PIREP-IC-06

The Republic of North Macedonia has received financing from the World Bank, acting as trustee of the Grant Facility for Project Preparation (GFPP), for the preparation of the Zletovica Productivity through Irrigation and Renewable Energy Project (PIREP), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. The Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Water Economy (MAFWE), through its Project Implementation Unit (PIU), is responsible for the implementation of the grant.

The preparation grant supports the updating of technical and hydraulic studies, dam safety documentation, transboundary water analyses, and environmental and social instruments for Phases II and III of the Zletovica Hydrosystem, comprising irrigation development and hydropower generation. The PIU implements the grant in close partnership with PS Zletovica, which leads the technical preparation and prioritization of activities.

The objective of this assignment is to provide overall technical leadership and independent engineering oversight to PS Zletovica, in coordination with the PIU, for preparing Phases II and III. The Consultant will serve as Technical Team Leader, coordinating and assuring the quality of construction-ready detailed designs, cost estimates, technical specifications and civil works bidding documents, and supporting appraisal, permitting, procurement and financing readiness.

The consulting services ("the Services") include coordinating multidisciplinary technical inputs; reviewing studies, investigations, water-resources and hydraulic analyses; advising on investment options and prioritization; reviewing final detailed designs and dam-safety interfaces; integrating environmental and social requirements; providing technical inputs for international-waterways assessments under OP 7.50, economic and financial analyses and jobs contribution reporting; supporting permits and regulatory compliance; reviewing and finalizing technical procurement packages; providing technical procurement support subject to applicable conflict-of-interest requirements; and undertaking capacity building, reporting and missions. The Consultant will report contractually to the PIU Project Director/Coordinator and work in close technical coordination with the Director and designated technical representatives of PS Zletovica, coordinating the inputs of the local Senior Irrigation Engineer and other technical specialists.

The assignment is expected to require up to 90 working days during the GFPP implementation period, ending in December 2027. The allocation of inputs by task and deliverable will be proposed in the inception work plan, with the timing of services coordinated with project-preparation milestones and related activities. The Consultant may work remotely and in North Macedonia, subject to the approved work plan. At least one-third of the total level of effort shall be delivered in North Macedonia. When in North Macedonia, the Consultant will be based primarily at PS Zletovica’s offices, with travel to project sites and relevant institutions as required. Monthly trips to North Macedonia will be required, as agreed with PS Zletovica and the PIU.

The complete Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment are included in Annex 1 to this Request for Expressions of Interest and form an integral part of it.

MAFWE now invites eligible individuals ("Consultants") to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information (curriculum vitae and references in English language only) demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

•     Master’s degree in civil, hydraulic, water resources, irrigation, hydropower, or a closely related engineering field. A relevant professional engineering registration or equivalent certification is desirable.

•     At least 15 years of relevant professional experience in hydraulic engineering, water-resources planning, irrigation infrastructure, hydropower, and multipurpose water systems.

•     Demonstrated senior-level experience in at least three large or technically complex irrigation or multipurpose water-resources projects involving dams or reservoirs, water-conveyance systems, pressurized or gravity-fed irrigation networks, and/or hydropower facilities.

•     Experience as Team Leader, Technical Team Leader, Lead Engineer, or Independent Technical Reviewer in at least two multidisciplinary assignments covering feasibility, detailed design, procurement documentation, and implementation readiness.

•     Demonstrated experience reviewing final detailed designs, design calculations, drawings, technical specifications, bills of quantities, cost estimates, construction methods, and civil works bidding documents.

•     Strong experience in hydrological and hydraulic analysis, water allocation and reservoir operation, climate-resilience assessment, irrigation demand, pumping and conveyance systems, and technical interfaces with dam safety and hydropower.

•     Experience with flow measurement, automation, SCADA, commissioning, operation and maintenance, and asset-management arrangements is desirable.

•     Experience providing engineering inputs to environmental and social assessments, economic and financial analysis, construction permitting, and international-waterways assessments is highly desirable.

•     Familiarity with World Bank-financed investment projects, the Environmental and Social Framework, OP 7.50, Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, and Standard Procurement Documents is a strong advantage.

•     Experience in North Macedonia, the Western Balkans, or countries with comparable technical and regulatory conditions is desirable.

•     Strong analytical, leadership, coordination, and technical writing skills, including the ability to communicate complex issues clearly and provide practical, decision-oriented recommendations.

•     Excellent written and spoken English. Knowledge of Macedonian or another relevant regional language is an advantage.

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraphs 3.15, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, Seventh Edition, September 2025 ("Procurement Regulations"), setting forth the World Bank’s policies on conflict of interest and unfair competitive advantage.

The objective of this assignment is to provide PE HS Zletovica and the PIU with senior technical advice and engineering oversight for the preparation and early implementation of the Phase III hydropower investments, while ensuring their integration with Phase II irrigation investments and the existing multipurpose system. The Engineer will help ensure that the investments are technically sound, economically and financially justified, safe, climate-resilient, construction-ready, operable and maintainable, compliant with applicable national requirements, and aligned with World Bank requirements.

The consulting services ("the Services") include supporting hydropower-related procurement and, when formally appointed, providing technical input as a member of evaluation committees; reviewing feasibility studies, hydrological and energy-yield analyses, detailed designs, technical specifications, bills of quantities, cost estimates and bidding documents; optimizing hydropower schemes; reviewing electro-mechanical and electrical systems, SCADA, grid interconnection and commissioning arrangements; coordinating hydropower development with irrigation, drinking-water supply, reservoir operations and dam safety; integrating environmental and social requirements; supporting approvals and permits; reviewing consultant and contractor outputs; conducting site inspections; supporting construction, testing, commissioning and handover; and providing appraisal inputs, reports and capacity building. The Engineer will report technically to the Director of PE HS Zletovica. The PIU Coordinator/Project Director will serve as the contract-management focal point and provide administrative oversight and coordination on procurement, fiduciary, environmental and social matters.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

Republic of North Macedonia

Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Water Economy

Zletovica Productivity through Irrigation and Renewable Energy Project (PIREP)

Grant No.: TF0D2152

Assignment Title: Environmental and Social Specialist – Project Implementation Unit

Reference No.: PIREP-IC-08

The Republic of North Macedonia has received financing from the World Bank, acting as trustee of the Grant Facility for Project Preparation (GFPP), for the preparation of the Zletovica Productivity through Irrigation and Renewable Energy Project (PIREP), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. The Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Water Economy (MAFWE), through its Project Implementation Unit (PIU), is responsible for implementation of the grant.

The preparation grant supports the updating of technical and hydraulic studies, dam safety documentation, transboundary-water analyses, and environmental and social instruments for Phases II and III of the Zletovica Hydrosystem, comprising irrigation development and hydropower generation. The PIU implements the grant in close coordination with the Public Enterprise for Water Management Activities HS “Zletovica”–Probištip (PE HS Zletovica), which provides technical leadership, data, access to facilities and institutional support.

The objective of the assignment is to ensure that environmental and social considerations are systematically integrated into: (i) the planning and implementation of GFPP-financed studies, surveys, investigations, and other preparatory activities; and (ii) the technical, environmental, social, permitting, procurement, and institutional preparation of the proposed World Bank-financed investment for Phases II and III. The Specialist will support compliance with the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF), the Environmental and Social Standards (ESSs) determined to be relevant through project screening and assessment, the World Bank Group Environmental, Health and Safety Guidelines, applicable good international industry practice, World Bank Operational Policy OP 7.50 on Projects on International Waterways, as applicable, and the environmental and social legislation of North Macedonia.

The assignment will cover integrated environmental and social risk management, while recognizing that specialized technical inputs may be required for complex subjects. Particular emphasis will be placed on environmental and social assessment, biodiversity and natural-habitat protection, environmental flows and water quality, pollution prevention, land and livelihood impacts, labor and working conditions, stakeholder engagement and grievance management, dam and community safety, climate resilience, cumulative and transboundary impacts, cultural heritage, and incorporation of mitigation measures into designs, cost estimates, bidding documents, contracts, and supervision arrangements.

The Environmental and Social Specialist will serve as the Project Implementation Unit’s principal environmental and social focal point and will support the unit in managing environmental and social risks associated with GFPP-financed preparatory activities and the proposed Zletovica irrigation and hydropower investments, ensuring compliance with national legislation, the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework, relevant Environmental and Social Standards, and applicable requirements on international waterways. Responsibilities will include screening project activities; reviewing and quality-assuring environmental and social assessments and management instruments; integrating mitigation measures into technical designs, bidding documents and implementation arrangements; and addressing water resources, biodiversity, climate, cumulative impacts, land acquisition, labor and community safety considerations, in coordination with technical and dam-safety experts. The Specialist will monitor preparatory field activities and corrective actions, support incident reporting, coordinate stakeholder engagement and grievance management, track environmental and social commitments and permitting requirements, liaise with competent authorities and the World Bank, and provide training, technical advice and reporting to strengthen the PIU’s and PE HS Zletovica’s capacity for project preparation and implementation.

The Specialist will report directly to the PIU Coordinator and will work in close coordination with PE HS Zletovica management and technical staff, World Bank environmental and social specialists, consultants preparing technical and environmental and social documentation, and relevant national and local authorities. PE HS Zletovica and other stakeholders will provide inputs through the PIU Coordinator to maintain a clear and consistent reporting line.

The assignment will be full-time for twelve (12) months during the GFPP-funded preparation period. The duty station will be agreed with the PIU and specified in the contract. The Specialist will be expected to work regularly from PE HS Zletovica offices and undertake travel to PIU office, project sites, communities, government institutions, and meetings elsewhere in North Macedonia as required.

The complete Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment are included in Annex 1 to this Request for Expressions of Interest and form an integral part of it.

MAFWE now invites eligible individuals ("Consultants") to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information (curriculum vitae and references in English language only) demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

  • Advanced university degree (master’s degree or equivalent) in environmental engineering, environmental or social science, ecology, civil/water engineering with a strong environmental specialization, or another directly relevant discipline.
  • Additional education or training in social impact assessment, stakeholder engagement, occupational health and safety, biodiversity, water resources, dam safety or World Bank environmental and social requirements will be an advantage.
  • At least seven (7) years of relevant professional experience in environmental and social impact assessment, environmental management, social risk management, or environmental and social supervision of infrastructure projects.
  • Demonstrated experience preparing or reviewing ESIAs, ESMPs or ESMFs, stakeholder-engagement instruments, labor-management measures, land-acquisition or resettlement instruments, and specialized environmental or social studies for complex infrastructure projects.
  • Relevant experience in the water sector—preferably involving dams, reservoirs, irrigation, hydropower, river-basin management, or water-supply infrastructure—is required.
  • Demonstrated knowledge of biodiversity and natural-habitat assessment, environmental flows, water quality, pollution prevention, climate resilience, cumulative impacts, land and livelihood risks, stakeholder engagement, labor and working conditions, and occupational and community health and safety.
  • Experience with World Bank-financed or other multilateral development bank-financed projects and good working knowledge of the World Bank ESF or a comparable framework is strongly preferred.
  • Experience integrating environmental and social requirements into designs, cost estimates, bidding documents, contracts, and supervision arrangements is required.
  • Knowledge of North Macedonia’s environmental, water, nature-protection, land, EIA, permitting, and construction-related regulatory framework is required.
  • Experience working with public institutions, public enterprises, affected communities, and multidisciplinary technical teams is required.
  • Strong analytical, review, drafting, and reporting skills, with the ability to translate environmental and social requirements into practical design, procurement, permitting, and implementation measures.
  • Excellent communication, consultation, facilitation, and coordination skills, including the ability to work effectively with government institutions, technical consultants, local authorities, workers, and affected communities.
  • Ability to manage several workstreams, meet deadlines, identify decision points, and maintain clear and auditable records.
  • Full professional proficiency in written and spoken Macedonian and English sufficient to prepare, review, and present all contractual deliverables in both languages. Knowledge of Albanian will be considered an advantage where relevant to stakeholder engagement.
  • High professional integrity, independence of judgment, respect for confidentiality and personal data, and commitment to environmental and social sustainability.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraphs 3.15, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, Seventh Edition, September 2025 ("Procurement Regulations"), setting forth the World Bank’s policies on conflict of interest and unfair competitive advantage.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – CONSULTANCY FIRM)

 

ADVANCING PUBLIC SECTOR ACCOUNTING AND FINANCIAL REPORTING IN ALBANIA (IPSAS)

 

For

 

“Communication and Training of Accounting and Audit Staff on New Requirements and Information Collection”
 

Ref. No: AL-PSA-2.1

 

ALBANIA

Project: Advancing Public Sector Accounting and Financial Reporting in Albania

TF No.: C7858

Assignment Title: “Communication and Training of Accounting and Audit Staff on New Requirements and Information Collection”

Reference No.: AL-PSA-2.1

 

The Government of the Republic of Albania has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the project “Advancing Public Sector Accounting and Financial Reporting in Albania” and intends to apply part of the proceeds to payments for goods and consulting services to be procured under this project. The project is implemented by the Ministry of Finance (MoF) of the Republic of Albania, which is responsible for the overall coordination and implementation of project activities.

 

The consulting services (“the Services”) include the design and delivery of a comprehensive, competency-based capacity-building and communication program to support the implementation of the new Public Sector Accounting (PSA) framework in Albania. The Services will include the development and delivery of IPSAS-based training programs for accounting, finance, and audit staff and experts from central government institutions, including training on public sector financial accounting and reporting, opening balances and first-time adoption, financial reporting and consolidation, PPPs and concession arrangements, borrowings, revenue, and operational system usage (AGFIS).

 

The Services will also include the preparation and validation of training needs, training curricula and schedules, training materials and e-learning content, delivery of face-to-face and live virtual training sessions, post-training webinars and targeted Q&A sessions, assessments and certification, coaching and mentoring of trainers, and the preparation of a Training Replication and Sustainability Toolkit and a Training Completion Report. The assignment will support the institutionalization and sustainability of PSA capacity-building activities, including the replication and scaling-up of training through trainers certified during the first phase of the Project.

 

The training program is expected to reach approximately 600 public sector accountants and experts from central government institutions, including staff from general government spending units, line ministries, the Treasury, debt and revenue functions, controlling units, and units with direct access to AGFIS. Participants will be organized into cohorts based on their roles, competency levels, areas of responsibility, and operational functions.

 

The training program will be delivered through a blended learning model, combining face-to-face training, live virtual instructor-led sessions, post-training webinars and targeted Q&A sessions, and on-demand e-learning modules. The program will include practical exercises, case studies, assessments, certification, and guidance to support the replication and sustainability of training within public sector institutions.

 

The assignment is expected to commence in December 2026 and continue for a period of 15 months, through March 2028.

 

The expected level of effort for the assignment is a maximum of 90 expert man-days and 130 trainer man-days spread over the implementation period.

 

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website: https://financa.gov.al/

 

The Ministry of Finance of the Republic of Albania now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

 

The shortlisting criteria are as follows. At a minimum, the firm shall meet the following requirements:

A. Qualifications of the Firm:

  1. Relevant Professional Experience:
    • At least five (5) years of proven experience in the design and delivery of training or capacitybuilding activities in accounting, financial reporting, and or public financial management.
  2. Accounting and Financial Reporting Knowledge:
    • Demonstrated experience with IFRS or IPSASbased accounting frameworks, accrual accounting reforms, or comparable accounting standards (at least 1 experience).
    • Experience supporting public sector institutions during accounting or financial reporting reforms will be considered an asset.
  3. Training Delivery Capacity
    • Proven experience in delivering structured training programs on accounting and financial reporting and related business processes, including curriculum development, preparation of training materials, and facilitation of training sessions. (at least 2 experiences during the last 5 years).
    • Experience delivering training to multiple cohorts or institutions is desirable.
  4. Knowledge Transfer:
    • Experience in designing and delivering Training of Trainers (ToT) programs or similar capacitydevelopment approaches aimed at sustainability and replication within public institutions (at least 1 experience during the last 5 years).
  5. Operational Capacity:
    • Demonstrated ability in project management which involves mobilizing qualified experts and managing logistics necessary to deliver the assignment within the proposed timeframe, evidenced by experience in at least one large-scale project involving the deployment of specialized expertise and complex logistical management.

 

The consulting firms will be assessed as follows:

 

  1. General Qualifications, including core business and years in business (30 points)
  2. Relevant experience, including previous experience in the field of assignment (60 points)
  3. Technical, managerial, and operational capacity (10 points)

 

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers: Procurement in Investment Project Financing Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services” (September 2023) (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

 

In addition, please refer to the following specific information on conflict of interest related to this assignment: in accordance with the Terms of Reference, the Consultant shall have no material interest in any of the outputs of this assignment. In addition, the Consultant shall comply with the applicable conflict of interest and confidentiality requirements under the consulting contract and shall be bound by the confidentiality arrangements agreed with the Ministry of Finance. All materials created under the Contract shall remain the sole property of the Ministry of Finance, and any re-use of such materials shall require formal written approval.

 

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

 

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Consultants’ Qualifications-based Selection (CQS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations, under a Lump-Sum Contract.

 

Expressions of interest (CV, Cover letter and documentary evidence for fulfilling the qualifications) must be delivered in a written form to the address below in person, or by mail, or by fax, or by e-mail no later than 13:00 hours (Albania local time) on 27 October 2026.

 

 

 

 

Mrs. Veronika KORKAJ, General Director

General Directorate of Financing and Contracting (GDFC)

Ministry of Finance

  1. Background

The Government of Malawi through the Ministry of Health is implementing the Malawi Health Emergency Preparedness, Response and Resilience project (MHEPRR). The project is financed by the International Development Association (IDA) and Global Financing Facility (GFF). The five-year project seeks to strengthen the capacity and resilience of Malawi’s health system to prevent, prepare for, detect and respond effectively to public health emergencies. It places particular emphasis on strengthening multisectoral coordination, surveillance, laboratory systems and other core capacities required for health emergency preparedness and response.

Laboratories across human, animal and environmental sectors are essential for surveillance, diagnostics, research and response, but often function in silos, leading to fragmented data sharing, inconsistent protocols and inefficient resource utilization. Harmonizing these laboratories strengthens collaboration, improves early detection systems, and supports evidence-based policies at national, regional and global levels.

The MHEPRR Project therefore seeks to engage a consultant to undertake a comprehensive assessment of the existing laboratory landscape and develop a strategic framework for strengthening inter-sectoral laboratory collaboration in Malawi.

  1. Objectives of the consultancy

Main objective: To develop and provide clear, actionable strategies and a framework for strengthening inter-sectoral laboratory collaboration to achieve more effective, efficient, and sustainable health outcomes in Malawi.

Specific objectives:

    • Conduct a comprehensive analysis of the current state of inter-sectoral laboratory collaboration, identifying existing mechanisms, gaps, challenges, and opportunities.
    • Engage with key stakeholders to understand their perspectives, roles, and potential contributions to collaborative One Health initiatives.
    • Develop a strategic framework that outlines different levels of collaboration in areas of communication, partnership, integration, and potential mechanisms like joint committees, policy agreements, and others.
    • Provide concrete, evidence-based recommendations and action plans for implementing a strategic framework that includes specific activities such as

 

achieving SLIPTA 3-star accreditation,               strengthening point             of entry laboratories, establishing national proficiency testing programs, etc.

  1. Scope of work
    • Conducting a situational analysis of existing diagnostic and laboratory services.
    • Identifying opportunities for test integration, economies of scale, and cost savings.
    • Proposing recommendations for policy harmonization and coordination.
    • Providing technical advice and supporting stakeholder interaction.
    • Developing strategies to integrate tier-specific testing for human, animal, and environmental health.

Specifically, the consultant will perform the following tasks:

    • Analyze existing policy documents, reports, and strategic plans related to health and development.
    • Identify and analyze the roles, interests, and potential influence of key

stakeholders from different sectors: human, environment, veterinary, plant and wild-life health.

    • Conduct in-depth interviews with senior officials and experts from relevant sectors.
    • Facilitate participatory workshops with stakeholders to build consensus and gather insights.
    • Develop a detailed report outlining the collaboration framework, strategies, and implementation plan.
    • Present the draft findings and recommendations to stakeholders for feedback and validation.
    • Deliver a final, comprehensive report incorporating all feedback and detailed action plans.
  2. Deliverables

The consultant is expected to produce the following:

    • Inception report: A document detailing the consultant's understanding of the TOR, proposed methodology, work plan, and timeline.
    • Data collection and analysis report: A report summarizing data collection findings and the stakeholder mapping of roles, interests, and influence.
    • Draft collaboration strategy: The main report presenting the harmonized strategic framework, recommendations, and action plans.

 

    • Final collaboration strategy: The final validated report, including all annexes such as interview and workshop summaries.
  2. Deliverables and Timelines

 

Deliverables

Timelines

Acceptance Criteria

Responsible

PHIM/PIU

Final Validated Collaboration Strategy

10 days after the approved draft collaboration strategy

 PHIM/PIU

 

 

 

 

  1. Consultant qualifications and experience

The consultant should possess the following:

  • An advanced degree (Master's or higher) in Laboratory Sciences, One Health, Public health, Health System Management or other health related fields.
  • Minimum of 5 years proven experience in health systems strengthening, strategic planning, and fostering multi-sectoral collaboration, preferably in a developing country context.
  • Demonstrated experience in conducting research, stakeholder engagement, and developing actionable strategies.
  • Excellent analytical, communication, and report-writing skills.
  • A strong understanding of the dynamics and challenges of inter-sectoral laboratory work.
  • Demonstrated experience in developing national or regional laboratory networks.
  • Proven ability to work with One Health approaches and integrated disease surveillance.
  • Experience in areas like disease outbreak investigation, antimicrobial resistance, or specific diagnostics is highly desirable.

 

  • Excellent technical knowledge in diagnostics, laboratory systems, biosafety and Biosecurity.
  1. Duration of the assignment

The assignment shall be completed within 120 calendar days.

 

  1. Management and supervision

The consultant will be hired under the terms of the MHEPRR Project and will be supervised by the Public Health Institute of Malawi, in collaboration with the Project implementing Unit, solely for the purpose of delivering the agreed outputs. The Ministry, as the client, shall provide the necessary support to the consultant to facilitate the execution of the assignment throughout the consultancy period. This support will include:

  • Access to relevant project documents necessary for the execution of duties under this consultancy.
  • Contact details of relevant stakeholders.

 

Regular progress updates will be required to ensure alignment with the project objectives and timelines.

 

9. SELECTION METHOD

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES - INDIVIDUAL SELECTION)

 

UNITED REPUBLIC OF TANZANIA

SUSTAINABLE RURAL WATER SUPPLY AND SANITATION PROGRAM (SRWSSP) PHASE II

 

Assignment Title: Consultancy Service for Engagement of an Individual Consultant to Provide Technical Expert Services in Water Resources Management

 

Reference No. TZ-MOWEM-576846-CS-INDV

 

The Revolutionary Government of Zanzibar (RGoZ), through the United Republic of Tanzania, has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of Sustainable Rural Water Supply and Sanitation Program (SRWSSP) Phase II and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

 

Objective of the Assignment

The overall objective of this assignment is to provide sustained technical support to the Ministry of Water, Energy and Minerals in strengthening water resources management systems in Zanzibar.

 

Specifically, the assignment aims to:

  • Improve understanding of water resources availability and utilization
  • Strengthen monitoring, data management, and decision-making systems
  • Promote sustainable and equitable allocation of water resources
  • Enhance climate resilience and environmental protection
  • Strengthen institutional capacity for effective water governance

The outputs of this assignment will be used to inform

  1. Future water resources and WASH investments in Zanzibar;
  2. strengthening of regulatory and abstraction control mechanisms;
  3. climate and drought preparedness planning; and
  4. coordination with development partners and the private sector, including utilities and major water users.

Success of the assignment will be measured by improved availability of water resources information; informed and enhanced decisionmaking on water resources allocation, planning, abstraction and protection; strengthened institutional capacity and well-aligned practices; and increased readiness to manage climate and drought risks in water resources management.

 

Specific Tasks of the Consultant

The Consultant will act as a Technical Advisor and Lead Expert, strengthening the institutional capacity of the Division of Water Resources Management by supporting analysis, providing technical guidance, undertaking capacity development endeavours and coordination, while implementation and daytoday data collection remain the responsibility of relevant institutions. The Technical Advisor shall support the Division of Water Resources Management through undertaking the following tasks:

  • Undertake capacity appraisal for the division and identify strategic areas of support
  • Conduct a comprehensive assessment of water resources, including groundwater and surface water systems.
  • Review existing policies, laws, and strategies related to water resources management.
  • Assess current water abstraction, usage patterns, and demand projections.
  • Evaluate the status of aquifers, recharge areas, and catchment zones.
  • Identify risks related to climate change, pollution, and over-extraction.
  • Develop strategies for sustainable water resources management, including conservation and protection measures.
  • Conduct consultations (physical and virtual) with experts and stakeholders at national, regional (Eastern & Southern Africa), and international levels to identify and promote best IWRM practices applicable to Zanzibar.
  • Propose mechanisms for improving water resources monitoring, data collection, and information systems.
  • Support development of regulatory and institutional frameworks for effective water governance.
  • Support Technical Assistance on drafting of new Water and Sanitation Act.
  • Prepare and present technical reports and recommendations to the Ministry.

 

The Ministry of Water, Energy and Minerals now invites eligible expert to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

 

  • At least Master’s Degree in Water Resources Engineering, Hydrology, Environmental Engineering, or related field.
  • At least 12 years of experience in undertaking Water Resources Management projects.
  • Proven experience with international donor-funded programs (World Bank, AfDB, etc.).
  • Demonstrated completion of at least three (3) comparable assignments as an individual consultant or team leader.
  • Experience in national-level assignments. Must have participated in at least 1 assignment of a similar nature in Tanzania (mainland or Zanzibar)
  • Competency in water resource management analytics (especially groundwater), capacity development, team building, policy analysis, reporting, and stakeholder engagement.
  • Registered by the relevant registration and professional boards.
  • Fluency in written and spoken English; working experience in Water Sector in Zanzibar and knowledge of Kiswahili is a strong advantage.

 

The attention of interested consulting firms is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers”, Seventh Edition, September 2025, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. Consulting firms intending to submit an Expression of Interest shall not have any conflict of interest or unfair competitive advantage and must comply with the provisions of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations.

 

The Consultant will be selected in accordance with the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, Seventh Edition, September 2025, using the Individual Consultant Selection method through an open national competitive process.

1. Background

The Government of the Republic of South Sudan (GRSS), through the Ministry of Water Resources and Irrigation (MWRI), is implementing the Regional Climate Resilience Program (RCRP) and preparing the National WASH Project (NWP) with financing from the International Development Association (IDA) of the World Bank.

 

The Projects aim to strengthen climate resilience, improve water resources management, and expand access to safe drinking water, sanitation, and hygiene services. To support effective implementation of both Projects, the MWRI intends to engage qualified personnel within the Project Implementation Unit (PIU). The Government of Indonesia (GOI), in collaboration with the World Bank, is implementing the Local Service Delivery Improvement Project (LSDP), which aims to improve local government (LG) performance through Performance-Based Grants (PBGs). Under the PBG mechanism, grants are provided based on the achievement of agreed policy and service delivery targets. The performance of participating LGs will be monitored and verified by the Central Project Management Unit (CPMU), with support from an Independent Verification Agent (IVA). The consulting services (“the Services”) will focus on verifying the baseline and performance of each participating LG against the agreed Minimum Conditions and Performance Indicators and calculate the proposed amount of Annual allocation and Performance allocation based on the indicators verified. The duration of project task implementation is estimated to be 48 (fourty eight) months and the location of task implementation is located in Jakarta and across designated regions.  Detailed TOR is attached in the REOI. The Ministry of Home Affairs, Directorate General of Regional Development now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the services. REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST
