LOWLANDS LIVELIHOOD RESILIENCE PROJECT – PHASE II (LLRP-II)

Credit No.: 7519-ET

Assignment Title: Consultancy Services for Route Selection and Survey, Feasibility Study, Detailed Engineering Design, ESIA and Tender Document Preparation of Two (2) Gravel Roads: Gereni – Dubti Woreda and Abida – Gelealu Woreda Gravel Road Projects, Afar Region

Reference No.: ET-AFR-RPCU-569662-CS-QCBS

The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Lowlands Livelihood Resilience Project – Phase II (LLRP-II), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include route selection and survey, feasibility study, detailed engineering design, Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) and preparation of tender documents for two (2) gravel roads in Afar Region: (i) Gereni – Dubti Woreda Gravel Road, approximately 85 km, in Zones 01 and 06; and (ii) Abida – Gelealu Woreda Gravel Road, approximately 30 km, in Zone 03.

The Services will be carried out in two phases, following the latest Ethiopian Roads Administration (ERA) design manuals and quality manual, the LLRP-II environmental and social instruments and the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF):

 

(a)  Phase I – Route Selection and Survey, and Feasibility Study: identification and multi-criteria comparison of at least three alternative routes; site reconnaissance and investigation; stakeholder consultation; traffic counts and axle load surveys; full topographic survey and Digital Terrain Model; preliminary design; ESIA of the selected route; preliminary cost estimates; economic evaluation; and climate and natural hazard vulnerability assessment.

(b) Phase II – Detailed Engineering Design, ESIA and Preparation of Bidding Documents: materials and site investigation; geometric, drainage, pavement, geotechnical and bridge/structural design, including an independent bridge design check; road safety design and audit; utilities and private accesses; estimate of the construction contract period; final ESIA and Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP); and preparation of bidding documents based on the World Bank Standard Procurement Documents, including technical specifications, drawings, bills of quantities and the Engineer’s cost estimate.

The implementation period is three (3) months from the date of commencement, and the assignment is expected to start in December 2026.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained at the address given below.

The Afar National Regional State, Office of the President, Lowlands Livelihood Resilience Project (LLRP-II) Regional Project Coordination Unit now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. (a)  Core business and years in business: the firm’s core business shall be in road/highway engineering consultancy services. Provide the company profile, certificate of registration and number of years in business.

(b) General experience: experience in civil engineering consultancy services (studies, design and/or construction supervision of roads, bridges or other civil infrastructure) during the last ten (10) years.

(c)  Specific experience: experience in assignments of similar nature and complexity, i.e. feasibility studies and detailed engineering design of roads (new construction, rehabilitation or upgrading, including gravel/low-volume roads), covering route selection, topographic surveys, drainage and bridge structures, ESIA and preparation of bidding documents, preferably in arid, semi-arid or lowland areas and under projects financed by the World Bank or other international development partners. (d) Technical and managerial capability of the firm: organizational structure, survey equipment (e.g. GPS and total stations), access to soil and materials testing laboratories, road design and economic evaluation software, quality assurance systems, and capacity to mobilize multidisciplinary field teams to remote areas of Afar Region.

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

Country: KENYA

Name of Project: NATIONAL YOUTH OPPORTUNITIES TOWARDS ADVANCEMENT (NYOTA)

Credit No. IDA-7355-KE/ Grant No: E210-KE

Assignment Title: Consultancy Services for the Provision of Monitoring and Verification Firm for NYOTA Project

 

The Government of Kenya, with financing from the World Bank, invites eligible consulting firms to submit Expressions of Interest (EOI) for the assignment indicated above under the National Youth Opportunities Towards Advancement (NYOTA) Project.

The NYOTA Project aims to increase employment and earnings and promote savings for targeted youth at national scale. The Project is expected to reach 820,000 vulnerable youth across all 47 counties of Kenya, including refugees in Garissa and Turkana counties. The Project beneficiaries are youth aged 18-29 years, and up to 35 years for persons with disabilities, with little or no education, who are unemployed or in vulnerable employment.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include independent monitoring and verification of results reported by Employer Organizations and other Service Providers under the NYOTA On-the-Job Experience (OJE) results-based financing arrangement. The assignment will cover verification of placement into apprenticeship, retention during apprenticeship, and retention in paid employment after apprenticeship, including review of Project system records, administrative data, remote verification, field verification, spot checks, evidence logs, and payment eligibility summaries. For clarity, the results-based financing milestones to be verified are: Milestone 1: placement into apprenticeship; Milestone 2: retention in apprenticeship for five months; and Milestone 3: retention in paid employment for six months after apprenticeship. These are referred to in the TOR as M1, M2 and M3 verification cycles, respectively. The estimated beneficiary population from which verification claims may arise is 90,000, with geographic coverage across the 47 counties.

The initial contract period shall be twelve (12) months. The contract may be renewed in twelve-month periods, subject to satisfactory performance against agreed deliverables, continued need for the services, availability of funds, and compliance with quality and timeliness requirements. The contract shall not extend beyond the Project closing date of 31st December 2028, unless that date is formally extended and the Contract is amended in accordance with the applicable procurement and contract provisions.

Interested firms should provide information and proof demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The shortlisting criteria are:

a) Demonstrated seven (7) years' experience in independent verification, results-based financing, performance audit, monitoring and evaluation, social protection, labour market, skills development, youth employment, or other large-scale beneficiary programmes, preferably including experience in sub-Saharan Africa;

b) Proven track record of having undertaken at least two (2) assignments of a similar nature and complexity in the last five (5) years, including verification of results, payment-linked outputs, or large beneficiary datasets;

c) A consultancy profile that includes the organizational structure, clearly stating the duties assigned to each of the personnel identified to support the delivery of verification, measurement and reporting;

d) Demonstrated technical and managerial capability to deliver the assignment.

Note: Key experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The attention of interested consulting firms is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank's "Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers" dated July 2016 and revised in September 2025 (6th Edition) ("Procurement Regulations"), setting forth the World Bank's policy on conflict of interest. In addition, consulting firms shall not be hired for any assignment that would be in conflict with their prior or current obligations to other clients, or that may place them in a position of being unable to carry out the assignment in the best interests of the Borrower.

Consultants may submit their REOI as an individual firm or in association in the form of a joint venture or sub-consultancy. All the members of the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire assignment. However, the experience of sub-consultant will not be considered while short-listing.

A Consultant/firm will be selected in accordance with Quality Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the World Bank Regulations.

Interested firms may obtain further information from the Project Supply Chain Management Office at NYOTA offices, Bruce House, Standard Street, 3rd Floor Northern Wing Room No. 321 during official working hours (8.00 a.m-5.00 p.m.) and days. Complete REOI document (paginated and stamped/signed on each page) and enclosed in plain sealed envelope marked with the tender reference number and addressed to the Principal Secretary, State Department of Youth Affairs and Creative Economy, P. O. Box 34303 –00100, Nairobi, Kenya and should be deposited in the Tender Box at Bruce House 3rd Floor to be received on or before 29th October, 2026, at 10.00 hours

The REOIs will be closed/opened immediately thereafter at the NYOTA Boardroom, Bruce House, 3rd Floor Standard Street Nairobi.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (REOI)

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

 

Country:                    Federal Republic of Somalia

Name of Project:       Eastern Africa Regional Digital Integration Project (EA-RDIP)   

Project ID:                 P176181    

Assignment Title:      Design, Deployment and Operationalization of the Government API Gateway, Government Single Sign-On (SSO) and National Digital Government Portal

Reference No.:           SO-MOCT-FGS-576851-CS-QCBS

Place Of Assignment: Mogadishu, Somalia

Submission Date:      October 29, 2026, 2.00pm (local time, Mogadishu, Somalia)

The Federal Republic of Somalia has received a grant from the International Development Association (IDA) of the World Bank toward the cost of the Eastern Africa Regional Digital Integration Project (EA-RDIP), and the Ministry of Communications and Technology intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“Services”) are required to be undertaken by an external consulting firm supporting the client, the Ministry of Communications and Technology (MoCT), FGS, through its E-Government Department, to carry out the “Design, Deployment and Operationalization of the Government API Gateway, Government Single Sign-On (SSO) and National Digital Government Portal”. The assignment aims to design, deploy, commission and operationalize the first production phase of Somalia’s shared digital government platforms, translating the Government Enterprise Architecture (GEA), the Government Interoperability Framework (GIF) and the standards developed under Package 1 into operational digital infrastructure. The scope includes: (i) a production-grade Government API Gateway and Developer Portal for secure API publishing, discovery, access, monitoring and lifecycle management; (ii) a centralized Identity and Access Management (IAM) and Government Single Sign-On (SSO) platform based on open standards (OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect and SAML), including multi-factor authentication and role-based access control; (iii) development of integration connectors and onboarding of at least two (2) priority government services/systems; (iv) a responsive, mobile-first, accessible and multilingual (Somali, Arabic and English) National Digital Government Portal serving as a common digital front door for citizens and businesses; and (v) operational, security, monitoring, backup and disaster-recovery arrangements, a minimum six-month post-Go-Live stabilization period, hands-on capacity building and full handover of source code, configurations and documentation to MoCT. The solution will be hosted in the Government National Data Center. The consultant firm will undertake all the specific tasks detailed in the Terms of Reference (ToR). The assignment is expected to be completed within approximately fourteen (14) months from the date of contract effectiveness.

Terms of Reference (ToR) can be found at the following website: https://moct.gov.so/en/jobs/  or it can be provided upon submission of application in person or by e-mail. The e-mail address is provided below.

The Ministry of Communications and Technology now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services (brochures, description of similar assignments, experience in similar conditions, availability of appropriate skills among staff, etc.).

The short-listing criteria are as follows:

  1. Core business of the firm and at least eight (8) years of relevant organizational experience in software development, enterprise software platforms, systems integration, interoperability, digital government or closely related implementation work, with evidence of the company registration certificate, business license or operational permit, and a company profile indicating services offered and years in operation.
  2. The firm should demonstrate successful completion of at least three (3) comparable assignments, including at least one (1) live production implementation involving API management/interoperability and at least one (1) involving Identity and Access Management (IAM)/Single Sign-On (SSO) or identity federation. In addition, also demonstrated experience deploying and supporting enterprise or government digital platforms in production environments, including API gateways, developer portals, IAM/federation, connector development, citizen-facing portals and DevOps/cloud or hybrid infrastructure, as well as cybersecurity, privacy, high-availability, monitoring, backup and disaster-recovery capability, is required. These may be demonstrated within the same assignment. For each assignment, firms should indicate the client, contract value, duration, scope of services and the firm’s role.
  3. Demonstrate experience of relevant services implemented in Somalia, or in Africa region, government, fragile/conflict-affected or comparable institutional environments similar to that of Somalia; and
  4. The technical and managerial organization of the firm, and evidence of adequate financial, technical and staffing capacity to complete and stabilize the assignment. (Provide only the structure of the firm’s organization.) Do not provide CVs of staff. Key experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers: Procurement in Investment Financing - Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services dated July 2016 and revised in November 2017, August 2018, November 2020 and September 2023, (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a Joint venture and/ or a Sub consultancy. In case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. 

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

SOLICITUD DE EXPRESIONES DE INTERÉS SERVICIOS DE CONSULTORÍA

República Dominicana

Proyecto de Respuesta a Emergencias y Resiliencia de la República Dominicana

Préstamo No.: 9473-DO

Título del Trabajo: Comunicación Estratégica – Contratación de Firma para Servicios de Consultoría.

No. de Referencia: DO-MEPYD-531293-CS-QCBS

Fecha de publicación: 9 de octubre de 2026

 

El Gobierno de la República Dominicana ha recibido financiamiento del Banco Mundial para cubrir el costo del Proyecto de Respuesta a Emergencias y Resiliencia de la República Dominicana a través del Ministerio de la Presidencia y tiene la intención de aplicar parte de los fondos a la contratación de servicios de consultoría.

Los servicios de consultoría ("los Servicios") comprenden el diseño, implementación y ajuste continuo de una estrategia integral de comunicación para el Proyecto de Respuesta a Emergencias y Resiliencia de la República Dominicana (P180163), bajo la rectoría del Ministerio de la Presidencia (MINPRE) y en coordinación con la Unidad Ejecutora del Proyecto (UEP) y las entidades involucradas. La consultoría deberá facilitar la comprensión y apropiación de los objetivos, procesos, instrumentos y resultados del Proyecto; fortalecer la coherencia de los mensajes y las vocerías institucionales; apoyar la articulación entre el nivel nacional, sectorial y territorial; gestionar riesgos comunicacionales y escenarios sensibles; y contribuir a la adopción y uso institucional de los productos generados por el Proyecto.

El alcance se estructura en cinco líneas de trabajo complementarias: (i) diagnóstico comunicacional; (ii) diseño estratégico; (iii) implementación de la estrategia; (iv) acompañamiento institucional y territorial; y (v) monitoreo y ajuste adaptativo. Incluye, entre otros aspectos, el análisis y priorización de actores y públicos; el diseño de la Estrategia Integral y Plan de Comunicación Estratégica segmentado por públicos prioritarios, líneas, canales, formatos, frecuencia y momentos; narrativa, mensajes clave, argumentarios y fortalecimiento de vocerías; estrategia de divulgación y posicionamiento; gestión de asuntos sensibles y riesgos comunicacionales; producción de materiales y contenidos; acompañamiento a procesos territoriales; acciones para facilitar la adopción, uso institucional y sostenibilidad de instrumentos como PNOT, PRODT, PMOT, SNIT, información y cartografía geoespacial y herramientas de gestión del riesgo; diseño o fortalecimiento del portal web del Proyecto; y seguimiento mediante indicadores de alcance, interacción, comprensión, participación y apropiación. Los Servicios tendrán una duración de doce (12) meses calendario consecutivos. Esta descripción es de carácter general; el detalle del alcance, actividades, productos y condiciones se encuentra en los Términos de Referencia (TDR).

El Ministerio de la Presidencia ahora invita a las firmas consultoras elegibles ("Consultores") a indicar su interés en proporcionar los Servicios. Los Consultores interesados deben proporcionar información que demuestre que tienen las calificaciones requeridas y la experiencia relevante para prestar los Servicios. Los criterios de preselección son:

 

  • Actividad principal, experiencia y trayectoria de la firma. La firma consultora deberá acreditar al menos diez (10) años de experiencia comprobable en comunicación estratégica, comunicación pública o comunicación para el desarrollo, y haber ejecutado satisfactoriamente al menos cinco (5) proyectos de comunicación estratégica para instituciones públicas, programas nacionales o proyectos de desarrollo, de alcance y complejidad comparables, ejecutados en los últimos diez (10) años. Deberá evidenciar experiencia en contextos institucionales complejos que involucren múltiples actores, procesos de toma de decisión, coordinación entre niveles de gobierno, producción de materiales comunicacionales de alto nivel, gestión adaptativa y escenarios de alta exposición institucional o sensibilidad pública.
  • Experiencia específica y comparabilidad de proyectos. La firma deberá acreditar, como mínimo, la ejecución satisfactoria de al menos un (1) proyecto de alcance nacional que haya involucrado coordinación con gobierno, gobiernos locales y entidades sectoriales, demostrando capacidad para operar simultáneamente en los niveles nacional y territorial. En conjunto, las experiencias presentadas deberán evidenciar de manera verificable: (i) diseño e implementación de estrategias de comunicación vinculadas a políticas públicas, programas gubernamentales o iniciativas de desarrollo; (ii) articulación interinstitucional y gestión de actores en contextos multinivel; (iii) fortalecimiento de vocerías y elaboración de insumos estratégicos para tomadores de decisiones; (iv) gestión de riesgos comunicacionales y de escenarios sensibles o de alta exposición; (v) traducción de contenidos técnicos complejos en mensajes claros y accionables para autoridades, actores territoriales y ciudadanía; y (vi) diseño, implementación o fortalecimiento de plataformas digitales o portales institucionales. Se valorará especialmente la experiencia vinculada a ordenamiento territorial, gestión del riesgo de desastres, cambio climático, planificación territorial, infraestructura o desarrollo sostenible, así como la experiencia previa en proyectos financiados por el Banco Mundial, organismos equivalentes o con el Gobierno de la República Dominicana.
  • Capacidad técnica, organizativa y operativa. La firma deberá demostrar capacidad para ejecutar de manera continua una consultoría de alcance nacional y territorial durante doce (12) meses, incluyendo infraestructura propia o asociada para diseño gráfico, producción digital y gestión de plataformas web; recursos computacionales suficientes; y sistemas internos de gestión de proyectos y control de calidad que aseguren planificación, seguimiento oportuno, consistencia técnica de los productos y capacidad de iniciar oportunamente la ejecución.

 

  • Correspondencia con el alcance de la consultoría. La correspondencia será valorada mediante el análisis integrado de la experiencia y capacidades institucionales acreditadas frente a la escala y complejidad de los Servicios. Para ser considerada comparable, la experiencia deberá evidenciar funciones sustantivas de comunicación estratégica relacionadas con varios de los siguientes ámbitos: diagnóstico y segmentación de públicos; diseño e implementación de planes de comunicación; gestión de actores y articulación multinivel; posicionamiento institucional; fortalecimiento de vocerías; gestión de riesgos y asuntos sensibles; producción de insumos estratégicos para toma de decisiones; comunicación territorial; gestión de canales y plataformas digitales; y monitoreo de resultados y apropiación. Se considerará particularmente relevante la capacidad demostrada para transformar información técnica compleja en contenidos utilizables en procesos institucionales, territoriales y de política pública.

Los Servicios se prestarán en modalidad combinada de gabinete y actividades presenciales, incluyendo desplazamientos a los territorios cuando corresponda. La firma deberá tener capacidad para trabajar simultáneamente en los niveles nacional y municipal y para coordinar de forma continua con el MINPRE, el VIOTDR, la UEP, entidades sectoriales y gobiernos locales. Los productos contractuales serán preparados en idioma español e inglés, conforme a los TDR.

Nota: Los Expertos Clave no serán evaluados en la etapa de preselección y no deberán presentarse CV en esta etapa.

Para estos fines, la firma consultora deberá remitir la documentación de forma clara, estructurada, verificable y directamente vinculada con los criterios de preselección establecidos en la presente Solicitud de Expresiones de Interés (SEI). El documento principal no deberá exceder de cuarenta (40) páginas. Los documentos legales y los soportes documentales presentados para acreditar la experiencia y capacidad declaradas no se computarán dentro de este límite y deberán incorporarse como anexos debidamente identificados, paginados y referenciados. La documentación técnica de soporte no deberá exceder de ciento cincuenta (150) páginas para una firma consultora individual. En caso de APCA, consorcio, joint venture o asociación equivalente, el límite será de ciento cincuenta (150) páginas por cada integrante que acredite experiencia o capacidad relevante para los criterios de preselección. El registro mercantil, la nómina de accionistas y los documentos legales equivalentes no se computarán dentro de estos límites de páginas.

 

La documentación requerida es la siguiente:

  • Carta de expresión de interés, con datos generales de la firma consultora (firmada y sellada).
  • Detalle de la experiencia directa de la firma consultora donde se evidencie: actividad principal y años de experiencia; experiencia general y específica; y correspondencia con los criterios indicados. Para cada experiencia declarada deberá indicarse, como mínimo, el nombre del contrato o proyecto, cliente y país, fechas de ejecución, monto contractual, alcance y objetivos, rol desempeñado por la firma o integrante de la APCA, productos o actividades efectivamente ejecutados, ámbito institucional y territorial, actores o niveles de gobierno involucrados, componentes de comunicación estratégica desarrollados, criterio o criterios de preselección que acredita y referencia exacta del soporte documental presentado.
  • Estructura organizativa general de la Firma Consultora o APCA, con una breve descripción de sus áreas técnicas, capacidades institucionales, recursos permanentes, infraestructura para diseño gráfico, producción digital y gestión web, recursos computacionales y sistemas internos de gestión de proyectos y control de calidad relevantes para la consultoría. En esta etapa no deberán presentarse CV ni se evaluarán las calificaciones de expertos individuales.
  • Descripción de la capacidad organizativa y operativa para iniciar oportunamente la consultoría y operar de manera simultánea en los niveles nacional y territorial, incluyendo los mecanismos previstos para coordinación, seguimiento, aseguramiento de calidad y cumplimiento de plazos.
  • Registro mercantil actualizado o equivalente en su país de origen.
  • Nómina de accionistas o documento equivalente en su país de origen.

Nota: Toda la documentación que se presente deberá estar en idioma español.

La lista corta estará integrada por un mínimo de cinco (5) y un máximo de ocho (8) firmas consultoras.

Se llama la atención de los Consultores interesados sobre la Sección III, párrafos 3.14, 3.16 y 3.17 de las “Regulaciones de Adquisiciones para Prestatarios en Proyectos de Inversión del Banco Mundial”, actualizadas a noviembre de 2020 (“Regulaciones de Adquisiciones”), en las que se establece la política del Banco Mundial sobre conflictos de intereses.

 

Los Consultores podrán asociarse con otras firmas para mejorar sus calificaciones y deberán indicar claramente si la asociación se presenta como APCA (joint venture, consorcio o asociación equivalente) o como subconsultoría. En caso de APCA, todos sus integrantes serán conjunta y solidariamente responsables de la totalidad del contrato, si resultan seleccionados.

Se puede obtener más información durante el horario de oficina de 08:00 a 16:00 horas, en las oficinas de este Viceministerio ubicadas en la calle César Nicolás Penson núm. 48, Distrito Nacional, Santo Domingo, República Dominicana, o mediante comunicación escrita dirigida al correo electrónico adquisicioneseyr@minpre.gob.do.

Los TDR podrán solicitarse, sin costo, mediante comunicación dirigida al correo electrónico antes indicado, haciendo constar en el asunto la referencia del proceso, o descargarse desde el enlace correspondiente a este proceso, publicado en el Portal de Transparencia del Ministerio de la Presidencia: https://minpre.gob.do/transparencia/proyecto-de-respuesta-a-emergencias-y-resiliencia-de-la-republica-dominicana/.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT)

ALBANIA

BUILDING RESILIENT BRIDGES PROJECT (BRBP)

Project ID.: P174595

Loan No.:  94790-AL

Assignment Title: PIT- Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) Specialist  

Reference No. AL-ARA-415789-CS-INDV

Recruitment Type: Local Recruitment

The Government of Albania has received a loan in the amount of 51.6 million EUR financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Building Resilient Bridges Project (BRBP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for individual consulting services under this Request for Expressions of Interest (REoI).  

The Albanian Road Authority (ARA), as the implementing agency of the Project, now invites eligible individual consultants to indicate their interest in providing the services described below.

The consulting services include the provision of services as an Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) Specialist as an integral member of the Project Implementation Team (PIT) established within the ARA for implementation of the BRBP. The OHS Specialist will provide specialized technical expertise and support to the PIT in the planning, implementation, monitoring and reporting of occupational health and safety requirements associated with the rehabilitation and reconstruction of bridges and associated infrastructure under the Project. The Consultant will be responsible for monitoring and assessing occupational health and safety risks and hazards at Project sites and ensuring that Project activities are implemented in compliance with applicable Albanian legislation and regulations, relevant World Bank requirements, Environmental, Health and Safety Guidelines, good international industry practice, and applicable Project environmental and social instruments and contractual requirements.

The assignment is expected to be carried out on a full-time basis, with the Consultant based at the ARA/PIT office in Tirana and undertaking frequent visits to Project construction sites as required. The initial duration of the assignment is twelve (12) months from contract signing and/or entry into force of the contract, subject to a three (3)-month probation period. Subject to satisfactory performance, the contract may be renewed for the duration of the Program or for such other period as may subsequently be agreed in writing by the parties. 

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website https://www.arrsh.gov.al/njoftime-brbp

Interested Candidates should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and be able to demonstrate previous experience as follows:

  • University degree in Civil Engineering or related field
  • Certified qualification in construction safety (e.g., NEBOSH, IOSH, or national equivalent).
  • A minimum of five (5) years of relevant working experience as a Health and Safety Specialist in infrastructure projects / programmes, in transport sector, preferably in bridge and/or road projects;
  • Proven experience in construction safety management, including bridge or road works, with demonstrated knowledge of ESHS risk control, traffic management, and SEA/SH awareness training;
  • Working knowledge of local and international health and safety standards and risk management;
  • Specific work experience with projects financed, in whole or in part, by the World Bank or other international financial institutions/donors;
  • A minimum of three (3) years of relevant working experience as an engineer in infrastructure sector. Previous experience in projects financed by the World Bank or other international financial institutions, would be considered an advantage;
  • The candidate must be computer literate, with proficiency in computer software operations (AutoCAD, Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, etc.);
  • Reliable, independent, and dynamic worker with high social competency and good team spirit
  • Excellent knowledge in presentation, communication and writing of English and Albanian language (in speaking and writing).

Applicants who meet the minimum qualification requirements will be evaluated based on the following criteria:

  1. General Qualifications – 30 points
  2. Adequacy for the Assignment – 60 points
  3. Language – 10 points

The interested candidates will be selected in accordance with the Open Competitive Selection of Individual Consultants method set out in the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, November 2020.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL SELECTION)

Country:   Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia

Name of Project: Eastern Africa Regional Digital Integration Project (EARDIP)

Project ID: P180931

Assignment Title: Recruitment of 3(Three) Senior Full-Stack Software Engineers for Optimization of Ethiopian eServices Platform.

Reference No.: ET-MINT-570555-CS-INDV

  1. Background

The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Easter Africa Regional Digital Integration Project (EARDIP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for the services of hiring qualified and experienced professionals to work as part of the Project Implementation Unit (PIU) for Easter Africa Regional Digital Integration Project established under Ministry of Innovation and Technology (MInT). MInT want to hire qualified and experienced enior Full-Stack Software Engineers for Optimization of Ethiopian eServices Platform.

2. Objective

The overarching objective of this consultancy assignment is to source, embed, and utilize top-tier technical professionals to ensure the successful delivery, scaling, and maintenance of national e-Government services and their associated public infrastructure modules. In alignment with the current national digital strategy, Digital Ethiopia 2030, these experts will spearhead the modernization of public service delivery by strictly adhering to international digital government benchmarks. This includes the systematic implementation of mobile and API-first architectures, cloud-native approaches, open-source technologies, and deep interoperability frameworks rooted in user-centered service design.

3. Main Responsibilities

The Senior Full-Stack Software Engineers will take complete technical ownership of the engineering lifecycle governing the nation's e-Government platforms. They will lead active coding sprints, define microservice patterns, manage versioning branches, and ensure the absolute operational continuity of public-facing live systems.

Their detailed responsibilities include:

3.1.1 Defining Optimization and Establishing a Baseline

  • Conduct Current-State Assessments: Perform an initial assessment of the existing platform to establish an architectural baseline and build a unified consensus with MInT on optimization priorities before prescribing future modernizations.  
  • Formulate a Quantifiable KPI Framework: Support MInT in defining and formalizing and defining the optimization of KPIs through a clear taxonomy, setting precise data sources and evaluation frequencies to transform broad optimization goals into measurable technical metrics.
  • Collaborate, Define, and Track Key Indicators: Collaborate with MInT stakeholders to establish baseline performance metrics and directly define, implement, and track key platform optimization indicators—including transaction processing times, online application completion rates, system availability, and transaction success rates.
  • Embed Institutional Sustainability and Knowledge Transfer: Integrate structured mentoring, paired-working arrangements, and continuous knowledge sharing into daily baseline activities to prepare MInT technical staff for long-term platform ownership.

Concrete Deliverable: Knowledge Transfer and Institutional Sustainability Package

To ensure knowledge transfer is a defined, measurable output rather than a generalized activity, the following tangible assets must be delivered:

  • Technical Training Artifacts & Delivery: Development and execution of practical technical training sessions for MInT developers and operational staff, accompanied by training materials, code walkthroughs, and recorded sessions covering system architecture, deployment environments, and operational workflows.
  • Comprehensive System Documentation Suite: Delivery of an up-to-date, centralized technical repository containing architecture diagrams, database schemas, API specifications, automated deployment procedures, configuration maps, troubleshooting guides, and operational runbooks.
  • Structured Mentoring & Competency Log: Implementation of a paired-programming and co-engineering schedule with designated MInT technical counterparts, validated by a brief competency sign-off log documenting the shared handling of system tasks.
  • Formal Platform Handover & Control Transfer: A verified handover package ensuring that all source code, deployment artifacts, infrastructure configurations, and administrative access controls are fully transferred to, and natively managed under, MInT's exclusive infrastructure control.

3.1.2 Full-Stack Architectural Design and Feature Development

  • Lead the comprehensive end-to-end design, system modeling, backend programming, and frontend user-interface construction of new modules within transactional e-Government applications.
  • Develop modular, reusable, and testable components, ensuring strict separation of concerns and adherence to international clean-coding standards.
  • Provide technical support, routine maintenance, and immediate bug-fixing for existing live public-facing platforms to ensure zero service disruption.
  • Construct dynamic, cross-browser compatible, and mobile-responsive frontend user experiences that match modern public design systems.
  • Design and execute highly efficient database schemas, indexing strategies, and raw query optimizations for complex enterprise relational and non-relational storage layers.
  • Optimize application performance, scalability, and code quality while ensuring integration with national digital ID and payment gateways.

3.1.3 Foundational National System Integrations

  • Architect and program secure, low-latency RESTful and gRPC API channels to connect e-Government applications directly with the national single sign-on (SSO) and the Fayda National Digital ID ecosystem.
  • Integrate multi-channel fintech infrastructures into the core, allowing real-time, verified payment processing across commercial banks, electronic wallets, and state-backed payment clearings.
  • Implement secure data exchange protocols (including tokenization and cryptographic signing) to safely transmit cross-ministry records without compromising data integrity or privacy.

3.1.4 Platform Maintenance, Optimization, and Zero-Disruption Support

  • Take immediate accountability for the active, live production environment of public e-services, minimizing downtime through preventative server-side optimization and resource scaling.
  • Provide immediate, tier-3 diagnostic support and rapid bug-fixing routines for errors identified by public citizens, civil servants, or automated monitoring frameworks.
  • Implement containerization technologies (e.g., Docker) and orchestrate deployments via Kubernetes clusters to support zero-downtime rolling upgrades and automatic failure recoveries.
  • Configure automated application performance management (APM) systems and centralized logging pipelines to track error conditions and system bottlenecks in real-time.

3.1.5 Code Quality, Governance, and Sustainable Knowledge Transfer

  • To guarantee long-term state capacity and institutional sustainability, the consultancy team shall treat knowledge transfer not merely as an ongoing activity, but as a defined, verifiable project output. The consultants shall establish strict engineering governance and execute the following structured mandates:
  • Rigorous Peer Review & Branch Governance: Establish and enforce rigorous peer code review processes, requiring all engineering branch merges to satisfy strict security protocols, comprehensive test coverage baselines, and mandatory documentation updates before production deployment.
  • Comprehensive System Documentation & Runbooks: Draft, maintain, and publish complete technical system documentation under version control. This must include comprehensive architecture diagrams, database schemas, interactive API specifications (e.g., Swagger/OpenAPI), deployment configurations, troubleshooting guides, and step-by-step operational runbooks.
  • Practical Technical Training Sessions: Develop and deliver practical, structured technical training sessions and deep-dive code walkthroughs for MInT developers and designated technical staff. Training must thoroughly cover the optimized application architecture, the core codebase, cloud deployment environments, and daily operational procedures.
  • Structured Counterpart Mentoring: Establish a practical, daily mentoring and paired-working arrangement with designated MInT technical counterparts throughout the duration of the assignment to systematically build internal engineering capabilities.
  • Absolute Handover & MInT Control: Execute a formal, documented handover process ensuring that all source code repositories, deployment artifacts, technical documentation, configuration keys, and operational knowledge are fully transferred to, verified by, and maintained under MInT’s absolute institutional control.

4. Required Technical Competencies and Experience

4.1 Senior Full-Stack Software Engineer Profiles (Core Team Structure)

Candidates submitted for evaluation under these profiles must explicitly demonstrate a mature engineering pedigree, characterized by a history of shipping scalable, secure, and production-proven web applications. Rather than maintaining uniform generalist responsibilities, the consultancy team shall be deployed across three distinct areas of deeper technical focus while sharing a unified engineering core.

4.1.1 The Cross-Functional Collaboration Framework (Explicit Relationships)

To ensure the elimination of traditional development silos, all three engineering profiles must execute tight, continuous synchronization with separate Business Analyst and UX/UI design functions through the following defined responsibilities:

  • Requirement Translation: Collaborate closely with external UX/UI designers and Business Analysts to seamlessly translate citizen, business, and government user requirements into scalable, secure technical solutions.
  • Iterative Usability Optimization: Actively participate in iterative usability testing cycles and systematically incorporate user feedback into platform and service code improvements.
  • Pre-Automation Process Simplification: Partner directly with Senior Business Analysts to map administrative government workflows, transform complex functional rules into clean technical requirements, and support process simplification before writing automated code.

4.1.2 Professional Experience

  • Continuous Pedigree: A minimum of five (5) years of continuous, verifiable, and direct hands-on professional software development experience within production-grade environments.
  • Domain Relevance: Demonstrated experience working on large-scale web systems, public e-Government engines, or comparable high-volume transactional environments (such as core banking, digital payment switches, fintech networks, or telecommunications platforms).
  • Targeted Implementation Expertise: Candidates must explicitly demonstrate a mature, production-proven background across the following operational domains directly relevant to this assignment:
    • High-Availability Systems: Designing, scaling, and maintaining large-scale, fault-tolerant production systems with a history of ensuring continuous service reliability under high concurrency.
    • Legacy Modernization: Modernizing, refactoring, and decomposing legacy, monolithic software architectures into cloud-native microservices or modular frameworks.
    • API and Systems Integration: Orchestrating advanced API design and deep systems integration frameworks over diverse, heterogeneous data environments.
    • Database Engineering: Executing advanced database design, data modeling, index tuning, caching mechanisms, and rigorous query performance optimization.
    • Modern DevSecOps: Managing automated CI/CD code delivery pipelines, Docker/Kubernetes containerization, infrastructure-as-code, and live production deployments.
    • Secure Development Lifecycle: Implementing secure software development workflows, defensive coding patterns, payload encryption, and strict protection against vulnerabilities.
    • Localization & Multilingual Support: Building accessible application layers that natively support localization configurations, localized time/date formats, and multilingual engines (including Amharic script processing).
    • Production Platform Support: Active troubleshooting, root-cause anomaly analysis, log monitoring, and engineering support for active production environments.
    • Technical Governance: Compiling comprehensive technical documentation, conducting rigorous peer code reviews, and mentoring junior developers to foster engineering growth.

4.1.3 Position 1: Senior Full-Stack Engineer – Backend &    Systems Integration

A. Position Focus

This position serves as the core systems and backend architect of the sprint team, taking primary ownership of business logic execution, heavy data orchestration, and deep ecosystem integrations (e.g., Fayda National ID and central payment rails).

B. Targeted Technical Competencies

  • Advanced Backend Frameworks: Expert-level mastery building enterprise engines using Java (Spring Boot, Spring Security), asynchronous Node.js microservices, or Python (Django, FastAPI) with deep ORM tuning.
  • Database & Query Optimization: Verifiable experience configuring, indexing, and performance-tuning high-throughput relational engines (PostgreSQL, MySQL) and unstructured data layers (MongoDB).
  • High-Throughput Interoperability: Complete clarity constructing, securing, and orchestrating distributed RESTful, GraphQL, and gRPC endpoints across diverse legacy agency backends.

4.1.4 Position 2: Senior Full-Stack Engineer – Frontend & User Experience

A. Position Focus

This position bridges user requirements and hard engineering under the assumption of a separate UX/UI function. This engineer takes primary ownership of translating design mockups into high-performance, responsive code, focusing heavily on accessibility, multi-language support, and deployment across resource-constrained client devices.

B. Targeted Technical Competencies

  • Modern Frontend Architectures: Production-level mastery constructing modular, reactive user interfaces utilizing React.js (Redux Toolkit, Context API), Angular, or Vue.js.
  • Mobile-First & Low-Bandwidth Engineering: Deep technical experience executing client-side asset optimization, aggressive asset caching, lazy loading, and lightweight bundle delivery to ensure high performance over low-bandwidth, unstable networks.
  • User-Centered Interface Translation: Proven pedigree in translating highly accessible, universal design wireframes into clean semantic code, ensuring digital inclusivity for diverse citizen demographics.

4.1.5 Position 3: Senior Full-Stack Engineer – DevSecOps, Cloud & Platform Reliability

A. Position Focus

This position serves as the operational safeguard of the platform, taking primary ownership of environment isolation, security engineering, deployment automation, and continuous server performance testing to maximize system availability (uptime).

B. Targeted Technical Competencies

  • Automated CI/CD & Infrastructure-as-Code: Advanced proficiency managing containerized environments (Docker, Kubernetes) and configuring high-availability orchestration and automated code delivery pipelines.
  • Cloud & Platform Reliability: Deep production experience managing cloud-native deployments, load-balancing traffic spikes, and maintaining high uptime metrics across centralized integration gateways.
  • DevSecOps & Threat Mitigation: Implementing strict security configurations, static/dynamic code analysis workflows, automated backup frameworks, and zero-trust vulnerability auditing.

5. Data Migration and Management

Where platform optimization and architectural refactoring involve structural changes to the core application architecture, underlying database schemas, or cloud hosting environments, the consultancy team shall take absolute technical responsibility for the secure preservation and transition of active production data.

To ensure complete continuity of government operations and to mitigate the risk of data loss or corruption, the consultants shall execute the following data migration mandates:

  • Comprehensive Approach Design: Formulate and document secure, end-to-end data migration methodologies, establishing clean structural mapping protocols between legacy storage layouts and targeted future-state data models.
  • Rigorous Validation & Cleansing: Implement automated data cleansing, format standardization, and validation workflows to eliminate anomalies, duplicate records, or data structural defects prior to executing data ingestion cycles.
  • Integrity & Reconciliation Auditing: Execute mandatory cryptographic integrity checks, automated checksum verifications, and thorough data reconciliation procedures to guarantee that zero information loss occurs during the transit window.
  • Fault-Tolerant Rollback Arrangements: Establish, test, and maintain robust, near-instantaneous rollback mechanisms and disaster recovery procedures to safely revert database environments to their exact pre-migration state in the event of an migration anomaly.
  • Strict Sovereignty & Privacy Compliance: Enforce unwavering compliance with all applicable national data protection frameworks and privacy requirements, ensuring that sensitive citizen attributes remain fully encrypted, masked, and audited throughout the entire migration pipeline.

6. Project Governance, Reporting, and Operational Arrangements

6.1 Reporting Hierarchy

The consultants will report directly to the appointed Focal Person of the EARDIP Project Implementation Unit (PIU) at the Ministry of Innovation and Technology. Technical engineering outputs will undergo secondary structural verification by MInT’s internal Digital Government Infrastructure Lead.

6.2 Administrative Frameworks

Progress Reviews: Consultants are required to participate in bi-weekly sprint reviews, updating project tracking software (Jira) to reflect task velocities and systemic technical roadblocks.

Monthly Statements: On the final working day of each calendar month, consultants must submit a concise Monthly Progress Report summarizing items developed, bugs resolved, and documents authored. This report serves as the mandatory supporting document for monthly invoice clearances.

6.3 Inputs Provided by the Client (MInT / EARDIP PIU)

To facilitate the immediate, uninterrupted execution of tasks, the client will supply the consultants with the following resources:

  • Secure, designated physical workspace within the Ministry of Innovation and Technology headquarters in Addis Ababa.

High-speed, enterprise-grade internet connectivity and stable access to internal development servers.

  • Comprehensive administrative access to existing legacy software source repositories, data schemas, server hosting environments, and hardware setups.
  • Formal letters of introduction to secure access, host discovery workshops, and extract process documentation from partner public institutions.

6.4 Assignment Duration, Location, and Institutional Terms

6.5 Timeline

The initial duration of this consultancy service contract is strictly fixed at twelve (12) calendar months. Upon the conclusion of the initial year, the contract may be renewed by mutual consent for an additional term. Any extension remains subject to exceptional individual performance evaluations, ongoing funding availability from the World Bank, and technical needs of the work.

6.6 Nature of Position

This is a full-time, dedicated professional consultancy position. The consultant cannot maintain external corporate employment or consulting obligations that compromise their project availability. The duty station is entirely based in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, requiring regular on-site attendance at MInT offices (Arada Sub-city, Tracon Building).

7. Payment

Payment will be made on a monthly basis.

8. Selection Method

The attention of interested individual is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” July 2016 (“Procurement Regulations”) revised November 2017, August 2018 and September 2023, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest

An individual consultant will be selected in accordance with the Selection of Individual Consultant (Section V) method set out in the Procurement Regulations. Further information can be obtained, by email at the address below during office hours from 8:30 AM to 5:30 PM Addis Ababa time.

Interested applicants should send expressions of interest, together with information demonstrating that they have the required qualification and relevant experience to perform the service (description of similar assignments, experience in similar conditions, qualifications, and so forth) by providing CVs, formal application letter and all supporting documents to the address indicated below in person, or by mail, on or before October 29th, 2026, but preferably by e-mail.

The consulting services (“the Services”) involve the preparation of a comprehensive and legally sound National Land Use Plan (NLU Plan) for Belize. Assignment Title: Local Hydro-Mechanical Engineer

Reference No.: PIREP-IC-09

The Republic of North Macedonia has received financing from the World Bank, acting as trustee of the Grant Facility for Project Preparation (GFPP), for the preparation of the Zletovica Productivity through Irrigation and Renewable Energy Project (PIREP), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. The Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Water Economy (MAFWE), through its Project Implementation Unit (PIU), is responsible for implementation of the grant.

The preparation grant supports the updating of technical and hydraulic studies, dam safety documentation, transboundary-water analyses, and environmental and social instruments for Phases II and III of the Zletovica Hydrosystem, covering irrigation development and hydropower investments. The PIU implements the grant in close coordination with the Public Enterprise for Water Management Activities HS “Zletovica”–Probištip (PE HS Zletovica), which provides technical leadership and institutional support.

The objective of the assignment is to provide full-time technical oversight, engineering support, and quality assurance on hydro-mechanical systems and equipment associated with the preparation of Phase II irrigation and Phase III hydropower investments. The Consultant will serve as the principal hydro-mechanical advisor to the PIU and PE HS Zletovica, supporting technically sound, safe, reliable, maintainable, cost-effective, and climate-resilient solutions in accordance with applicable national requirements and World Bank standards.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include reviewing feasibility studies, hydraulic assessments, detailed engineering designs, technical specifications and cost estimates; assessing gates, valves, penstocks, pressure pipelines, pumping stations, steel structures, intake and outlet works, and related equipment; reviewing interfaces with Kneevo Dam, existing water supply and operational systems, dam safety, electrical, automation and SCADA systems; providing hydro-mechanical inputs to environmental and social instruments; supporting preparation and review of bidding documents, bills of quantities, equipment schedules, testing and commissioning requirements; reviewing manufacturers’ submissions and quality-control records; contributing to technical evaluation, construction supervision arrangements, operational improvements, training, project reporting, field visits and World Bank missions.

The Consultant will report technically to the Director of PE HS Zletovica, who will provide day-to-day technical direction and review outputs. The PIU Coordinator/Project Director will serve as the contract-management focal point and provide administrative and procurement-related oversight.

The assignment is expected to be full-time during the GFPP-funded preparation period, subject to the contract terms and project schedule. The Consultant will be based full-time at HS Zletovica in North Macedonia and undertake regular field visits to project sites, existing facilities, and relevant institutions as required. Any continuation into project implementation will be subject to satisfactory performance, project approval, financing availability, and the applicable contracting arrangements.

The complete Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment are included in Annex 1 to this Request for Expressions of Interest and form an integral part of it.

MAFWE now invites eligible individuals (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information (curriculum vitae and references, in English) demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

  • University degree in Mechanical Engineering, Hydro-Mechanical Engineering, Hydraulic Machinery Engineering, Hydropower Engineering, or a closely related field. A Master’s degree would be considered an advantage.
  • Minimum 10 years of relevant professional experience in hydro-mechanical engineering associated with dams, hydropower facilities, irrigation infrastructure, pumping stations, water supply systems, or other major hydraulic infrastructure.
  • Demonstrated experience in at least three large or technically complex water infrastructure projects involving hydro-mechanical equipment, gates, valves, penstocks, pumping systems, hydraulic steel structures, or hydropower facilities.

  • Demonstrated experience as Senior Hydro-Mechanical Engineer, Mechanical Engineer, Technical Reviewer, Design Engineer, Construction Supervision Engineer, or similar senior technical role.
  • Experience in review of consultant outputs, equipment specifications, procurement packages, factory inspections, testing, commissioning, and contract implementation supervision is highly desirable.
  • Familiarity with World Bank-financed projects, procurement procedures, and Environmental and Social Framework requirements is an advantage.
  • Strong analytical, coordination, and technical report-writing skills.
  • Professional proficiency in written and spoken Macedonian and English.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraphs 3.15, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, Seventh Edition, September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policies on conflict of interest and unfair competitive advantage.

Kazakhstan

Loan No.: IBRD-97350

Assignment Title: Construction Supervision Consultant for the Jezkazgan–Karagandy Road Section under OPBRC Contracts

Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): KZ-KAZAUTOZHOL-562877-CS-QCBS

 

The JSC “NC “KazAvtoZhol” has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Transport Resilience and Connectivity Enhancement Project (P500565) Jezkazgan–Karagandy Section of Trans–Caspian International Transport Route (Middle Corridor) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

 

The assignment covers the provision of Construction Supervision Consultant (CSC) services for the rehabilitation and long-term performance-based maintenance of approximately 457 km of the Jezkazgan–Karagandy road section, forming part of the Trans-Caspian International Transport Route (Middle Corridor). The road works are structured under four Output- and Performance-Based Road Contracts (OPBRC) following the World Bank's applicable Standard Procurement Documents for OPBRC. Works are being carried out under four separate OPBRC contracts, all of which have been signed in July 2026 and are currently under implementation, as follows:

 

Lot 1

km 783 – km 905

122 km

Lot 2

km 683 – km 783

100 km

Lot 3

km 583 – km 683

100 km

Lot 4

km 448 – km 583

135 km

Total

 

457 km

 

The CSC will be responsible for supervising all four lots under a single contract with KazAvtoZhol, following the World Bank's applicable Standard Procurement Documents for OPBRC. The CSC's responsibilities include review of contractor designs, supervision of civil works during the construction, contract administration, and reporting. The assignment also encompasses environmental and social supervision obligations under the World Bank's Environmental and Social Framework (ESF), including monitoring of resettlement, biodiversity impacts (including saiga antelope migration corridors), and implementation of the project's Sexual Exploitation and Abuse/Sexual Harassment (SEA/SH) prevention measures. The total estimated input is 473 person-months across 9 Key Expert and 13 Non-Key Expert positions

The initial duration of this time-based contract is expected to be approximately 24 months.  The extension and expansion of the services may be considered subject to the Consultant’s satisfactory performance.

 

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment is attached to this request for expressions of interest.

 

JSC NC KazAvtoZhol invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to express their interest in providing the above-mentioned services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Assignment. The main criteria for shortlisting Consultants are as follows:

1. Experience in Supervision of Road Construction

Experience in completed contracts under which the firm acted as the lead supervision consultant for road works involving road sections of at least 30 km each. Such contracts must have been completed within the last fifteen (15) years.

2. Experience with OPBRC / DB (Design-Build) / DBO (Design-Build-Operate) / PBM (Performance-Based Maintenance) / EPC (Engineering, Procurement and Construction) / PBC (Performance-Based Contract) Contracts and International Financial Institution-Financed Projects

At least one (1) completed or substantially advanced assignment involving the supervision or administration of an OPBRC, DB (Design-Build), DBO (Design-Build-Operate), PBM (Performance-Based Maintenance), EPC (Engineering, Procurement and Construction), PBC (Performance-Based Contract), or similar type of contract; or experience in at least two (2) contracts financed by multilateral development banks, such as the World Bank, the Asian Development Bank (ADB), the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD), or the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB), completed within the last ten (10) years.

3. Geographic Experience

Demonstrated experience in supervising road works in Kazakhstan or region with similar geographic and climatic conditions within the last ten (10) years, however experience in Kazakhstan is an advantage.

Key Experts will be evaluated at the Technical Proposal submission stage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.15, and 3.16 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” 7th Edition, September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.  In addition, please refer to the following specific information on conflict of interest related to this assignment: any firm (or its affiliate) that participated in the preparation of the OPBRC works contractor bidding documents, the feasibility study, or the detailed design for this road section shall not be eligible to apply, as this would constitute a conflict of interest under paragraphs 3.15–3.16 of the Procurement Regulations.

   

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

 

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality And Cost-Based Selection method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST

(Consulting Services – Individual Selection)

Ethiopia Digital ID for Inclusion and Services Project

Assignment Title

Finance Officer (Accountant)

Reference No.

ET-NIDP-576621-CS-INDV

The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia, Ministry of Finance (MoF), has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Ethiopia Digital ID for Inclusion and Services Project. The National ID Program (NIDP), the ultimate project implementer, intends to apply part of the proceeds for selecting an individual consultant.

The National ID Program is looking for a Finance Officer (Accountant) to support the Program Management Unit (PMU) in the financial management and accounting of the Project. The position will support the PMU in ensuring that project funds are used for their intended purposes with due attention to economy, efficiency, effectiveness, transparency, and accountability, and in compliance with Government of Ethiopia requirements, the Financing Agreement, Project Implementation Manual (PIM), and World Bank financial management and disbursement requirements.

Key Responsibilities

  • Execute the overall financial management activities for the Project consistent with applicable agreements, manuals, and project documents.
  • Work closely with the Financial Management Specialist on budgeting, accounting, internal controls, fund flows, financial reporting, and audit matters.
  • Support annual planning and budgeting and the process of incorporating the project budget into the Government budget.
  • Maintain budget discipline and report budget variances and the reasons for such variances to the Financial Management Specialist.
  • Support the preparation and submission of budgets and ensure that relevant development-partner requirements are appropriately captured.
  • Implement and maintain adequate financial management systems and procedures and ensure that books of accounts and accounting records are complete, current, and properly documented.
  • Support periodic financial reporting for development partners and the Government in accordance with applicable reporting requirements and formats.
  • Prepare quarterly Interim Financial Reports (IFRs) and annual project financial statements in accordance with World Bank and Government requirements and ensure timely submission.
  • Participate in mitigating financial risks and implement applicable development-partner disbursement procedures in accordance with the financing agreements and requirements.
  • Collect bank advice and bank statements and prepare timely bank reconciliations.
  • Support preparation and submission of Withdrawal Applications, monitor Designated Account balances, and reconcile project expenditures with Client Connection records and disbursement reports.
  • Apply internal controls for petty cash and bank management and participate in safeguarding project assets, fixed assets, and inventories.
  • Process monthly employee salary payments and support management of income tax and pension contributions.
  • Ensure timely settlement of advances, prepayments, and payables and timely reporting to tax authorities and other relevant government organizations.
  • Verify the completeness, accuracy, and adequacy of supporting documents before processing payments and ensure compliance with applicable procedures, financing agreements, and project manuals.
  • Support internal and external audits, ensure documents are available to auditors, and coordinate implementation of audit recommendations through an appropriate tracking mechanism.
  • Carry out other related duties as assigned by NIDP/PMU.

Minimum Qualifications and Experience

  • Minimum of a Bachelor’s Degree in Finance, Accounting, or a related field; a Master’s Degree is preferred.
  • At least four (4) years of relevant professional experience for Bachelor’s Degree holders, or at least two (2) years for Master’s Degree holders, with progressively responsible experience in a major company, government institution, or non-government organization.
  • At least three (3) years of prior experience in implementing projects/programs or in project financial management.
  • Relevant experience in Government of Ethiopia or donor-financed projects is required; experience in a World Bank-financed project is an advantage.
  • Ability to use accounting and financial management software, including IFMIS, Peachtree/accounting software, spreadsheets, and databases.
  • Knowledge and practical experience with World Bank financial management, disbursement, reporting, and Client Connection procedures is an advantage.
  • Excellent communication and reporting skills, including the ability to present financial information and analysis to management.
  • Fluency in English and Amharic.
  • High level of personal integrity and a transparent, systematic, and accountable working style.
  • Ability to work under pressure, meet deadlines, and undertake additional assignments as required by NIDP/PMU.

Duration and Location

The consultant will be engaged on a full-time basis for an initial period of twelve (12) months, with the possibility of extension subject to satisfactory performance and availability of budget. The position will be based in Addis Ababa.

Selection Method

The selection method is based on paragraphs 7.36 and 7.37 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations. The attention of interested individuals is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers,” July 2016, as revised, including February 2025, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

An individual will be selected in accordance with the Selection of Individual Consultant (Section V) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

The Expression of Interest should include a CV, formal application/cover letter, and documentary evidence supporting the stated qualifications and experience, including descriptions of relevant assignments and experience in similar conditions.

Lao People's Democratic Republic

                                    Peace, Independent Democracy, Unity, Prosperity

                                     Job Title:                   

Department:

Impact Assessment International Consultant

(Part-time, Lump Sum Contract)

(01 Position)

Ministry of Education and Sports

Department Technical and Vocational Education and Training (DTVET)

Lao PDR: Priority Skills for Growth Project (Lao-PSG)

Project ID: P172774 Project Coordinator Unit (PCU-DTVET)

Location:

            Commence date

Vientiane Capital

15 January 2027

JOB PURPOSE

The Lao People's Democratic Republic (Lao PDR) faces a significant skills gap, particularly in key economic sectors such as agriculture, logistics, and information and communication technology (ICT). At the same time, labor market intermediation services remain underdeveloped, making it difficult for job seekers, even those with relevant skills, to find suitable employment. Women, migrants, and disadvantaged populations face even greater challenges in accessing opportunities for skills development and employment. For Lao PDR to realize its economic growth potential and ensure inclusive development, strategic investments in skills supply and employment services are critical.

Recognizing these challenges, the World Bank has been supporting the Government of Lao PDR through technical assistance and financial loan support to implement the Priority Skills for Growth Project from July 2022 to June 2027. This project is led by the Ministry of Education and Sports (MOES) and the Ministry of Labor and Social Welfare (MOLSW) and aims to enhance access, quality, and relevance of skills development and employment services for youth and other vulnerable groups in the three priority sectors: agriculture, logistics, and ICT. Over five years, the project aims to catalyze system-level reforms, ensuring that skills training programs are more aligned with labor market needs.

As part of evidence-based reporting, Lao-PSG will send consultants to assess the impact of the Priority Skills for Growth Project (Lao-PSG). The Project Impact Assessment will cover the assessment of Lao-PSG inputs and deliverables based on the Project Design Monitoring Framework (DMF), specifically but not limited to the following:

The study will be carried out on behalf of the Ministry of Education and Sports' Department of Technical Vocational Education and Training (DTVET) and the Ministry of Labor and Social Welfare. The evaluation results will be used in evidence-based reporting to influence the technical and vocational education, job centers, and skill development centers (SDCs) subsector, as well as future projects.

The consultant will conduct a project impact assessment for Loan No. Credit No. 7042-LA, Lao PSG. Based on the PIM, including the DMF, Covenants/Safeguards, and others, the impact assessment will provide (i) an overall assessment of project results by outputs focused on achievement, constraints including capacity, financial support, ownership and commitment at all levels, and legal framework or policy; (ii) analysis of findings and recommendations; and (iii) detailed information and analysis in terms of capacity, financing, and ownership. The findings and recommendations can be used and mentioned in the project's final report. It will examine and revise the DMF, ESF, and other covenants.

To support this endeavor, the project is looking to an international consultant to conduct a joint impact evaluation of the Lao-PSG and make strategic recommendations to increase its role in skills development and workforce planning. The nation consultant will work closely with both ministries, MOES and MoLSW.

SCOPE OF WORK

Scope of Work

At the overall project level, covering the components and activities implemented by both MOES and MOLSW, the study will address the following objectives:

  1. Assess implementation progress and the delivery of project activities, outputs, and outcomes across the components implemented by MOES and MOLSW, including achievement of targets under the Results Monitoring Framework (RMF).
  2. Assess the project’s relevance and alignment with government priorities, labour market needs, and the needs of target beneficiaries.
  3. Assess the project’s effectiveness and the positive and negative effects of its interventions on access to, quality of, and relevance of skills development, technical and vocational education and training, employment services, and self-employment support.
  4. Assess the project’s efficiency, including the use of financial, human, and institutional resources, implementation arrangements, coordination between the two ministries, monitoring mechanisms, and delivery timelines.
  5. Assess institutional capacity development, ownership, and commitment at central and subnational levels across MOES and MOLSW, including supported institutions and service providers.
  6. Assess the sustainability of project results, systems, services, and institutional capacities beyond project completion, and identify associated risks and practical mitigation measures.
  7. Identify cross-cutting and component-specific implementation gaps, lessons learned, and good practices, and recommend practical measures for the remaining implementation period and future skills development and employment projects.
  8. Provide clear quantitative and qualitative evidence to substantiate all assessment findings and ratings, with analysis disaggregated by ministry, component, institution, location, and beneficiary group where relevant.
  9. .

Detailed Tasks and/or Expected Output

The international consultant will work with the national consultant in carrying out the following project impact assessment stages and will help ensure timely completion of the report. The consultant will also both with PMUs, and relevant stakeholders under MOES and MOLSW to complete following project impact assessment stages and ensure the timely submission of all required report.

First Stage Implementation

  1. Develop a sound understanding of the project.
  2. Identify key project activities, outputs, and outcomes.
  3. Identify the most critical indicators of progress and results.
  4. Review the project’s RMF and apply it to the assessment.

 

Second Stage Implementation

  1. Prepare survey tools and instruments
  2. Pilot and refine the tools and instruments

Third Stage Implementation

  1. Review secondary data.

2. Collect field data

Fourth Stage Implementation

  1.  Analyze the data and prepare the report.
  2. Validate the report.

Finalize and complete the reportData will be gathered from; (i) fieldwork supported by the national consultant; (ii) secondary sources; (iii) meetings with key stakeholders, and beneficiaries across the MOES-; MOLSW-implemented components; (iv) relevant project and government information systems, including the TVET Education Management Information System (TVET-MIS) and Labour Market Information System (, LMIS);; and (v) other relevant sources. Both  PMUs  will provide available data, facilitate access to relevant institutions and stakeholders, and support the consultants’ fieldwork.

The consultants may use field survey questionnaires and group discussions to generate quantitative and qualitative evidence for the assessment and analysis.

The study will be completed within five months. The first three months will be devoted to field visits and data collection, and the remaining two months to data consolidation, analysis, reporting, and report validation.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

The International Consultant should have the following qualifications and experience:

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

Country

Department of Finance and Administration (DOFA)

Assignment Title

Finance Consultant for Chuuk State

Time Based
