The Government of The Federated States of Micronesia (FSM) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Strengthening Public Financial Management II (PFM II) Project (P181237) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

 

The consulting services (“the Services”) involve providing full-time technical advisory and capacity-building support under Component 2 – Expand Core Financial Management Information System (FMIS), Subcomponent 2.1 – Continued Rollout of Core Public Finance System of the PFM II Project.

 

The Finance Consultant for Chuuk State will support the Chuuk State Finance Department in the continued rollout, operationalization, and stabilization of the FreeBalance FMIS. The assignment will focus on validating financial transactions and data migrated from FundWare to FreeBalance, reconciling FY26 opening balances, strengthening accounting and financial reporting processes, improving internal controls related to FMIS operations, and building the capacity of State Finance staff to use the system effectively and sustainably.

 

The key responsibilities will include, but not be limited to:

  • Reviewing and validating financial transactions, account balances, and data migrated from FundWare to FreeBalance, including the reconciliation and validation of FY26 opening balances.
  • Supporting FreeBalance stabilization by identifying, documenting, prioritizing, escalating, and following up on accounting, data migration, transaction-processing, reporting, and system-related issues.
  • Supporting monthly financial reporting, bank reconciliations, accounting entries, and month-end and year-end accounting processes in accordance with applicable GASB, GAAP, and FSM accounting requirements.
  • Reviewing and strengthening internal controls, accounting procedures, and compliance-monitoring practices relevant to FMIS operations.
  • Providing hands-on coaching and on-the-job training to Chuuk State Finance staff in government accounting, FreeBalance operations, reconciliations, financial reporting, data validation, and issue resolution.
  • Coordinating with the FSM Department of Finance and Administration at the National Government level, the PFM II Project Management Unit, the FMIS Adviser, ICT personnel, and FreeBalance specialists to resolve accounting and system issues and support sustainable FMIS operations.

 

The assignment will be based in Weno, Chuuk State, Federated States of Micronesia, with coordination with the FSM Department of Finance and Administration at the National Government level. The consultancy is expected to be full-time for twelve (12) months, with an anticipated start date as soon as possible, subject to completion of the selection and contracting process.

 

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the Department of Finance and Administration website: https://dofa.gov.fm, as part of this REOI, or can be obtained at the address given below.

 

The Department of Finance and Administration now invites eligible individuals (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. Consultants should submit a Curriculum Vitae (CV) describing their qualifications, professional experience, experience in similar assignments and relevant experience in similar institutional or country contexts together with a cover letter outlining their interest in the assignment and suitability for the position.

 

The criteria for selecting the Consultant are:

Mandatory Requirements:

The Consultant shall possess:

  1. Education: A Master's degree in Accounting. Candidates holding a CPA qualification together with a degree in Finance, Information Systems, Public Administration, or an equivalent related field are also encouraged to apply.
  2. Professional Experience: At least ten (10) years of progressive experience in public sector accounting, financial management, and Public Financial Management (PFM) reforms.
  3. Technical Expertise: Demonstrated expertise in applying Governmental Accounting Standards Board (GASB) pronouncements and Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP), extensive experience with FMIS implementation, operationalization, stabilization, transaction processing, financial reporting, reconciliation and/or data migration, and demonstrated ability to identify, analyze, and resolve accounting, financial data, and system-related issues in an FMIS environment.

Desirable:

  1. Software Proficiency: Experience with FundWare and/or FreeBalance, particularly in FMIS stabilization, troubleshooting, issue escalation, and coordination with system vendors and national-level technical teams.
  2. Capacity Building and Communication: Proven ability to train and mentor government staff in financial reporting, PFM principles, and new software systems, supported by excellent analytical, communication, and report-writing skills.
  3. Governmental Accounting Knowledge: Thorough knowledge of governmental fund financial statements and government-wide financial reporting, including the Statement of Net Position, the three categories of Net Position, program and general revenues, Transfers and Internal Balances, the five categories of Fund Balance, and the distinction between Revenues and Other Financing Sources and Expenditures and Other Financing Uses.
  4. Geographic Experience: Prior experience working with island nations or small governments.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, Seventh Edition, September 2025 (“the Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

 

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours 08:00 to 17:00 hours, Pohnpei Time.

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below by e-mail only preferably by 5pm Pohnpei Time, October 31, 2026. Expressions of Interest must be submitted by email only to the following addresses:

 

Attn: Osbert Atusaasiire
Project Manager PFM II

Department of Finance and Administration

Palikir, Federated States of Micronesia

Email: osbert.atusaasiire@dofa.gov.fm

And cc to: arrio.abello@dofa.gov.fm

 

Terms of Reference – Finance Consultant

Title:

Finance Consultant

Location:

Finance Department of the Chuuk State Government with Coordination with the FSM Department of Finance & Administration at the National Government level

Duration:

12 months 

Tentative Start Date:

As soon as possible

 

1. Background

The project, Federated States of Micronesia (FSM) Strengthening Public Financial Management II (PFM II), builds upon key public financial management (PFM) reforms achieved under the previous FSM Project for Strengthening Public Financial Management (P161669) (PFM I).  The objective of PFM II is to improve fiscal management practices and increase fiscal transparency at the National Government level.  PFM II supports key strategic areas defined in FSM’s 2023-2026 PFM Reform Roadmap, e.g. addressing challenges in core institutional public finance capacity.  Specifically, the project supports:

  1. Improved fiscal management practices and controls (Component 1)
  2. Expanded core financial management information systems (Component 2)
  3. Enhanced human resource capacity, communications and change management (Component 3)
  4. Project management (Component 4)

 

The Federated States of Micronesia (FSM) Department of Finance & Administration is committed to enhancing its financial reporting and overall public financial management (PFM) capabilities.

 

The Government's financial statements must adhere to a complex set of reporting requirements, including those of the Governmental Accounting Standards Board (GASB) and Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP). Additionally, the FSM Government operates with various funds and component units, which necessitate specialized accounting and reporting treatments. Beyond financial reporting, the Government seeks to strengthen its budget preparation process, internal controls, and overall compliance framework to ensure greater efficiency, transparency, and accountability.

 

To address these challenges and improve the quality of financial management, the FSM Department of Finance & Administration (DOFA) seeks to engage a highly qualified  Financial Consultant with expertise in public sector accounting, GASB, GAAP, fund accounting, financial reporting, FMIS operationalization and stabilization and broader PFM principles.

 

The Finance Consultant will be assigned to the Chuuk State Finance Department and will work closely with State Finance staff, the FSM Department of Finance and Administration (DOFA) at the National Government level, the PFM II Project Management Unit, the FMIS Advisor, FreeBalance specialists and relevant ICT personnel. The Consultant will support the ongoing stabilization and effective operationalization of FreeBalance, including addressing accounting and data issues arising from the migration from FundWare to FreeBalance.

 

2. Objective

The primary objective of the consultancy is to strengthen financial management, accounting, reporting and FMIS operations at the State level, with particular emphasis on supporting the ongoing FreeBalance Stabilization Strategy and ensuring the accuracy and completeness of financial information in FreeBalance. The Consultant will:

  1. Verify revenue and expenditures including payroll and other financial transactions for accuracy, completeness, appropriate classification and compliance with applicable accounting requirements.
  2. Conduct transaction reviews and reconciliations to validate data originating from FundWare and other legacy records against data captured in FreeBalance and identify and address outstanding accounting and migration issues.
  3. Establish and implement robust procedures for validating, classifying, coding and recording revenues and expenditures in FreeBalance.
  4. Provide hands-on support to relevant Finance staff in processing, reviewing and validating transactions in FreeBalance and strengthening their ability to use the system effectively.
  5.  Support the identification, reconciliation and resolution of outstanding accounting and data migration issues from FundWare to FreeBalance, and validate that migrated financial information is accurate, complete and appropriately classified.
  6. Ensure that GASB, GAAP and applicable FSM accounting and financial reporting requirements are appropriately reflected in transactions, reconciliations, migrated data and financial reports.
  7. Validate that opening balances for FY26 accounts in FreeBalance are accurate, complete, properly supported and reconciled to the relevant prior-period financial records.
  8. Coordinate technical and system-related issues with the FSM Department of Finance and Administration at the National Government level, including the FMIS Advisor, ICT Advisor, FreeBalance specialists and other designated technical resources.

 

 

 

3. Scope of Work

The consultant will be responsible for, but not limited to, the following tasks:

A. FMIS Operationalisation, Stabilization and Data Validation:

  • Data Migration and Accounting Issues: Support the review and resolution of outstanding accounting and data migration issues arising from the transition from FundWare to FreeBalance. The Consultant will work with State Finance staff and relevant technical specialists to identify discrepancies, determine appropriate accounting treatment and follow up on corrective actions.
  • FreeBalance Stabilization: Actively support the implementation of the FreeBalance Stabilization Strategy by identifying, documenting, prioritising and following up on operational, accounting, transaction, reporting and data issues affecting the State Finance Department.
  • Data and Transaction Validation: Work with State Finance staff and relevant technical specialists to validate migrated data and transactions, identify discrepancies and ensure that corrective actions are properly implemented.
  • FY26 Opening Balances: Review and reconcile FY26 opening balances in FreeBalance to the relevant prior-period records and supporting documentation, and ensure that opening balances are accurate, complete and appropriately classified.
  • Ongoing Operational Support: Provide on-site and remote support to address continuing FreeBalance operational, accounting, data and reporting issues as part of the stabilization process.
  • Software Training: Collaborate with the software vendor and internal staff to ensure the training program for the new FreeBalance system effectively addresses the needs of all users.
  • Technical Coordination and Escalation: Coordinate technical issues with the FSM Department of Finance & Administration at National Government level, including the FMIS Adviser, ICT personnel and FreeBalance specialists. Where appropriate, document and escalate issues through the FreeBalance support channels and follow up until resolution or an agreed corrective action is established

 

B. Internal Control and Compliance:

  • Internal Control Framework: review and strengthen the existing accounting policies, procedures and manual to enhance the internal control framework, focusing on key financial processes such as revenue collection, asset management, payroll, etc.
  • Compliance: assist in the development of a compliance checklist or a compliance-monitoring system to ensure adherence to financial/accounting regulations, laws, and policies.
  • Risk Assessment: Conduct a risk assessment of key financial processes and recommend mitigation strategies.
  • Control Implementation and Follow-up: Provide practical support to Finance staff in implementing and monitoring accounting controls, particularly controls relating to transaction processing, reconciliations, financial reporting, data quality and FreeBalance operations.

 

 

C. Accounting and Financial Reporting Support:

  • Train accountants in government institutions on how to post accounting entries in the FreeBalance system and provide on the job support.
  • Support government accountants to produce monthly reports on the FreeBalance system
  • Provide on the job support to do bank reconciliations and enter government assets into the FreeBalance system.
  • Support the preparation and review of monthly and periodic financial reports, including review of supporting schedules and follow-up of unusual balances, unreconciled items and reporting discrepancies.
  • Support bank and other account reconciliations and follow up on outstanding reconciling items.
  • Review transactions and account balances to identify accounting errors, incomplete postings, incorrect classifications or other issues affecting the reliability of financial information.
  • Support month-end and year-end accounting processes and ensure that relevant balances and supporting records are appropriately reconciled and maintained.
  • Provide specific support to validate FY26 opening balances and ensure that they are complete, accurate, reconciled and supported by appropriate documentation.

 

D. FreeBalance Stabilization and Issue Management

    • Maintain a structured record of FreeBalance issues identified by the State Finance Department, including the nature of the issue, affected transactions/accounts, actions taken, responsible parties and status.
    • Work with the FMIS Adviser, FreeBalance specialists, ICT personnel and National DoFA to investigate and resolve issues affecting transaction processing, accounting, reporting, data migration and system functionality.
    • Escalate unresolved technical issues through the appropriate FreeBalance support channels and coordinate follow-up with National DoFA and relevant technical specialists.
    • Validate implemented corrections and confirm that resolved issues have been appropriately addressed from an accounting and financial reporting perspective.

 

E. Knowledge Transfer:

  • Conduct workshops and one-on-one training sessions for the Department of Finance & Administration staff on financial reporting, PFM principles, and internal controls.
  • Assist in the development or revision of financial reporting, budgeting, and internal control policies and procedures to align with best practices and international standards.
  • Provide hands-on coaching and on-the-job training to State Finance staff in FreeBalance transaction processing, reconciliations, financial reporting, data validation and issue identification.
  • Build the capacity of State Finance staff to independently identify, document, escalate and follow up on FreeBalance and accounting issues.
  • Coordinate capacity-building activities with the FMIS Adviser, FreeBalance specialists and National DoFA to avoid duplication and ensure consistency of technical guidance.

 

4. Deliverables

The consultant will be expected to produce the following deliverables:

No.

Deliverable

Frequency / Timing

1

Initial Assessment and Work Plan – assessment of accounting, financial reporting, reconciliation, FreeBalance operationalisation, outstanding FundWare-to-FreeBalance issues, FY26 opening balances, internal controls and key capacity needs, with an agreed work plan.

  1. Background

The Government of the Federated States of Micronesia (FSM), through the Department of Finance and Administration (DOFA), is implementing the FSM Strengthening Public Financial Management II Project (PFM II), financed by the World Bank. The PFM II Project supports strengthening public financial management systems, fiscal transparency, financial accountability, institutional capacity, and financial reporting across the National Government and State Governments. As part of these reforms, the Government seeks to progressively strengthen its capacity to prepare financial statements in accordance with applicable United States Governmental Accounting Standards Board (US GASB) requirements and reduce long-term reliance on external technical assistance.

 

While progress has been made in improving public financial management systems and implementing the FreeBalance Financial Management Information System (FMIS), significant work remains to strengthen accounting policies, reporting procedures, Chart of Accounts structures, financial statement preparation processes, and institutional capacity at both National and State Government levels.

 

The Government therefore intends to engage a Senior US GASB Financial Reporting and Capacity Building Advisor to support the institutionalization of US GASB-compliant financial reporting practices, strengthen financial reporting systems and frameworks, support achievement of PFM II Results Framework indicators, and build sustainable Government capacity to prepare National Government, State Government, and ultimately consolidated financial statements.

 

Project Components

  • Component 1: Improved Fiscal Management Practices and Controls
  • Component 2: Expanded Core Financial Management Information Systems
  • Component 3: Enhanced Human Resource Capacity, Communications and Change Management
  • Component 4: Project Management

 

  1. Objective of the Assignment

The objective of this assignment is to strengthen the capacity of the FSM National Government and State Governments to prepare, review, and sustain US GASB-compliant financial statements and progressively establish the institutional foundations required for consolidated Whole-of-Government financial reporting.

 

The assignment will support:

  • Strengthening accounting policies, procedures, and financial reporting frameworks;
  • Development of standardized financial reporting manuals, templates, and guidance materials;
  • Strengthening the Government Chart of Accounts and related reporting structures;
  • Building practical financial reporting capacity within National and State Governments;
  • Supporting implementation of US GASB-compliant financial reporting practices;
  • Supporting achievement of PFM II Results Framework indicators relating to in-house preparation of financial statements;
  • Strengthening institutional sustainability and reducing long-term dependency on external consultants.

 

  1. Scope of Services

The Consultant shall work closely with DOFA, State Government Finance Departments, Treasury personnel, FMIS teams, auditors, and other stakeholders.

 

    1. US GASB Policy and Reporting Framework Strengthening

The Consultant shall:

  • Review existing accounting policies and financial reporting procedures;
  • Assess compliance with applicable US GASB requirements;
  • Develop or update Government accounting policies and reporting guidance;
  • Support development of standardized year-end financial reporting procedures;
  • Develop practical guidance on application of US GASB standards within FSM;
  • Recommend improvements to strengthen consistency of financial reporting across National and State Governments.

 

    1. Financial Reporting Manuals, Templates and Procedures

The Consultant shall:

  • Develop and maintain financial reporting manuals;
  • Develop standardized working paper templates;
  • Develop financial statement templates;
  • Develop disclosure templates and supporting schedules;
  • Establish reporting procedures supporting consistent preparation of financial statements;
  • Support adoption of standardized reporting formats across National and State Governments.

 

    1. Chart of Accounts and Financial Reporting Structure Strengthening

The Consultant shall:

  • Review the existing Chart of Accounts;
  • Assess alignment with US GASB requirements;
  • Recommend enhancements to support improved financial reporting;
  • Strengthen account classifications relating to assets, liabilities, fund balances, revenues and expenditures;
  • Support alignment between FMIS reporting outputs and financial reporting requirements;
  • Support development of reporting structures required for future consolidation of Government financial statements.

 

    1. National Government Financial Reporting Capacity Building

The Consultant shall:

  • Support Treasury and accounting staff involved in preparation of National Government financial statements;
  • Provide practical mentoring and coaching;
  • Conduct workshops and training activities;
  • Support implementation of recommendations arising from annual financial statement reviews;
  • Support progressive achievement of PFM II Results Framework Indicator IR-1 relating to preparation of National Government US GASB-compliant financial statements.

 

    1. State Government Financial Reporting Capacity Building

The Consultant shall:

  • Work with State Government Finance Directors and accounting personnel;
  • Assess capacity gaps relating to financial reporting;
  • Deliver targeted training and mentoring activities;
  • Support adoption of standardized financial reporting practices;
  • Strengthen State Government readiness for preparation of US GASB-compliant financial statements;
  • Support future consolidation requirements.

 

    1. Consolidation and Whole-of-Government Reporting Readiness

The Consultant shall:

  • Assess current arrangements for consolidation of financial information;
  • Recommend frameworks supporting future Whole-of-Government reporting;
  • Support harmonization of reporting classifications and formats across National and State Governments;
  • Develop a roadmap for progressive implementation of consolidated financial reporting arrangements;
  • Support achievement of PFM II Results Framework Indicator IR-2 relating to consolidated financial statements.

 

    1. Training, Certification and Sustainability

The Consultant shall:

  • Develop annual financial reporting capacity development plans;
  • Recommend suitable US GASB certification and professional development programs;
  • Support development of training curricula and materials;
  • Establish knowledge transfer mechanisms;
  • Support development of an internal cadre of Government officers capable of independently preparing financial statements;
  • Strengthen long-term institutional sustainability of US GASB financial reporting practices.

  1. Reporting Arrangements

The Consultant shall report to the Assistant Secretary – Treasury and work closely with:

Republic of North Macedonia

Ministry of Transport

VACANCY ANNOUNCEMENT

Recruitment of Individual Consultant

                                                                                                                   Job Position: LEGAL EXPERT

 

WBTTFP–8929-MKD-411L-2

General Information: The Ministry of Transport (the CLIENT) intends to engage a highly qualified individual consultant to provide services as Legal Expert of the Project Implementation Unit (PIU) for the Trade and Transport Facilitation Project (TTFP), the Local Roads Connectivity Project (LRCP), and the Grant Facility for Project Preparation for the Railway Sector Reform Project (GFPP for the RSRP).

The assignment is full-time until November 15, 2027. The Consultant shall be available to commence the assignment no later than thirty (30) days from receipt of the notification of selection.

Project Background: The TTFP is implemented in its first phase in Serbia, North Macedonia and Albania, the Local Roads Connectivity Project (LRCP) is in final phase of implementation and the Project Preparation for the Railway Sector Reform Project (GFPP for the RSRP) is in preparation phase and shall be implemented in North Macedonia.

The PIU in North Macedonia is staffed with different expert profiles to support implementation, monitoring and coordination of the Projects.

The Trade and Transport Facilitation Project Phase 1 is implemented in Serbia, North Macedonia and Albania. In North Macedonia, it includes investments, technical assistance, and regulatory and institutional reforms, including the National Single Window (NSW), improvements at the border crossing points at Deve Bair and Kjafasan, deployment of an Intelligent Transport System (ITS) on the A1 motorway (Corridor X), and related technical assistance.

The Local Roads Connectivity Project (LRCP) supports selected municipalities through investments in the reconstruction, rehabilitation and upgrading of local roads and streets to improve mobility, connectivity and road safety. Investments may also include sidewalks, bicycle paths, street lighting, slope and landslide stabilization, junction improvements, pedestrian crossings, drainage, and capacity building of municipal staff.

The Grant Facility for Project Preparation for the Railway Sector Reform Project (GFPP for the RSRP), Grant No. TF0D2237, supports preparation of the proposed Railway Sector Reform Project, including procurement readiness, market engagement and analysis, preparation of terms of reference, technical documentation and bidding documents, and capacity-building activities.

Position Objective: The Legal Expert shall support and report to the Project Director and Project Coordinator and provide legal advice on project activities, contracts and administrative procedures. The Legal Expert is responsible for supporting compliance with the applicable North Macedonian legal framework, relevant project documents, contractual provisions and World Bank requirements; preparing and reviewing contractual instruments, amendments and annexes; and identifying and mitigating legal risks that may affect Project implementation.

Immediate superiors: Project Director and Project Coordinator. The Legal Expert shall coordinate closely with the relevant Procurement Specialist and Contract Manager on procurement and contractual matters.

Tasks and Responsibilities: The Legal Expert shall carry out the following legal and administrative responsibilities, including but not limited to:

- Prepare and review contractual documentation, amendments and annexes, in cooperation with the relevant Project Managers and the Procurement Specialist and Contract Manager, in accordance with the applicable Project Operations Manual (POM), Project Appraisal Document (PAD), the relevant legal agreements between the Republic of North Macedonia and the World Bank, applicable World Bank requirements and relevant North Macedonian legislation;

- Provide legal advice and support on matters arising during implementation of the TTFP, LRCP and GFPP for the RSRP, in coordination with the relevant PIU team members and competent authorities. This includes, but is not limited to, legal support for contract implementation, preparation and review of information and submissions to the Government, and assistance with other legal matters arising under applicable national legislation in connection with project activities;

- Control and ensure that all respective project activities and reporting obligations are in strict accordance with the POM, Project Appraisal Document (PAD), the relevant legal agreements between the Republic of North Macedonia and the World Bank, World Bank’s procedures, and North Macedonian national legislation;

- Control and ensure that all reporting and contractual obligations of the PIU staff and consultants are performed in a timely manner and in accordance with the legal provisions of their respective contracts;

- Coordinate the legal review, control, and validation of all project deliverables related to service and works contracts, ensuring that payments are legally justified and backed by proper documentation;

- Ensure that contractual deadlines and legal requirements applicable to service, works and goods contracts under the TTFP, LRCP and GFPP for the RSRP are monitored and addressed;

- Support the PIU team in addressing and implementing the World Bank’s comments, recommendations and requirements, and provide legal support for the necessary actions in accordance with applicable World Bank regulations and procedures and WB Team guidance;

- Assist the Project Director, Project Coordinator and Procurement Specialist and Contract Manager in preparation and review of project management and legal documents, including contract templates, scope statements and project procedures;

- Provide legal review and advice in relation to project procurement processes, including review of bidding/selection documents and evaluation documentation for consistency with applicable national law and project requirements;

- Support the Procurement Specialist and Contract Manager throughout the procurement process, including preparation and legal review of procurement notices, bidding/selection documents, clarifications and addenda, publication, bid/proposal opening, evaluation, notification of results, award and contract signing, as applicable;

- Participate in and provide legal support to evaluation committees, including review of qualification and compliance matters, clarifications, due diligence, preparation and/or legal review of evaluation reports and other evaluation records and decisions;

- Support monitoring and follow-up of procurement processes, including key deadlines, required approvals and World Bank no-objections, procurement-related correspondence, complaints or challenges, and completeness of procurement records, in coordination with the Procurement Specialist and Contract Manager, including STEP-related documentation, as applicable;

- Assess the legal needs of project beneficiaries and define legal requirements, acceptance criteria, and contractual timelines for sub-projects;

- Coordinate the allocation of project resources and ensure that the project team has the necessary legal instruments (contracts, decisions, authorizations) at the right time;

- Provide legal guidance to PIU team members on the legal implications of project milestones, deliverables and contractual actions;

- Act as the primary legal liaison between the project team, consultants, contractors, and beneficiaries throughout the project life cycle;

- Support the Project Director and Project Coordinator in monitoring the legal and contractual performance of contractors and consultants and provide regular legal updates;

- Schedule, attend, and provide legal counsel during stakeholder meetings, ensuring all minutes and resulting reports are legally accurate;

- Monitor contract implementation from the legal perspective, including drafting and processing contract annexes, amendments and variations under the authorization of the Project Director and in coordination with the Procurement Specialist and Contract Manager;

- Participate in bidding procedures in the capacity of a Legal Member of the Evaluation Committee, as authorized by a Decision issued by the Minister of Transport;

- Submit Quarterly Progress Reports to the Project Director and Project Coordinator within ten (10) days prior to the end of each quarter, a Monthly Timesheet at the end of each month, and ad-hoc reports on major legal or contractual issues as requested.

- Perform other legal and administrative tasks assigned by the Project Director, Project Coordinator and/or Minister of Transport.

Knowledge, experience, skills, and competences:

Educational qualifications: University degree in Law, meeting either of the following requirements: (i) a four-year university degree in Law awarded under the pre-Bologna higher education system; or (ii) qualifications in Law obtained under the Bologna higher education system, comprising completion of both the first cycle (Bachelor’s Degree in Law) and the second cycle (Master’s Degree in Law / LL.M. or equivalent), with a cumulative minimum of 300 ECTS credits, corresponding to at least five years of higher education studies in Law.

Area of professional expertise: Law, Legal Affairs and Contractual Matters;

Years of experience: At least 5 years of professional experience in the legal field, including relevant experience in legal advisory, contractual or regulatory matters;

Required skills and competencies: Previous experience as a Legal Expert, Legal Consultant or in a comparable legal role; Excellent knowledge of relevant national legislation, including construction, procurement and expropriation legislation;

Desirable: Experience in implementation of projects financed by international donors (World Bank, EBRD, EU etc.); Experience in the public sector; Passed Bar Exam in North Macedonia;

Required languages: Excellent knowledge of English (reading, speaking and writing) and Macedonian;

Computer skills: MS Office and legal databases;

Managerial skills: Self-planning and organizing, problem solving, work under pressure, communication, teamwork and initiative.

Applications: The candidates should submit their Letters of Application, CVs, and Letters of Motivation (all documents in the English language) only electronically to the following e-mail: konkursi@mtc.gov.mk . The deadline for submitting the applications is November 2, 2026, at the latest. The candidates can find the ToR for the announced job position at http://mtc.gov.mk  and https://e-nabavki.gov.mk/PublicAccess/home.aspx#/international-donor-announcements .

Minimum experience and capability:

  • Bachelor’s degree in civil and/or structural engineering (or relevant discipline) with a minimum 15 years of progressively responsible professional experience in leading and managing complex engineering projects as a government or private sector employee, consultant, or contractor.
  • Holder of a Chartered Engineering Membership and registration with IPES or similar (e.g.CPEng) in Civil or Structural Engineering.
  • Demonstrated experience in design, contract administration and construction supervision of at least 5 major civil or structural infrastructure projects.
  • Proven work experience with Government or development partner-funded projects and other relevant institutions.
  • Minimum 5 years of experience integrating climate resilient, disaster risk reduction and hazard risk reduction development.

  • Experience in delivering workshops and training particularly the module list detailed in the Terms of Reference.
  • Served as Engineer or Superintendent to the Contract or equivalent role on at least five (5) infrastructure projects valued at US$1 million or more, covering design-build, design and supervise, and build only contract arrangements.

  • Proven knowledge and practical experience in applying Environmental and Social Safeguards, environmental management, social risk assessment, stakeholder engagement, and compliance monitoring processes.
  • Fluent in written and spoken English; and
  • Minimum five (5) years of professional experience working in developing countries.

Skills and competencies:

  • Demonstrated proficiency in the use of Microsoft Office Suite (e.g., Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook), with a minimum of five (5) years of professional application for technical reporting, project management, communication, and data analysis.
  • Proficient in AutoCad, or another professional drawing applications software, demonstrated through application on a minimum of five (5) civil or structural engineering projects.
  • Minimum five (5) years of hands-on experience with using structural assessment software such as ETABS, SAP2000, or STAAD or similar, for structural assessment, modelling, design verification, and seismic or wind loading analysis.

  • Willingness and ability to undertake regular travel within Samoa for visiting sites and inspection of project works.

Desirable qualifications, experience, and skills:

  • Prior experience working in the Pacific islands or on Small Island Developing States (Samoa experience highly regarded) with participation in at least three (3) infrastructure, urban development, climate resilience or community development projects. Danmanlar, Satn Alma Düzenlemelerinde belirtilen Bireysel Danmanlar için Onaylanm Seçim Yöntemleri dorultusunda seçilecektir. Sözleme, Yenilik ve Eitim Teknolojileri Genel Müdürlüü (YEGITEK) ile Danman arasnda imzalanacaktr.

Ek’te yer alan örnee uygun olarak hazrlanm Türkçe ve ngilizce özgeçmiler, özgeçmite atfta bulunulan diploma, sertifika, referans mektubu ve dier destekleyici belgelerin fotokopileri ile adayn mesleki deneyimi hakknda bilgi alnabilecek kiilerin isim ve telefon numaralaryla birlikte, en geç 02/11/2026 günü saat 17.00’ye (yerel saat) kadar aada belirtilen e-posta adresine e-posta yoluyla veya aada belirtilen adrese elden teslim edilmelidir.

 The Association of African Universities has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of the Learning and Evidence Agenda for Regional Collaboration in Eastern and Southern Africa (LEARN-ESA) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services for the engagement of an individual consultant as the Education and Research Specialist at the AAU Headquarters in Accra, Ghana.

Under the direct supervision of the Director of Special Projects, the Education and Research Specialist will provide technical and academic leadership for the projects regional learning agenda and implementation research initiatives. REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

Individual Consultant Selection

Ethiopian Statistical Service (ESS)

Reference No.: ET-ESS-574801-CS-INDV

Hiring of Sector Coordinator (Senior Statistician) for Administrative Data Production

The Ethiopian Statistical Service (ESS) intends to recruit a Sector Coordinator (Senior Statistician) for Administrative Data Production under the Modernizing Ethiopia's Statistical System Project (MESSP) financed by the World Bank. The position will support the implementation of activities related to administrative data harmonization, quality assurance, statistical standards, institutional integration, and the production of official statistics from administrative data sources.

The Sector Coordinator will provide technical leadership and coordination for administrative data production and utilization within Ethiopia's National Statistical System. The successful candidate will work closely with sector ministries, regional bureaus, and development partners to strengthen administrative data systems, improve data quality, enhance institutional coordination, and support the production of high-quality official statistics.

Duty Station: Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.

Reporting: The consultant will report directly to the Desk Head, Statistics Standard and Quality under the Administrative Data Harmonization, Standard and Quality Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of the Ethiopian Statistical Service.

Contract Duration: Twelve (12) months, with annual performance-based renewal options up to 2031.

Interested candidates should possess:

  • Master's Degree in Statistics, Economics, Data Science, Demography, Public Policy, Information Systems, or another closely related quantitative discipline. A PhD in a relevant field will be an added advantage.
  • At least ten (10) years of progressively responsible professional experience in official statistics, statistical system development, administrative data systems, data quality management, statistical standards, metadata management, or related areas.
  • Demonstrated experience working with national statistical systems, government institutions, or international development organizations.
  • Experience supporting statistical modernization programs financed by international development partners, including the World Bank, will be an advantage.
  • Strong understanding of international statistical principles, standards, administrative data systems, and best practices.
  • Demonstrated ability to coordinate multi-stakeholder technical activities involving government institutions and development partners.
  • Experience in administrative data integration, institutional coordination, data-sharing frameworks, and statistical quality improvement initiatives.
  • Excellent analytical, technical writing, presentation, and communication skills.
  • Proven ability to deliver high-quality technical outputs within agreed timelines.
  • Fluency in written and spoken in Amharic & English.

The detailed Terms of Reference (ToR) can be obtained from the Ethiopian Statistical Service (ESS) upon request.

The consultant will be selected using the Selection of Individual Consultants (INDV) method in accordance with the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers.

Credit No.: IDA 68570

Assignment Title: Consultancy Services for the Design and Establishment of a Wholesale (Apex) Development Finance Framework

Reference No. ET-DBE-575977-CS-QCBS

  1. The Development Bank of Ethiopia (DBE) is one of the state-owned financial institutions providing project finance and lease financing for small and medium enterprises (SMEs) to support the country's overall economic development. In addition to financing projects, the Bank serves as a financial intermediary that administers funds and appraises and monitors participating financial institutions through its wholesale financing program, ensuring successful project implementation.
  2. DBE invites expressions of interest (EOIs) from legally formed consulting firms to provide consultancy services for the Design and Establishment of a Wholesale (Apex) Development Finance Framework.
  3. The consulting services (“the Services”) comprise technical assistance to the Development Bank of Ethiopia (DBE) to design, document, and prepare for implementation a wholesale (apex) development finance capability as an institutional pillar of the Bank. The Services include: the design of a wholesale banking framework covering the lending model and the intermediary engagement model; an assessment of the institutional, legal and delivery structure options for housing the wholesale function; the development of a Wholesale Lending Policy and Operational Manual and of a credit guarantee and de-risking framework grounded in an explicit additionality framework; the design of a technical advisory and capacity-building program for participating financial institutions, including a dedicated module on expanding outreach to women entrepreneurs and women consumers; the integration of environmental and social risk management into intermediary accreditation and supervision; and support to DBE in preparing pilot wholesale arrangements and the associated portfolio segregation and ring-fencing arrangements. The assignment is financed under Sub-component 5.3 of the Project. The implementation period is approximately twenty (20) weeks from contract signature, with the Consultant based primarily in Addis Ababa for the core design and approval phases.
  4. The Development Bank of Ethiopia now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

       4.1. Relevant experience of the firm

Assignments count only if completed within the last ten (10) years, and only where the Consultant acted as lead firm or joint venture member – sub-consultancy roles do not count. A single assignment may satisfy more than one of the requirements listed below.

  • At least three (3) completed assignments involving the design of wholesale or apex lending frameworks, on-lending or refinancing facilities, blended-finance or credit-guarantee structures, or DFI institutional design.
  • Of these, at least one (1) was carried out for a development finance institution, state-owned development bank or apex financial institution.
  • At least one (1) assignment involving the design or operationalization of a credit guarantee, first-loss, risk-sharing or partial credit guarantee instrument, including its pricing, eligibility and claims arrangements.
  • At least one (1) assignment on a World Bank or other multilateral-financed line of credit, apex facility or financial intermediary lending operation.
  • At least two (2) assignments delivered in Sub-Saharan Africa or comparable frontier and emerging markets. For this purpose, a country is a comparable frontier or emerging market if, as at the date of the EOI submission deadline, it is (a) eligible for IDA financing (including blend countries), (b) classified by the World Bank as a low-income or lower-middle-income economy, or (c) a constituent of the MSCI Frontier Markets Index. Consultants must state, for each assignment relied upon, the country and the limb (a), (b) or (c) relied upon.

Assignments consisting solely of the following do not count under this sub-section 4.1: general management or organizational consulting; audit, tax or accounting services; IT or core-banking system implementation; training delivery without design content; market or feasibility studies without design of a lending framework or instrument; retail or corporate lending work with no financial-intermediary component.

       4.2. Technical and Managerial Capability of the Firm

  • The Consultant demonstrates in-house coverage of the following disciplines through named permanent professional staff: development finance/apex lending; credit risk; financial modeling; institutional or organizational design; inclusive/gender-responsive finance. An organogram and headcount by discipline are required. There is no minimum total headcount; the in-country mobilization requirement set out below tests capacity to deliver at the scale of this assignment.
  • The Consultant has a documented quality assurance and project management system (ISO 9001 certification or an equivalent internal QA manual, described in no more than one page).
  • The Consultant has completed at least one (1) assignment in the last seven (7) years in which it mobilized and sustained a team of five (5) or more international and national experts in-country for a period of four (4) months or more, demonstrating capacity to deploy in Addis Ababa for an engagement of approximately 20 weeks. Evidence: client name and contact, assignment dates, team size and composition, and country of deployment.

      4.3. Core Business and Organizational Experience

  • The Consultant is a legally registered firm and has at least ten (10) years of organizational experience in development finance, financial sector development or financial institution advisory. Evidence: certificate of incorporation or registration, together with the experience record submitted under the following bullet.
  • Development finance, financial sector development or financial institution advisory is a core business line of the Consultant, evidenced by at least five (5) completed consulting assignments in this field in the last ten (10) years.

5. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” July 2016, revised November 2017, August 2018, November 2020 and September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. In addition, the following specific information on conflict of interest applies to this assignment: a firm that DBE has engaged to prepare or implement activities that would place it in conflict with the obligations of this assignment, or that would confer an unfair advantage, is not eligible. Consultants shall disclose any current or prior advisory or contractual relationship with DBE within the last five (5) years.

6. The selection process will be conducted using Quality and Cost Based Method of Selection (QCBS) as laid out in the World Bank Procurement Regulation.

7. The Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. Where the Consultant is a joint venture, the core business requirement in sub-section 4.3 and at least two (2) of the three (3) assignments required under the first bullet of sub-section 4.1 shall be met by the lead member alone; the remaining requirements may be met by the members combined; and each member individually shall be eligible under Section III of the Procurement Regulations and shall not be subject to World Bank suspension or debarment. A joint venture shall submit a joint venture agreement or a letter of intent signed by all members, identifying the lead member. The qualifications, experience and resources of sub-consultants are not taken into account in shortlisting.

8. Consultants/Applicants shall submit the required documents for the EOI consideration including business registration certificate, renewed trade license, VAT registration certificate (for local consulting firm only), and tax clearance certificate (for local consulting firm only). The EOI must not exceed twenty (20) pages, excluding the cover letter, registration certificate, and financial statements.

9. Interested applicants may obtain further information and clarification until October 26,2026 from DBE Head Office, Procurement Directorate, in front of DBE head office (Kiyamed Building 1st floor), Tel. +251 11 5578088, ext. 364; Fax +251 11 553 7982 or via email attention to Mr. Kirubel Girma, Procurement Director, kirubelg@dbe.com.et and must copy to tesfahunge@dbe.com.et

10.The Expression of Interest/ EoIs shall be submitted in English, one original and one copy, EoIs shall be submitted into the tender box prepared for the purpose on or before November 03, 2026 at 4:00 P.M (in the afternoon) at the Development Bank of Ethiopia, in front of DBE head office (Kiyamed Building 1st floor) or via email to Mr. Kirubel Girma, Procurement Director, kirubelg@dbe.com.et

DBE reserves the right to accept or reject a part/all of the entire bid.

data.title: The selection of Digital Transformation Senior Coordinator
data.project_name: Jordan: Modernizing Education, Skills, and Administrative Reforms (MASAR) Operation
data.notice_text:
Ministry of Education and Human Resources Development

Modernizing Education, Skills, and Administrative Reforms (MASAR) Program

Terms of Reference for:  Digital Transformation Senior Coordinator

Reference No.:  JO-MOE-566807-CS-INDV

Program Background:

The Modernizing Education, Skills, and Administrative Reforms (MASAR) Program for Results (PforR) is a transformative, system-wide reform initiative anchored in Jordan’s Economic Modernization Vision (EMV). The MASAR Operation is designed to support the Ministry of Education and Human Resources Development in addressing foundational bottlenecks in access, quality, and relevance of education, with a dual emphasis on equity and efficiency. The operation aims to strengthen institutional capacity while enabling measurable improvements in learning outcomes and employability, particularly through early childhood education and labor market-aligned technical and vocational education and training (TVET), and digital transformation in education.

The program became effective in 2024, with a total financing envelope of USD 400 million, supported by the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD). It comprises two core components:

  1. Program-for-Results (PforR): the principal financing instrument that disburses against verified achievement of results tied to government reform priorities.
  2. Investment Project Financing (IPF): a complementary technical assistance (TA) component aimed at supporting the implementation of system-strengthening activities and accelerating the achievement of Disbursement Linked Indicators (DLIs).

MASAR is structured around four interlinked Results Areas (RAs) that are strategically aligned with key education-sector transition points and cross-cutting governance reforms:

  • RA1: Home to School – Expanding Access to Foundational Learning. This includes (i) increasing equitable access to KG2, particularly in under-served districts and refugee-hosting communities; (ii) enhancing the quality of early childhood education through a revised KG1-KG2 curriculum and quality assurance mechanisms; and (iii) improving foundational literacy skills for Grades 1–3 through targeted pedagogical interventions and a comprehensive implementation plan.
  • RA2: School to Work – Increasing Access to Labor Market-Relevant TVET. MASAR seeks to improve the alignment of TVET with private sector needs by institutionalizing public-private partnerships, scaling apprenticeships, and expanding career guidance and employment pathways. This is complemented by the operationalization of an equivalency system that supports the portability and recognition of TVET qualifications, and enhanced use of learner trajectory data to inform student support services.
  • RA3: Strengthening Sector Governance and Efficiency. The program supports the operationalization of a restructured governance model for the education sector and introduces reforms to human resource management, with a particular focus on teacher recruitment, deployment, and professional development policies.
  • RA4: Digital Transformation in Education, to be introduced through the MASAR Additional Financing (AF), supporting digital and AI-enabled learning for students in Grades 4-12 and strengthening the institutional infrastructure needed for national-scale technology integration in education.

In addition to its core education objectives, MASAR embeds environmental and social sustainability principles across its implementation.

Ultimately, MASAR is designed to deliver measurable, inclusive, and sustainable improvements in Jordan’s education system. It expands access to early learning, strengthens foundational skills, improves graduate employability, strengthens digital skills, technology-enabled learning, and future-ready competencies, and reinforces institutional coherence through evidence-based policymaking. By supporting inclusive education and strengthening school-to-work transitions, the program directly contributes to Jordan’s long-term economic resilience and human capital development agenda.

Objectives of the Assignment:

The objective of this assignment is to provide strategic and operational support for the implementation of MASAR Result Area 4 (Digital Transformation in Education) and the coordination of MoE's digital education transformation portfolio, ensuring achievement of RA4 DLRs, alignment with national reform priorities, effective inter-institutional and donor coordination, and timely delivery of evidence required for programme verification and disbursement.

The Senior Coordinator will support operational follow-up, troubleshoot bottlenecks, monitor implementation against annual work plans, coordinate GFPP-financed preparatory activities, and contribute to institutionalizing sustainable digital education governance, EdTech implementation capacity, child-safe and inclusive digital learning standards, and cross-government coordination mechanisms within MoE systems.

Specifically, the Senior Coordinator will:

  • Lead MASAR RA4 preparation and implementation, driving progress against DLR 8.1-8.5 milestones and ensuring that technical assistance, procurement, capacity building, and institutional arrangements are sequenced to deliver required results on time.
  • Serve as the coordination focal point responsible for tracking, consolidating, and supporting delivery of RA4-related DLRs and associated verification evidence.
  • Coordinate GFPP-financed preparation activities so that technical assessments, pilots, PIU establishment, EdTech and AI Hub readiness, knowledge exchange, and capacity building directly inform the MASAR AF design and first-year implementation readiness.
  • Coordinate the digital education donor and partner portfolio, to ensure strategic alignment with the Education Strategic Plan, the National Education Sector Strategy, the EMV, and MASAR AF priorities while preventing duplication across programmes.
  • Produce regular, analytically rigorous RA4 and digital education portfolio progress reporting for DCU leadership, MASAR operational program manager, and relevant government counterparts.
  • Identify unresourced digital transformation priority areas and support resource mobilization and partner alignment.

Scope of Work

  1. MASAR RA4 Planning and Implementation
  • Develop, update, and closely monitor annual action plans for RA4, ensuring alignment with MASAR’s overall results framework, DLR timelines, and MoE priorities.
  • Break activities into operational tasks with clear milestones, dependencies, and responsible units.
  • Support the preparation and review of annual work plans, budgets, and implementation schedules to ensure timely delivery of programme results.
  • Conduct periodic implementation reviews and recommend adjustments to activities, sequencing, resource allocation, and technical assistance arrangements to maintain progress toward DLR achievement.
  • Provide regular progress reports against implementation for result area 4 workplan under MASAR, including the preparation of MASAR's bi-annual progress reports.
  • Support the preparation and quality review of ToRs for RA4 consultancies and contracts, including connectivity assessments, device pilots, EdTech technical assistance, AI governance, digital content development, cybersecurity, data privacy, and M&E assignments.

Digital Education Portfolio Coordination and Partner Alignment

  • Maintain and analyse a Digital Education Projects Matrix as a strategic portfolio management tool, identifying gaps, duplication risks, sequencing challenges, and opportunities for synergies across interventions.
  • Advise DCU and MASAR leadership on the prioritisation, alignment, endorsement, modification, and coordination of Digital Transformation initiatives to support implementation of the Education Strategic Plan (ESP) and national reform priorities.
  • Screen new digital education, EdTech, AI, connectivity, content, teacher training, and device-related proposals for alignment with RA4 DLRs, existing interventions, MoE standards, and donor investments.
  • Facilitate division-of-labour arrangements among development partners and stakeholders, ensuring clarity of roles, responsibilities, expected results, and implementation timelines.
  • Identify un-resourced Digital Education priority areas and support resource mobilisation efforts through engagement with development partners and relevant stakeholders.
  • Maintain cluster meeting records and action trackers; ensure follow-through on agreed actions between meetings.
  • Serve as the focal point for the Google Chromebook project.
  1. Stakeholder Coordination and Representation
  • Serve as the primary coordination focal point for digital transformation reforms, ensuring effective collaboration among Ministry directorates, development partners, implementing agencies, and other stakeholders.
  • Coordinate regularly with relevant MoE directorates and external stakeholders to ensure clarity of roles, timelines, and expected contributions.
  • Participate in technical committees, working groups, task teams, and workshops, providing inputs and ensuring follow-up on agreed actions.
  • Attend all MASAR supervision missions as the RA4 technical focal point.
  • Represent DCU’s coordination mandate at all Digital Transformation technical working groups and maintain proactive, technically substantive relationships with implementing agencies including UN agencies, development partners, private sector technology firms, telecom providers, universities, and others, as needed.
  1. Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification
  • Track all RA4-relevant MASAR DLRs and maintain a real-time DLR risk register; flag at-risk DLRs to the Program Manager and DCU Leadership with sufficient lead time for corrective action.
  • Monitor implementation progress across the broader digital transformation portfolio, maintaining oversight of milestones, deliverables, risks, dependencies, and corrective actions
  • Coordinate the preparation, consolidation, and quality assurance of DLR verification evidence, ensuring compliance with agreed verification protocols and readiness for independent verification reviews.
  • Review Verification reports submitted by the verification agency for the DLRs under result area 4.
  • Support monitoring, evaluation, reporting, verification, and learning requirements across digital transformation-related donor-funded programmes, ensuring timely provision of data, performance information, and evidence in accordance with donor requirements.
  • Support supervision missions, evaluations, audits, verification exercises, and technical assessments by ensuring data readiness and facilitating access to relevant information and stakeholders.
  1. Risk Management and Troubleshooting
  • Identify implementation risks, bottlenecks, and systemic constraints affecting RA4 and the broader digital transformation portfolio.
  • Provide timely solutions or mitigation measures and engage relevant directorates to resolve issues.
  • Escalate critical challenges to the Program Manager and DCU Deputy Director with clear problem statements and recommended actions.
  1. Knowledge Management and Institutional Strengthening
  • Facilitate knowledge exchange across MoE directorates and donor partners, ensuring that lessons learned, technical guidance, and best practices are captured and shared.
  • Support capacity-building efforts related to EdTech program management, digital pedagogy, AI-supported teaching, digital content development, school connectivity, device management, cybersecurity, data privacy, and DLR verification.
  • Promote institutionalization of MASAR RA4 processes and DCU digital transformation coordination mechanisms within MoE systems to strengthen long-term sustainability.
  • Document lessons from pilots and knowledge exchanges and ensure that they inform implementation manuals, technical standards, procurement documents, and training packages.

Duration and Location

Contract duration is 1 year with possible extension based on performance and availability of funding.

Full-time presence is required. The Senior Coordinator will be based at the Ministry of Education and Human Resources Development, Amman, Jordan.

Required Qualifications and Experience

  • Education: A bachelor's degree in Education, Digital Education, ICT, Computer Science, Public Policy, Economics, Development Studies, Engineering, or a related field. A master's degree is preferred, particularly in education policy, digital transformation, educational technology, public
  • Experience: At least 10 years of progressively responsible experience in education sector reform, digital transformation, EdTech implementation, programme management, or donor coordination, including at least 5 years in a leadership or coordination role involving multiple stakeholders.
  • Technical Skills: Deep understanding of digital education systems, school connectivity, device deployment, digital content, teacher digital pedagogy, AI-enabled education tools, data privacy, cybersecurity, child online protection, accessibility, and inclusive technology design. Strong background in results-based management, including work planning, monitoring progress, tracking indicators, maintaining risk registers, and preparing progress reports. Experience with PforR, DLI/DLR-based programmes, World Bank operations, or large-scale public-sector technology programs is a strong advantage. Familiarity with Jordan's education sector, digital government architecture, and the Economic Modernization Vision is desirable.
  • Stakeholder Engagement and Communication: Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with a proven ability to engage and coordinate government officials, development partners, UN agencies, and private-sector stakeholders. Experience in facilitating workshops, leading working groups, and achieving consensus among diverse actors. Fluency in English and Arabic is required.
  • Political Economy and Organisational Skills: Strong political economy awareness with the ability to navigate complex multi-donor environments diplomatically. Self-driven, results-oriented, and capable of managing multiple simultaneous work streams. Demonstrated ability to produce high-quality, decision-ready briefings for senior leadership and meet tight deadlines.

Reporting and Institutional Arrangements

The Senior Coordinator shall report administratively to the MASAR Operational Program Manager and maintain a technical reporting line to the DCU Deputy Director for portfolio coordination functions. For day-to-day operations, the Senior Coordinator will work closely with designated focal points in the Ministry of Education and Human Resources Development, the World Bank task team, Digital Transformation donor programme teams, and DLR task team leaders as primary counterparts.

Submission 

Interested candidates are invited to submit their resume and any relevant certifications by the deadline specified in the announcement on the Ministry’s website, to the following email address: A.Orabi@moej.edu.jo 
Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for an interview.
