Reference No.:  JO-MOE-566808-CS-INDV

Program Background:

The Modernizing Education, Skills, and Administrative Reforms (MASAR) Program for Results (PforR) is a transformative, system-wide reform initiative anchored in Jordan’s Economic Modernization Vision (EMV). The MASAR Operation is designed to support the Ministry of Education and Human Resources Development in addressing foundational bottlenecks in access, quality, and relevance of education, with a dual emphasis on equity and efficiency. The operation aims to strengthen institutional capacity while enabling measurable improvements in learning outcomes and employability, particularly through early childhood education and labor market-aligned technical and vocational education and training (TVET), and digital transformation in education.

The program became effective in 2024, with a total financing envelope of USD 400 million, supported by the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD). It comprises two core components:

  1. Program-for-Results (PforR): the principal financing instrument that disburses against verified achievement of results tied to government reform priorities.
  2. Investment Project Financing (IPF): a complementary technical assistance (TA) component aimed at supporting the implementation of system-strengthening activities and accelerating the achievement of Disbursement Linked Indicators (DLIs).

MASAR is structured around four interlinked Results Areas (RAs) that are strategically aligned with key education-sector transition points and cross-cutting governance reforms:

  • RA1: Home to School – Expanding Access to Foundational Learning. This includes (i) increasing equitable access to KG2, particularly in under-served districts and refugee-hosting communities; (ii) enhancing the quality of early childhood education through a revised KG1-KG2 curriculum and quality assurance mechanisms; and (iii) improving foundational literacy skills for Grades 1–3 through targeted pedagogical interventions and a comprehensive implementation plan.
  • RA2: School to Work – Increasing Access to Labor Market-Relevant TVET. MASAR seeks to improve the alignment of TVET with private sector needs by institutionalizing public-private partnerships, scaling apprenticeships, and expanding career guidance and employment pathways. This is complemented by the operationalization of an equivalency system that supports the portability and recognition of TVET qualifications, and enhanced use of learner trajectory data to inform student support services.
  • RA3: Strengthening Sector Governance and Efficiency. The program supports the operationalization of a restructured governance model for the education sector and introduces reforms to human resource management, with a particular focus on teacher recruitment, deployment, and professional development policies.
  • RA4: Digital Transformation in Education, to be introduced through the MASAR Additional Financing (AF), supporting digital and AI-enabled learning for students in Grades 4-12 and strengthening the institutional infrastructure needed for national-scale technology integration in education.

In addition to its core education objectives, MASAR embeds environmental and social sustainability principles across its implementation.

Ultimately, MASAR is designed to deliver measurable, inclusive, and sustainable improvements in Jordan’s education system. It expands access to early learning, strengthens foundational skills, improves graduate employability, strengthens digital skills, technology-enabled learning, and future-ready competencies, and reinforces institutional coherence through evidence-based policymaking. By supporting inclusive education and strengthening school-to-work transitions, the program directly contributes to Jordan’s long-term economic resilience and human capital development agenda.

Objectives of the Assignment:

The objective of this assignment is to provide strategic and operational support for the implementation of MASAR Result Area 2 and the coordination of the implementation of other projects supporting the Ministry of Education and Human Resource Development’s TVET development portfolio, ensuring achievement of Disbursement Linked Results (DLRs), alignment with national reform priorities, effective donor coordination, and timely delivery of evidence required for programme verification and disbursement.

The Senior Coordinator will support operational follow-up, troubleshoot bottlenecks, monitor implementation against the Annual Work Plan, and contribute to institutionalizing sustainable TVET governance, labour market alignment, and donor coordination mechanisms within MoE systems.

Specifically, the Senior Coordinator will:

  • Lead MASAR RA2 implementation, driving progress against all DLR milestones and ensuring that TA inputs are sequenced to deliver required results on time.
  • Serve as the coordination focal point responsible for tracking, consolidating, and supporting delivery of all RA2-related DLRs and associated verification evidence.
  • Support the timely achievement of MASAR DLRs by facilitating coordination and sequencing across relevant donor-supported programmes, ensuring that required inputs are aligned with DLR timelines.
  • Coordinate the DCU’s full TVET donor portfolio, ensuring strategic alignment with the ESP 2026–2030 and preventing duplication across programmes, to prevent misalignment between parallel donor interventions through structured division-of-labour processes.
  • Produce regular, analytically rigorous TVET portfolio and RA2 progress reporting for DCU leadership and MASAR operational program management
  • Identify portfolio gaps for unresourced TVET priority areas.

Scope of Work

  1. MASAR RA2 Planning and Implementation
  • Develop, update, and closely monitor annual action plans for RA2, ensuring alignment with MASAR’s overall results framework, DLR timelines, and MoE priorities.
  • Break activities into operational tasks with clear milestones, dependencies, and responsible units.
  • Support the preparation and review of annual work plans, budgets, and implementation schedules to ensure timely delivery of programme results.
  • Conduct periodic implementation reviews and recommend adjustments to activities, sequencing, resource allocation, and technical assistance arrangements to maintain progress toward DLR achievement.
  • Provide regular progress reports against implementation for result area 2 workplan under MASAR, including the preparation of MASAR's bi-annual progress reports.
  • Supports the Managing Director of TVET at MoE in the preparation of TORs for activities identified in the workplan
  1. TVET Portfolio Coordination and Donor Alignment
  • Maintain and analyse the TVET Projects Matrix as a strategic portfolio management tool, identifying gaps, duplication risks, sequencing challenges, and opportunities for synergies across interventions.
  • Advise DCU leadership on the prioritisation, alignment, endorsement, modification, and coordination of TVET initiatives to support implementation of the Education Strategic Plan (ESP) and national reform priorities.
  • Screen new TVET programme proposals and assess their alignment with sector priorities, existing interventions, and donor investments.
  • Facilitate division-of-labour arrangements among development partners and stakeholders, ensuring clarity of roles, responsibilities, expected results, and implementation timelines.
  • Identify un-resourced TVET priority areas and support resource mobilisation efforts through engagement with development partners and relevant stakeholders.
  • Provide regular progress reports against implementation of the DCU’s full TVET donor portfolio.
  • Maintain cluster meeting records and action trackers; ensure follow-through on agreed actions between meetings.
  1. Stakeholder Coordination and Representation
  • Serve as the primary coordination focal point for TVET-related reforms, ensuring effective collaboration among Ministry directorates, development partners, implementing agencies, and other stakeholders.
  • Coordinate regularly with relevant MoE directorates and external stakeholders to ensure clarity of roles, timelines, and expected contributions.
  • Participate in technical committees, working groups, task teams, and workshops, providing inputs and ensuring follow-up on agreed actions.
  • Attend all MASAR supervision missions as the DCU TVET/RA2 technical focal point.
  • Represent DCU’s coordination mandate at all TVET technical working groups and maintain proactive, technically substantive relationships with implementing agencies including UNESCO, ILO, GIZ, and others.
  1. Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification
  • Track all TVET-relevant MASAR DLRs and maintain a real-time DLR risk register; flag at-risk DLRs to the Program Manager and DCU Leadership with sufficient lead time for corrective action.
  • Monitor implementation progress across the broader TVET portfolio, maintaining oversight of milestones, deliverables, risks, dependencies, and corrective actions
  • Coordinate the preparation, consolidation, and quality assurance of DLR verification evidence, ensuring compliance with agreed verification protocols and readiness for independent verification reviews.
  • Review Verification reports submitted by the verification agency for the DLRs under result area 2.
  • Support monitoring, evaluation, reporting, verification, and learning requirements across TVET-related donor-funded programmes, ensuring timely provision of data, performance information, and evidence in accordance with donor requirements.
  • Support supervision missions, evaluations, audits, verification exercises, and technical assessments by ensuring data readiness and facilitating access to relevant information and stakeholders.
  1. Risk Management and Troubleshooting
  • Identify implementation risks, bottlenecks, and systemic constraints affecting RA2 and the broader TVET portfolio.
  • Provide timely solutions or mitigation measures and engage relevant directorates to resolve issues.
  • Escalate critical challenges to the Operational Program Manager and DCU Deputy Director with clear problem statements and recommended actions.
  1. Knowledge Management and Institutional Strengthening
  • Facilitate knowledge exchange across MoE directorates and donor partners, ensuring that lessons learned, technical guidance, and best practices are captured and shared.
  • Support capacity-building efforts related to TVET programme delivery, labour market alignment, and TVET qualification equivalency systems.
  • Promote institutionalization of MASAR RA2 processes and DCU TVET coordination mechanisms within MoE systems to strengthen long-term sustainability.

Duration and Location

Contract duration is 1 year with possible extension based on performance and availability of funding.

Full-time presence is required. The Senior Coordinator will be based at the Ministry of Education and Human Resource Development, Amman, Jordan

Required Qualifications and Experience

  • Education: A bachelor’s degree in Education, Public Policy, TVET, Economics, Development Studies, or a related field. A Master’s degree is preferred, particularly in education policy, international development, or labour market economics.
  • Experience: At least 10 years of progressively responsible experience in education sector reform, TVET systems development, programme management, or donor coordination, including at least 5 years in a leadership or coordination role involving multiple stakeholders.
  • Technical Skills: Deep knowledge of TVET systems, governance, qualifications frameworks, and labour market linkages. Strong background in results-based management, including developing work plans, monitoring progress, tracking indicators, and preparing progress reports. Experience with Programme for Results (PforR) or DLI-based programmes is a strong advantage. Familiarity with Jordan’s education sector, TVET system, and the Economic Modernisation Vision is desirable.
  • Stakeholder Engagement and Communication: Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with a proven ability to engage and coordinate government officials, development partners, UN agencies, and private-sector stakeholders. Experience in facilitating workshops, leading working groups, and achieving consensus among diverse actors. Fluency in English and Arabic is required.
  • Political Economy and Organisational Skills: Strong political economy awareness with the ability to navigate complex multi-donor environments diplomatically. Self-driven, results-oriented, and capable of managing multiple simultaneous work streams. Demonstrated ability to produce high-quality, decision-ready briefings for senior leadership and meet tight deadlines.

Reporting and Institutional Arrangements

The Senior Coordinator shall report administratively to the MASAR Program Operational Manager maintain a technical reporting line to the DCU Deputy Director for portfolio coordination functions. For day-to-day operations, the Senior Coordinator will work closely with designated focal points in the Ministry of Education and Human Resource Development, the World Bank task team, TVET donor programme teams, and DLR task team leaders as primary counterparts.

Submission 

Interested candidates are invited to submit their resume and any relevant certifications by the deadline specified in the announcement on the Ministry’s website, to the following email address: a.abumtawea@moej.edu.jo
Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for an interview.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL SELECTION)

 

 

REPUBLIC OF ARMENIA

RESILAND: Armenia Resilient Landscape Project

Grant No.: P179988

Assignment Title: Procurement Specialist

Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): AM-EPIU-566921-CS-INDV

 

The Republic of Armenia has received financing has received financing from the World Bank (the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (“IBRD”), acting as an Implementing Agency of the Global Environment Facility (“GEF”) and as administrator of the Multi-Donor Trust Fund for Supporting Armenia Resilient Landscapes Project and International Development Association (“IDA”), acting as administrator of the Multi-Donor Trust Fund for Supporting Armenia Resilient Landscapes Project) toward the cost of the RESILAND: Armenia Resilient Landscape Project, and intends to apply part of the proceeds for individual consulting services.

 

The main objective of the Procurement Specialist is to implement and coordinate all procurement procedures for procurement activities under the Project. The Procurement Specialist shall be responsible for the efficient and timely procurement of Works, Goods, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services.

 

The duration of the assignment/contract: The Procurement Specialist will be hired for the initial period of 1 year. Procurement Specialist’s performance will be assessed, and the contract might be extended annually (for each additional year) based on satisfactory performance. The Procurement Specialist is expected to remain engaged throughout the entire Project implementation timeframe/period.

 

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment are attached to this request for expressions of interest in Annex 1.

 

The Environmental Project Implementation Unit now invites eligible Individual Consultants to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Individual Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

 

The Qualifications criteria are:

  • University-level degree in engineering, finance, economics, business administration, law, procurement, or related discipline;
  • At least 5 years of professional experience as a procurement and/or contract management specialist;
  • Experience in managing procurement under World Bank financed projects, or projects financed by other international financial institutions would be considered as an advantage;
  • Understanding of and experience with World Bank Procurement Regulations, procurement procedures and Systematic Tracking of Exchanges in Procurement (STEP) portal, will be considered an advantage;
  • Good interpersonal and communication skill;
  • Fluent knowledge of the English language;
  • Demonstrated ability to work in a team;
  • Computer literacy (MS Office).

 

 

The attention of interested Individual Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

 

An Individual Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Selection of Individual Consultant (Section V) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

 

Interested candidates are invited to submit their CV highlighting relevant experience and education, along with contact details of at least two professional references, to: resiland.epiu@gmail.com , clearly indicating the vacancy title “Procurement Specialist / RESILAND Armenia” in the subject line. Supporting documents (e.g., educational certificates) may be requested from shortlisted candidates at a later stage. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

The Evaluation Committee may invite the highest-ranked candidates, based on the assessment of their CVs, to participate in an interview prior to finalizing the evaluation results. Interviews may be conducted in person or through remote communication tools (e.g., telephone or video conference), as agreed with the candidate. The date and time of the interview will be communicated to the candidate at least five (5) calendar days in advance. If a candidate is unable to participate in the scheduled interview due to justified reasons, the Client may, at its discretion, agree on an alternative date and time. Failure to participate in the rescheduled interview may result in disqualification from the evaluation process. Any costs associated with participation in the interview shall be borne by the candidate.

 

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours (09:00-18:00).

 

Expressions of interest / CVs in English must be delivered via e-mail NO later than November 3, 2026, 18:00 (local time).

 

Environmental Project Implementation Unit

Attn: Armen Yesoyan (Acting Director of EPIU)

65A Tigran Mets Ave., 3rd fl.

Yerevan 0008, Armenia

Tel: +374 96 693 911

E-mail: resiland.epiu@gmail.com

 

ANNEX 1

 

 

 

RESILAND: ARMENIA RESILIENT LANDSCAPES PROJECT (P179988)

 

TERMS OF REFERENCE

for

PROCUREMENT SPECIALIST

 

  1.  Introduction and Background

The objectives of the RESILAND: Armenia Resilient Landscape Project are: (i) to increase the area under sustainable landscape management in Selected Locations and (ii) to promote sustainable economic activities to communities in Targeted Landscapes in Armenia. RESLAND Armenia follows an integrated landscapes approach to restore forests and wetlands and will rely on four key issues: (i) reduction of forest fragmentation and increase in density of tree cover by restoring the forest land degraded due to mining and by forest enrichment planting; (ii) improving management of neglected and abandoned wetlands, (iii) increasing community economic  benefits, and (iv) strengthen the institutional foundation for the sustainable management of landscapes, creating green jobs, and increasing community benefits. Project activities are grouped into four interrelated components and their respective subcomponents. Under its main three components, the project will finance consulting services, non-consulting services, goods, equipment, training, workshops, as well as small works.

       The Project  four Components include:

        Component 1: Institutional Capacity and Policy Development.

        Component 2: Landscape Restoration        

        Component 3: Promoting Communities Benefits.            

        Component 4: Project Management, Monitoring & Evaluation, and Communication.

2. Project Implementation Arrangements

The Environmental Project Implementation Unit (EPIU), a State agency under the Ministry of Environment, will provide overall management of the Project preparation activities aimed at achievement of the planned results. 

3. Objectives of the assignment

The main objective of the Procurement Specialist is to implement and coordinate all procurement procedures for procurement activities under the Project. The Procurement Specialist shall be responsible for the efficient and timely procurement of Works, Goods, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services.

4. Scope of Work

In order to achieve the objective, the Procurement Specialist shall:

4.1 Perform a variety of procurement activities including preparation of procurement documents, announcement, evaluation, contracting;

 4.2 Identify procurement arrangements based on Projects’ particular circumstances, market analysis, risks and operating context;

 4.3 Prepare and update Projects’ Procurement Plans and Project Procurement Strategy for Development on as needed basis, in close cooperation with the EPIU’s Management and Project Coordinator;

 4.4 Ensure the procurement of Goods, Works, Non-consulting Services and Consulting Services are handled in accordance with the World Bank procurement procedures and Procurement Regulations, dated September 2023;

 4.5 For prior and post review contracts, prepare all sorts of procurement documents using SPD (Standard Procurement Documents), or other bidding documents as agreed in advance with the World Bank, for Works, Goods, Non-consulting and Consulting Services. Review the completeness of the procurement documents before submission through STEP (Systemic Tracking of Exchanges in Procurement) system;

 4.6 Carry out pre-bid meetings, prepare clarifications and/or amendments of bidding documents and minutes of the pre-bid meetings, and make sure such are equally available to all bidders;

 4.7 Carry out pre-proposal conferences; prepare clarifications and/or amendments of requests for proposals and minutes of the pre-proposal conferences, on as needed basis; 

 4.8 Carry out bid opening procedures and prepare bid opening minutes;

 4.9 Carry out technical and financial proposals opening procedures and prepare minutes of proposal opening, on as needed basis; Prepare bid evaluation reports for procurement of Goods, Works, and Non-consulting Services. Prepare requests for clarifications of bids, and provide clarifications to the World Bank’s comments as the case may be;

 4.10 On as needed basis, prepare shortlist evaluation reports and technical/financial proposals evaluation reports, prepare requests for clarifications of proposals - for RFP other than for Consulting Services, and provide clarifications to the World Bank’s comments as the case may be;

4.11 Prepare Notification of Intention to Award the Contract to the bidders, proposers and consultants; and prepare award notices/acceptance letters to selected bidders and consultants, on as needed basis;

4.12 Carry out contract negotiations with the selected consultants, proposers and bidders on as needed basis;

4.13 For prior and post review cases too, as soon as such case is identified and before proceeding with negotiations with the successful bidder/proposer as per article 5.61 of the Procurement Regulations (of September 2023 or later version), inform the Bank of such decision, with all supporting information and basis for such decision;

4.14 Prepare final set of contract documents for Goods, Works, Consulting and Non-consulting Services for signature by the parties;

4.15 Provide recommendations to the Project team on proposed contract variations/amendments for Goods, Works, Consulting and Non-consulting Services;

4.16 Prepare contract variations/amendments for Goods, Works, and Non-consulting Services;

4.17 Prepare amendments to the Consultancy contracts;

4.18 Participate in customs procedures for procured Goods, if applicable; participate in acceptance and hand-over of goods procured - as the case may be;

4.19 Ensure procurement filing accurately and in a timely manner;

4.20 Ensure timely publication of procurement notices and advertisement as well as awarded contracts;

4.21 Register and update procurement information in the EPIU’s internal systems;

4.22 Register and upload necessary procurement information in the Client-Treasury system to ensure relevant contract management;

4.23 Use STEP system, for all type of procurements – for all prior and post review contracts on regular basis. Update all information in STEP from planning to payment. Assist in contract administration, which includes, inter alia, monitoring of: contract dates, guarantees, insurance policies, deliverables, etc.;

4.24 Update contract monitoring report in Bank format (for all contracts, including high value contracts – if any) at quarterly basis and share the report to Bank;

4.25 Assist audit processes, review findings and implementing changes;

4.26 Support/review the preparation of the technical specifications, BOQs, TORs, Employer’s Requirements etc. of the bidding / procurement documents (RFPs, RFBs, RFQs, REOIs) and ensure the consistency of these sections with the other sections of the bidding / procurement documents and make necessary recommendations for changes or make the changes where required;

4.27 Prepare response to the complaints of the bidders if any;

4.28 Prepare debriefing letters to unsuccessful bidders/consultants, and participate in debriefing meetings, if applicable;

4.29 Prepare procurement related reports at the request of the Project Coordinator;

4.30 Assist EPIU in the implementation and monitoring of contracts, in establishing good document filing system and in providing contract information for disbursement needs;

4.31 Undertake training of EPIU staff for the World Bank procurement procedures;

4.32 Conduct other procurement activities entrusted by EPIU.

SADC REGIONAL STATISTICS PROJECT (P175731)

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT SELECTION)

COUNTRY: São Tomé and Príncipe

PROJECT: SADC Regional Statistics Project (PER)

Consultancy Title: Recruitment of one (1) Specialist for the Calculation of the Consumer Price Index (CPI)

Reference No.: 54/C-STP/PER/2026

The Government of the Democratic Republic of São Tomé and Príncipe, through the Ministry of Economy and Finance, has received financing from the International Development Association (IDA) to support the implementation of the SADC Regional Statistics Project (PER), and intends to use part of these funds to procure consulting services.

The consulting service consists of recruiting one (1) Specialist for the Calculation of the Consumer Price Index (CPI).

Objectives of the Consultancy

The main objectives of the consultancy are:

a) To review, process, validate and compile the data collected in all districts of the country, including the Autonomous Region of Príncipe.

b) To calculate the new Consumer Price Index (CPI) weights and assess the price data collected for calculating prices for the base year, within the framework of the Household Budget Survey (IOF-2026).

The Terms of Reference (ToR) may be requested by email at the following addresses:

sadc.procurement@afap.st / dg.procurement@afap.st

The Project Administration Fiduciary Agency (AFAP) invites eligible individual consultants (Consultants) to express their interest in providing the services by submitting a Letter of Intent, an identity document, an updated and signed Curriculum Vitae (CV), and the relevant evidence of academic qualifications.

Interested consultants must provide information demonstrating that they have the qualifications and experience required to perform the services, in accordance with the Terms of Reference (ToR).

The Consultant must possess the following minimum qualifications:

  1. Academic Qualifications
  • A Master’s degree or equivalent qualification in statistics, mathematics or economics, with a focus on the production of statistical data, specifically price data analysis.

2. Professional Experience

  • Between 5 and 10 years of professional experience in the relevant university-trained field.
  • At least five (5) years of professional consulting experience in price data analysis.
  •  At least ten (10) years of cumulative professional experience in processing, compiling and analysing price data.

3. Technical Skills

  • Demonstrated knowledge and experience of the implications of their work in the implementation of World Bank projects.
  •  Good command of computer tools, including specialised software (PHOENIX) for entering, processing and calculating the Consumer Price Index (CPI).
  • Proficiency in statistical software (Stata, SPSS, R, SAS) and good command of Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint and other computer tools.

4. Language Skills

  • Knowledge of Portuguese, preferably, both written and spoken, or French.

Interested Consultants are referred to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, September 2025 edition, which sets out the World Bank’s policy on conflicts of interest.

The selection will be conducted using the Individual Consultant Selection (ICS) method, as provided for in the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, September 2025 edition.

Further information may be obtained at the address below during office hours, from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.

Expressions of interest must be submitted by 23:45 p.m. (local time in São Tomé and Príncipe) on 03 November 2026, by email to dg.procurement@afap.st / sadc.procurement@afap.st, or delivered in person to the address indicated below, quoting the following reference:

PROJECT ID: 165557

 

PROCUREMENT OF CONSULTANCY SERVICES (FIRMS)

 

BACKGROUND

The Government of Ghana, under World Bank and Global Partnership for Education (GPE) funding, is supporting the government’s education strategic plan to improve equitable access to quality basic education in Ghana. The Ghana Accountability for Learning Outcomes Project (GALOP), approved for an amount of USD 218.7 million, has the Project Development Objective (PDO) to improve the quality of education in low-performing basic education schools and to strengthen education sector equity and accountability in Ghana. The GALOP was originally implemented over a five-year period from Jan 2020 to Dec 2024. However, the parent project has been extended to close by 31st December 2026 and the Ministry has received a second additional financing (AF 2) totaling $118.8m to scale up successful interventions from the parent project to be implemented by 31st December 2028.

The Government of Ghana has recently secured funds from the World Bank (USD 300 million) for the Ministry of Education to implement the Second Education Transformation for Access, Relevance and Results for Jobs Project (STARR-J), with the PDO to expand access to, and improve the quality and relevance of, secondary education in Ghana. The Project focuses on expanding infrastructure and opportunities for underserved students, strengthening teaching and learning (especially in STEM and competency-based training), modernizing technical and vocational systems, and aligning education outcomes with skills demanded by employers, ultimately helping students transition more successfully into further education or decent work.

BACKGROUND

The Government of Ghana, under World Bank and Global Partnership for Education (GPE) funding, is supporting the government’s education strategic plan to improve equitable access to quality basic education in Ghana. The Ghana Accountability for Learning Outcomes Project (GALOP), approved for an amount of USD 218.7 million, has the Project Development Objective (PDO) to improve the quality of education in low-performing basic education schools and to strengthen education sector equity and accountability in Ghana. data.title: This activity will support development of Project Operations manual and related materials
data.project_name: GFPP for Promoting Participation and Enhancing Learning (PROPEL) Botswana
data.institution: Ministry of Child Welfare and Basic Education
data.notice_text:
TheGovernmentofBotswana(GoB) is undertaking the Promoting Participation and Enhancing Learning (PROPEL) (P513800) project supported by the World Bank (WB).  

The Project Development Objective (PDO) is to increase participation in preprimary and senior secondary education and improve learning conditions in supported schools, particularly at the junior secondary level. The Project consists of the following four components: 

  • Component 1: Increasing participation in education 
  • Component 2: Enhancing the learning environment 
  • Component 3: Strengthening system capacity for quality education service delivery 
  • Component 4: Project management and implementation support 

 

The Ministry of Child Welfare and Basic Education (MCWBE) is the implementing entity for the Project. AProject Delivery Unit (PDU)(or Program Coordinating Unit) is being  establishedwithin MCWBE to support the effective implementation of project activities, including procurement and contract administration; monitoring, evaluation and reporting of progress under the project; fiduciary management; and environmental and social safeguards management. Specifically, the PDU will be responsible for preparing the Project Operations Manual (POM) to guide the implementation of the project. The MCWBE seeks to engage an Individual Consultant to support the preparation of the POM.

 

The objective of this assignment is to support the PDU in the development and finalization of the POM to clearly describe how the project will be implemented to achieve the expected development objectives and outcomes.

 

The POM is expected to be the key document which describes the structure of the project and the many stakeholders that are going to be involved in its implementation, including defining the roles and responsibilities of the various stakeholders under each component and sub-component and clarifying the implementation arrangements for all the components and sub-components.

 

The POM should include (i) detailed description of Project activities; (ii) the specific roles and responsibilities of the Project Steering Committee (PSC), PDU, and other entities participating in the implementation of the project and the arrangements for ensuring coordination among them; (iii) arrangements on fiduciary matters, including financial management, audit, and procurement; (iv) institutional administration coordination and day to day execution of project activities; (v) selection criteria and modalities for technical assistance in project supported activities; (vi) monitoring and evaluation; (vii) reporting arrangements; (viii) social and environmental safeguards requirements and procedures; and (ix) other technical and organizational arrangements and procedures as shall be required for the Project.

 

The POM will be organized or structured as follows:

 

  • Section 1 will describe the Project Context. This will include a brief background to the development of the project; state the Project Development Objective (PDO) and the indicators that will be used to measure progress towards the achievement of the objective; clarify the project target beneficiaries; and define the scope of the project.
  • Section 2 will discuss implementation arrangements by components, sub-components and activities of the project. It will include detailed implementation plan (IP) for each activity under the sub-components with clear selection criteria for specific activities. This will also include a detailed section on implementation modalities for activities related to civil-works and community driven development.
  • Section 3 will describe the institutional administrative and implementation arrangements of the project by entity-roles, attributions and responsibilities.
  • Section 4 will discuss the Monitoring and Evaluation Framework and the data collection arrangements to effectively measure project results and communicate them to the project stakeholders.
  • Section 5 will clarify the roles and responsibilities related to the financial management arrangements of the project, including the fiduciary responsibilities, reporting requirements, disbursement arrangements and financial controls and auditing of the project.
  • Section 6 will expand on the procurement management and guiding principles. This will also include updating the procurement plan and preparation of Annual Work Plans and Budget (AWPB).
  • Section 7 will discuss social and environmental safeguards requirements and procedures.
  • Section 8 will discuss Grievance Redress Mechanisms, (GRM), Citizen’s Engagement, Gender and Climate actions. 
  • Section 9 will discuss the communication plan for the project.
  • Section 10 will discuss training and capacity building plan under the project.
  • Section 11 will discuss other provisions.

 

The Consultant shall deliver the following products:

 

  • Outline of the Project Operations Manual.
  • Draft version of the POM
  • Final version of the POM

 

The assignment is planned for up to 3 months between November 2026 and January 2027 and the expected level of efforts is 35 working days. The initial two (2) weeks will be earmarked for the outline of the POM, six (6) weeks for the draft version of the POM and the last four (4) weeks for the final version of the POM.

 

The consultant will report to the Project Coordinator at the Ministry of Child Welfare and Basic Education, Gaborone. The Consultant will work in close coordination with PDU and MCWBE staff and liaise with the World Bank task team, as required.

The Ministry of Child Welfare and Basic Education now invites eligible individual consultants to indicate their interest in providing the services. Interested consultants must provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services.

The Consultant shall have: 

  • At least a master’s degree in economics, social sciences, law, business administration, management or a related field. Background in engineering/architecture will be an added advantage.
  • At least 8 years of experience in Project Management and monitoring.
  • At least 3 years of direct relevant experience in preparing similar POMs, particularly in projects implemented in sub-Saharan Africa.
  • Knowledge and experience of World Bank procedures and familiarity with World Bank financed projects.
  • Knowledge of Botswana’s education system.
  • Ability to deliver under tight deadlines and produce high quality outputs.
  • Strong analytical, drafting, and organizational skills. 
  • Excellent written and oral communication skills in English. 
  • Proficiency in standard office software applications. 

 

The Consultant will be selected in in accordance with the “World Bank Procurement Regulations for Investment Project Financing Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services” (July 2016) revised in November 2017, August 2018, November 2020 & September 2025. A lump sum contract will be signed for the agreed duration of the services. 

 

Candidates who meet the required qualifications will be assessed based on the following evaluation criteria. The first ranked candidate will be invited for contract negotiations.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (REOI)


Arab Republic of Egypt

Greater Cairo Air Pollution Management and Climate Change Project

Loan No.: P172548

Assignment Title: “Updating guidelines for Healthcare Waste Management in Egypt”

Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): EG-EEAA-559382-CS-QCBS

The Greater Cairo Air Pollution Management and Climate Change Project (herein “the Project”) aims at reducing air emissions from critical sectors and increasing resilience to air pollution in Greater Cairo. The Project aims more specifically at reducing air emissions which is a key step toward the reduction of pollution concentrations and improvement of air quality. The Project will focus on two of the primary sources of air pollution in the Greater Cairo (GC) region (i.e., Cairo, Giza and Qalyoubia Governorates): open burning of solid waste and vehicle emissions; and will include six main components aiming at: (i) enhancing the air quality management framework and decision support system in Egypt; (ii) improving Solid Waste Management services; (iii) reducing air and climate pollutants from vehicle emissions; (iv) furthering stakeholder engagement, awareness and communication; (v) project management and monitoring & evaluation (M&E); (vi) addressing the important issue of unintended emissions of POPs.

Brief description about the  Enhanced E-Waste and HCW management for Reduction of uPOPs:                 

 It is an additional finance (AF) to the parent project; this new activity focuses on reduction of unintended persistent organic pollutants (uPOPs) aligns with the “GEF Project Design and Review Considerations in Response to the COVID-19 Crisis and the Mitigation of Future Pandemics”. This new component will comprise 3 sub-components.

Sub-component 6.2: Supporting Effective Healthcare Waste Management, Models, and Solutions has been designed under the proposed Greater Cairo Air Pollution Management and Climate Change project (P172548).

This sub-component aims to strengthen the enabling environment for sustainable healthcare waste (HCW) management. It seeks to develop and pilot innovative solutions to reduce unintentional Persistent Organic Pollutants (uPOPs) emissions and promote long-term systemic changes in HCW practices across Egypt.

Key activities under this sub-component include:

(i)         developing and modeling public/private financing and investment models for collection and treatment of HCW.

(ii)        providing technical assistance to select healthcare institutions on utilization of possible financial mechanisms, procurement of environmentally-sound equipment, training of staff, and integration with the new protocols and facilities.

(iii)       supporting the preparation of a plan to roll out proper HCW management throughout the country in collaboration with key agencies and stakeholders (including women and other vulnerable communities).

(iv)       pilot appropriate recycling and re-sale of safely segregated HCW.

The requested services covered by these terms of reference are to support the Project Coordination Unit (PCU) and the Technical Implementation Units (TIUs) of “Greater Cairo Air Pollution Management and Climate Change (GGAP&CC) Project” in the implementation of the service of Developing Guidelines for the Healthcare Waste Management in Egypt

The Project now invites eligible consultancy firms to indicate their interest in providing the services. Interested suppliers should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the scope.

The expected duration of the assignment is 12 months

Scope of Work:

The selected Consultant will be required to:

1. Review Existing Institutional Framework

  • Assess the roles and responsibilities of existing committees (for example, the Hazardous Waste Materials Committee in MOH, Committee 53 on Hazardous Materials and Waste in WMRA, Technology Accreditation Committee in MOH, and Egyptian Drug Authority (EDA)) within each relevant entity to ensure integration and effective coordination among stakeholders.

2. Review Existing Legal Guidelines

  • Review and update the existing HCWM guidelines developed under the GEF Medical and E-waste Project (2018), incorporating legislative and institutional updates, including the roles and responsibilities of all relevant authorities and stakeholders (WMRA, EEAA, MOHP, MOHE, EDA) involved in healthcare waste management. Identify gaps and areas requiring updates based on current regulations and practices.

3. Stakeholder Engagement

  • Collect and consolidate requirements, standards, and procedures from key entities such as WMRA, EEAA, MOHP, EDA, Ministry of higher education (MOHE), and other relevant stakeholders.
  • Organize consultations and workshops with stakeholders to gather feedback and ensure alignment.

4. Review HCW audit report conducted for the Ain Shams Specialized and French Kasr elany hospitals conducted within project.

  • The consultant should review and take into consideration the findings of the healthcare waste audit report conducted in this project at the two hospitals under study.

5. Update Existing Guidelines

  • Draft comprehensive HCWM guidelines incorporating:
    • National regulations and policies.
    • Input from stakeholders.
  • Address all stages of HCWM, including generation, identification, segregation, storage, transportation, treatment, and disposal.

6. Validation and Finalization

  • Circulate the draft guidelines to stakeholders (WMRA, EEAA, MOHP, MOHE, EDA) for validation and feedback.
  • Revise and finalize the guidelines based on received input.
  • Organize a workshop with all stakeholders to present the final version.

Deliverables:

  • A detailed work plan outlining the timeline for the proposed tasks.
  • Report on the review of existing guidelines and identified gaps.
  • Stakeholder consultation report summarizing collected inputs and feedback.
  • Draft  healthcare waste management guideline for adoption by the Ministry of Local development and Environment in coordination with the relevant competent authorities. Submit a concise "Key Issues and Resolution Report" outlining:

 (i) the main gaps and inconsistencies identified in the existing HCWM guidelines and how they have been addressed in the updated draft; and

 (ii) the key improvements and strengthened provisions introduced, together with a brief rationale for each revision.

  • Final updated guidelines, incorporating all feedback and aligning with national and international standards.

  • Component 2: Enhancing the learning environment
  • Component 3: Strengthening system capacity for quality education service delivery 
  • Component 4: Project management and implementation support

 

The Ministry of Child Welfare and Basic Education (MCWBE) is the implementing entity for the Project. Specifically, the PDU will be responsible for ensuring that implementation of social risk management activities is conducted in an efficient, transparent, and compliant manner. To strengthen implementation capacity and support timely delivery, the MCWBE seeks to engage an Individual Social Development Consultant as a core member of the PDU.

 

The objective of this assignment is to ensure that project activities comply with relevant national regulatory requirements as well as the World Bank's Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) and applicable Environmental and Social Standards (ESSs). This includes identifying and mitigating potential social risks, instrument preparation, monitoring, and reporting, overseeing stakeholder engagement and grievance redress processes, and building the capacity of MCWBE to manage social issues effectively throughout project implementation.

 

The Social Development Consultant will perform duties that include, but are not limited to, the following:

  • Social Risk Management: (i) Support PDU in establishing social risk management systems, screening tools, and procedures in line with Project Environmental and Social Commitment Plan (ESCP) requirements, including contributions to the Project Operations Manual (POM); (ii) lead or support the preparation of E&S instruments required under the ESCP and oversee fulfillment of ESF commitments, review site-specific Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP), conduct field visits, and maintain supervision records; and (iii) ensure E&S requirements (ESMP, LMP, Code of Conduct) are reflected in bidding documents and contracts prior to issuance; review contractor-submitted E&S plans and verify implementation on site. 
  • Gender Based Violence (GBV) and SEA/SH (Sexual Exploitation and Abuse and Sexual Harassment): Work closely with the GBV Specialist on the development and implementation of the SEA/SH Action Plan, and its integration into project activities.
  • Stakeholder Engagement: Implement the Stakeholder Engagement Plan (SEP), lead consultations with stakeholders including communities, schools, and government partners, and ensure inclusion of vulnerable groups.
  • Grievance Redress Mechanism: Facilitate establishment and operation of an accessible GRM, with appropriate channels to receive SEA/SH complaints, monitor resolution of complaints, and ensure confidential handling of SEA/SH cases, including adequate dissemination of information regarding GRM reporting channels to stakeholders and affected communities.
  • Labor and Working Conditions: Monitor contractor compliance with Labor Management Procedures (LMP) under ESS2.
  • Monitoring, Reporting, and Capacity Building: Prepare quarterly monitoring reports, contribute to mid-term and final evaluations, and strengthen capacity for MCWBE staff, school administrators, and project partners on E&S requirements. Develop guidance notes, checklists, and practical tools to support social risk management of the project.
  • Perform any other related tasks assigned by the supervisor within the scope of the assignment.

 

The Social Development Consultant will work as an integral member of the PDU and report to the Project Coordinator. The Social Development Consultant will work in close day-to-day coordination with the Environmental Consultant, GBV Consultant and other PDU staff and will maintain regular communication with the MCWBE and the World Bank Social Specialist assigned to the project.

 

The duration of the assignment is an initial period of 2 years from contract signature with a probationary period of three (3) months. A formal performance evaluation shall be conducted at the end of the first twelve (12) months by the MCWBE evaluation committee. Continuation of the contract for the second year shall be subject to a satisfactory performance assessment and availability of project funding. The performance assessment will consider, among other factors, the quality and timeliness of deliverables, compliance with the Terms of Reference, and overall effectiveness in supporting project implementation. After the initial period of 2 years, the contract will be renewable for the duration of the project based on satisfactory performance and project needs. The Ministry of Child Welfare and Basic Education now invites eligible individual consultants to indicate their interest in providing the services. Interested consultants must provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services.

 

The Social Development Consultant shall have the following minimum qualifications:

  • Master's degree in social sciences, sociology, anthropology, social work, gender studies, development studies, human geography or another relevant discipline.
  • Advanced training or specialization in areas such as social risk management, stakeholder engagement; training in gender and social inclusion will be an added advantage.
  • At least 5 years of relevant professional experience in social development, social safeguards, or related fields in the context of development projects.
  • Proven experience with infrastructure projects, with education sector experience being highly desirable.
  • Demonstrated experience with social sustainability issues in education sector or infrastructure projects, including gender mainstreaming, GBV prevention and response, inclusion of vulnerable groups, stakeholder engagement, and community grievance redress mechanisms.
  • Experience implementing and monitoring social risk management instruments (Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP), Stakeholder Engagement Plan (SEP), Resettlement Action Plan (RAP), Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM)) in projects financed by the World Bank or other international financial institutions.
  • Solid understanding of the Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) and Environmental and Social Standards (ESSs).
  • Experience working in Botswana or the Southern Africa sub-region is strongly desirable.
  • Familiarity with Botswana's national legislation on social protection, gender, labor, and child welfare is an advantage.
  • Ability and willingness to undertake regular field travel.
  • Strong analytical, communication, and report-writing skills in English and Setswana.
  • Excellent interpersonal and facilitation skills, with demonstrated ability to engage diverse stakeholders including government officials, school communities, civil society, and vulnerable groups.
  • Computer literacy, including proficiency in standard office software and data management tools.

 

The position offers competitive remuneration for the selected individual.

The attention of interested consultants is drawn to Section 111, paragraphs 3.14,3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IFP Borrowers (February 2025 version), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

The Project Development Objective (PDO) is to increase participation in preprimary and senior secondary education and improve learning conditions in supported schools, particularly at the junior secondary level. The Project consists of the following four components:

Specifically, the PDU will be responsible for ensuring that implementation of Environmental risk management activities are conducted in an efficient, transparent, and compliant manner. To strengthen implementation capacity and support timely delivery, the MCWBE seeks to engage an Individual Environmental Consultant as a core member of the PDU.

 

The objective of the assignment is to provide dedicated environmental risk management support to the PDU, to ensure that all project activities are prepared and implemented in compliance with the World Bank's Environmental and Social Standards (ESSs), WBG Environmental Health and Safety (EHS) Guidelines, and Botswana's national environmental regulatory framework. The consultant will be the primary technical resource for environmental risk identification, instrument preparation, monitoring, and reporting across various project activities, overseeing stakeholder engagement and grievance redress processes, and building the capacity of MCWBE to manage environmental issues effectively throughout project implementation.

 

The Environmental Consultant will perform duties that include, but are not limited to, the following:

  • Support the PDU in establishing environmental risk management systems, screening tools, and procedures in line with Project Environmental and Social Commitment Plan (ESCP) requirements, including contributions to the Project Operations Manual (POM).
  • Lead or support the preparation of E&S instruments required under the ESCP — including the project-level Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP), site-specific Contractor ESMPs (C-ESMPs) — ensuring coverage of key risks such as construction Occupational Health and Safety (OHS), community health and safety (CHS), waste management, Asbestos Management, including life and fire safety (LFS) plans for school facilities, and other project-specific risks, in compliance with applicable World Bank ESSs, WBG EHS Guidelines, and Botswana’s national environmental regulations.
  • Ensure E&S requirements (ESMP, LMP, Code of Conduct) are reflected in bidding documents and contracts prior to issuance; review and approve Contractor ESMPs prior to site mobilization at each location and monitor implementation on site.
  • Conduct regular field visits to monitor ESMP compliance, OHS and CHS performance, and contractor adherence to agreed E&S measures across project sites.
  • Notify his/her supervisor and the World Bank of any serious environmental, OHS, or CHS incident; participate in investigations and prepare corrective action plans per ESCP timelines.
  • Prepare and submit quarterly E&S monitoring reports and provide environmental inputs to World Bank supervision missions and implementation status reports.
  • Support implementation of the Stakeholder Engagement Plan (SEP) on environmental matters, facilitate community consultations at project sites, and ensure timely in-country disclosure of all cleared E&S instruments.
  • Develop and deliver training for PDU staff, supervision engineers, contractors, and government counterparts on ESF requirements, ESMP implementation, OHS, and other relevant topics.
  • Work closely with the Social Consultant / GBV Consultant and liaise regularly with the World Bank Environmental and Social Specialists, national regulatory agencies, and other relevant stakeholders.
  • Undertake any other tasks related to the environmental management of the project, including the preparation for complaints recorded in the project’s Grievance Redress System (GRS) as well as others that the project and the Bank could receive.

 

The Consultant will work as an integral member of the PDU and report to the Project Coordinator. The Consultant will work in close day-to-day coordination with the Social Specialist, GBV Specialist and other PDU staff and will maintain regular communication with MCWBE, and the World Bank Environmental and Social Specialists assigned to the project.

 

The duration of the assignment is an initial period of 2 years from contract signature with a probationary period of three (3) months. A formal performance evaluation shall be conducted at the end of the first twelve (12) months by the MCWBE evaluation committee. Continuation of the contract for the second year shall be subject to a satisfactory performance assessment and availability of project funding. The performance assessment will consider, among other factors, the quality and timeliness of deliverables, compliance with the Terms of Reference, and overall effectiveness in supporting project implementation. After the initial period of 2 years, the contract will be renewable for the duration of the project based on satisfactory performance and project needs.

 

The Ministry of Child Welfare and Basic Education now invites eligible individual consultants to indicate their interest in providing the services. Interested consultants must provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services.

The required qualifications and experience for shortlisting are as follows:

  • A minimum of a Bachelor's degree (BSc) in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Natural Resource Management, or related field. A Master's degree (MSc) in a relevant discipline is an advantage.
  • A minimum of 5 years professional experience of which at least 2 years involve construction – stage environmental monitoring, including environmental assessment, preparation of environmental risk management instruments, and monitoring.
  • Proven experience with infrastructure projects (education sector experience is highly desirable).
  • Experience preparing and implementing Environmental and Social Management Plans (ESMPs) or equivalent environmental instruments.
  • Prior experience working under the World Bank's Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) or predecessor Operational Policies (Safeguards) and/or under other donor funded projects is a strong advantage.
  • Demonstrated experience in OHS management in civil works; a relevant OHS certification (e.g., NEBOSH, IOSH, or equivalent) is an advantage.
  • Proven experience with Botswana’s national environmental policies, laws, and institutional frameworks.
  • Ability and willingness to undertake regular field travel.
  • Strong technical writing skills, with proven ability to prepare clear, well-structured E&S reports and instruments in English.
  • Strong organizational and coordination skills, with ability to manage multiple sites and stakeholders simultaneously.
  • Computer literacy, including proficiency in standard office software and data management tools.

  • Prepare project’s annual cash plan on the basis of the work plan and related procurement plan.
  • In accordance with the Government of Botswana’s budgeting rules and regulations, prepare annual budget estimates and revise estimates based on work plan/cash plan. Submit the estimates to MCWBE for inclusion in the annual budget in accordance with the annual Ministry of Finance budget call circular for the relevant year. Follow-up and periodically report on the release of funds for the approved budget.
  • Prepare timely annual and quarterly disbursement forecasts for all components of the Project in line with the Project’s procurement plan.
  • Ensure adequate funds are allocated in the MCWBE budget for Project activities supported through Performance Based Conditions (PBCs) and timely releases to associated parastatals.

 

  1. Funds Management
  • Ensure compliance with the internal control framework (Operations Manual and the Bank’s fiduciary guidelines, etc.) and Government of Botswana’s rules and procedures when processing payments.
  • Analyze, plan, design, implement and monitor GABS to augment internal controls in line with best practices in the process of payment and expenditure management.
  • Ensure compliance with accounting policies and practices as stipulated in the accounting regulations and procedures agreed for the Project.
  • Manage financial aspects of the contracts under implementation, including payment terms, purchase orders and variation orders.
  • . Executing comprehensive bank reconciliations and conducting timely follow-up on all identified reconciling items.
  • Liaise with MCWBE officials and World Bank in overseeing and managing Project bank accounts established for the implementation of activities under the Project.

 

 

  1. Expenditure/Payment Processing
  • Ensure that only eligible payments are forwarded for the Project Coordinator’s approval and drawing funds from the designated accounts.
  • Apply pre-audit checks on all payments before payment from designated accounts including budget availability, sanction of competent authority and compliance with applicable financial rules and regulations.
  • Facilitate issuance of a “No Objection Letter” by the Bank as necessary.
  • Prepare monthly bank reconciliation statements of designated accounts in Pula and United States Dollars (USD).
  • Prepare monthly payroll and submit to the Project Coordinator for approval, prior to making any payment under salaries.
  • Ensure that payments for all Project related expenditures are made in a timely manner.

 

 

  1. Accounting and Records Management
  • Maintain all project accounting books and records strictly on a cash basis.
  • Record all transactions timely and accurately in the books of accounts in the local currency and ensure that no expenditure remains unaccounted for.
  • Process monthly project payroll, enforcing proper payroll controls, and executing direct bank account transfers for eligible employees.
  • Ensure that the fixed assets records are maintained for the project, identifying the location and the user of each asset and arrange for the annual and periodical inventory of the assets and updating the records.
  • Ensure the safe custody of all financial records for review by Bank Missions, third party monitoring agents and external and internal auditors.

 

  1. Financial Reporting
  • Prepare and submit to the Bank, no later than 45 days after the end of each calendar quarter, interim unaudited financial reports (IFRs) for the Project covering the quarter in form and substance acceptable to the Bank. The IFRs will include quarterly cash forecasts, prepared in coordination with the project team and submitted to the World Bank for advance and replenishments of advance.
  • Prepare and process withdrawal applications in accordance with the Bank’s Disbursement Guidelines.
  • Ensure that all government financial reporting requirements are complied with.
  • Prepare monthly financial reports based on standard accounting principles with all necessary qualification documentation (invoice, bank drafts, bank reconciliations etc.)

 

  1. Audit
  • Arrange for annual external audit of program accounts in accordance with provision in the Loan Agreement and World Bank requirements and ensure that the report produced is in compliance with the audit requirements of the Bank.
  • Attend entry and exit meetings with external auditors, facilitate timely completion of audits by arranging timely submission of annual financial statements in the appropriate format, supply information and documents in response to queries, initiate actions for holding tripartite meetings and coordinate with various units in meeting audit objectives.
  • Ensure audit matters are resolved on timely basis.
  • Prepare audit schedules and files.
  • Collaborate with the World Bank and Government of Botswana to improve Project financial management, particularly in terms of following up on the action points agreed to in the project’s legal documents, during the Bank’s supervision missions, aide memoires and the recommendations of external and internal auditors.

 

  1. Perform any other procurementrelated tasks assigned by the supervisor within the scope of the assignment.

 

The Consultant will work as an integral member of the PDU and report to the Project Coordinator. The Consultant will work in close coordination with PDU and MCWBE staff and liaise with the World Bank task team, as required.

 

The duration of the assignment is an initial period of 2 years from contract signature with a probationary period of three (3) months. data.institution: Ministry of Child Welfare and Basic Education
data.notice_text:
The Government of Botswana is undertaking the Promoting Participation and Enhancing Learning (PROPEL) (P513800) project supported by the World Bank.

The Project Development Objective (PDO) is to increase participation in preprimary and senior secondary education and improve learning conditions in supported schools, particularly at the junior secondary level. The Project consists of the following four components:

  • Component 1: Increasing participation in education
  • Component 2: Enhancing the learning environment
  • Component 3: Strengthening system capacity for quality education service delivery 
  • Component 4: Project management and implementation support

 

The Ministry of Child Welfare and Basic Education (MCWBE) is the implementing entity for the Project. A Project Delivery Unit (PDU) (or Program Coordinating Unit) is being established within MCWBE to support the effective implementation of project activities, including procurement and contract administration; monitoring, evaluation and reporting of progress under the project; fiduciary management; and environmental and social safeguards management. Specifically, the PDU will be responsible for ensuring that procurement activities are conducted in an efficient, transparent, and compliant manner. To strengthen implementation capacity and support timely delivery, the Client seeks to engage an Individual Procurement Consultant as a core member of the PDU.

The objective of this assignment is to provide handson procurement support to the PDU to ensure that the procurement of goods, works, non-consulting services and consulting services is carried out in full compliance with the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (as applicable), the approved procurement arrangements, and good international procurement practice.

 

The Procurement Consultant shall support the PDU throughout the entire procurement cycle, including planning, preparation, processing, contract award, and contract administration. The Consultant’s responsibilities include, but are not limited to, the following:

The Consultant will work as an integral member of the PDU and report to the Project Coordinator. The Consultant will work in close coordination with PDU and MCWBE staff and liaise with the World Bank task team, as required.

data.notice_text:
REPUBLIC OF ANGOLA

MINISTRY OF SOCIAL ACTION, FAMILY AND THE ADVANCEMENT OF WOMEN

PROJECT TO STRENGTHEN THE SOCIAL PROTECTION SYSTEM FOR HUMAN CAPITAL AND RESILIENCE

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS)

Consultancy Services: Assessment and Specification of Equipment Required for the Single Social Registry (CSU)

Reference No.: SCEXT-SER 06-2025

The Republic of Angola, through the Ministry of Social Action, Family and the Advancement of Women (MASFAMU), has received financing from the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD), under Loan No. IBRD-97180, to support the implementation of the Project to Strengthen the Social Protection System for Human Capital and Resilience (P181495). The Project Implementation Unit (UIP-CSU) intends to apply part of the proceeds of this financing to eligible payments under the contract for the consultancy services described in this notice.

The assignment will include, inter alia: (i) assessing and surveying the CSU’s equipment requirements; (ii) evaluating alternatives available on the market; (iii) analysing suitability, performance, safety, interoperability, sustainability and cost-effectiveness; (iv) preparing neutral, clear and measurable technical specifications; (v) defining requirements for installation, technical support, maintenance and warranty; and (vi) preparing a technical matrix and recommendations to inform future procurement. The detailed scope and deliverables are set out in the Terms of Reference (ToR).

The UIP-CSU invites eligible consulting firms to express their interest in providing the services. Interested firms shall provide information demonstrating that they possess the qualifications and relevant experience required to perform the assignment, including experience in assignments of a similar nature and complexity. At the Expression of Interest stage, the assessment will focus on the firm’s qualifications and experience; Key Experts will not be evaluated at this stage.

The assessment will consider, among other relevant factors: (i) experience in assessing, planning and specifying technological equipment and infrastructure; (ii) experience in information-systems integration and related solutions; and (iii) knowledge of information security, interoperability, support and maintenance requirements, and cost analysis. Experience in public-sector and/or social-protection projects will be considered relevant.

The consulting firm will be selected using the Quality- and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method, with an open international market approach, through a lump-sum contract. The procurement is financed 100% from the proceeds of Loan No. IBRD-97180 and is subject to post review by the World Bank. The selection will be conducted in accordance with the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, Seventh Edition (September 2025), and the Procurement Plan recorded in STEP. Shortlisted firms will subsequently be invited to submit Technical and Financial Proposals using the World Bank Standard Procurement Document, Request for Proposals – Consulting Services (Non-Supervision).

Firms may associate with other firms to strengthen their qualifications. Any proposed association shall be clearly described in the Expression of Interest, including the form of association and the role of each participating firm, in accordance with the applicable procurement requirements.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (REOI)

CONSULTANCY SERVICES FOR THE DESIGN REVIEW AND CONSTRUCTION SUPERVISION OF BANSARA IRRIGATION SCHEME, CROSS RIVER STATE

The Cross River State Government has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Sustainable Power and Irrigation for Nigeria (SPIN) Project, and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The overall objective is to provide comprehensive technical support for the Bansara Irrigation Scheme located in Cross River State. The primary responsibilities of the Consultant will comprise:

Phase I – Design Review: Reviewing, updating, and validating the existing detailed engineering designs, hydraulic modelling, structural calculations, technical specifications and cost estimates for the irrigation infrastructure (headworks, canal networks, drainage systems, and access roads and expansion of the scheme).

Phase II – Construction Supervision: Acting as the Engineer representative / Supervisor to oversee civil works, ensuring compliance with approved designs, technical specifications, safety standards, quality assurance, timeframes.

  • Core business as an engineering consulting firm with at least 10 years of general experience in water resources and irrigation infrastructure development.
  • Proven track record of executing at least Two (2) similar assignments involving design and or construction supervision of medium-to-large scale gravity/pressurized irrigation schemes in sub-Saharan Africa or similar contexts within the last 8 years.
  • Technical and organizational capability of the firm (provide structural overview, quality control certifications, and managerial structure).

 (Note: Key Experts’ CVs are not evaluated at this REOI stage).

3. Interested Consulting Firm must be independent of and have no affiliation with any firm bidding for or engaged in the design or construction of irrigation schemes contracts under the SPIN Project.

Assignment Title: Consultancy Services for Geotechnical Studies for a Wind Farm Site

Reference: EOI/MME-PEDU/002/26-27

 

  1. BACKGROUND

 

Botswana plans to harness its renewable energy (RE) resources and accelerate renewable energy development through the implementation of the Integrated Resource Plan (IRP). The Government of Botswana is currently developing renewable energy projects at several pre-selected sites. The Project and Energy Development Unit (PEDU) under the Ministry of Minerals and Energy (the Client) is responsible for the development of these projects. A feasibility consultant has identified a proposed site for a wind farm based on a multi-criteria assessment considering preliminary wind resource data, transmission infrastructure, land use and ownership, and preliminary environmental and social considerations.

 

The geotechnical studies will support the development of a proposed 100 MW wind farm located north of Letlhakane, Botswana. The final coordinates and boundaries of the area to be investigated will be confirmed by the Client prior to commencement of the assignment.

 

  1. SCOPE OF WORK

 

The Client is seeking a qualified and experienced consulting firm to undertake geotechnical investigations to support the pre-development of the proposed 100 MW wind farm.

 

The assignment will include preliminary site-wide geotechnical investigations and, subsequently, location-specific investigations based on the preliminary wind farm layout.

 

The detailed scope, investigation areas, technical requirements and deliverables will be set out in the Terms of Reference provided at the next stage of the selection process.

 

  1. QUALIFICATIONS

 

PEDU invites eligible consulting firms ("Consultants") to indicate their interest in providing the services. Interested consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services. The shortlisting criteria are:

  1. Core Business: Minimum of ten (10) years of experience undertaking geotechnical investigations and related studies.
  2. Demonstrated experience in satisfactorily completing geotechnical investigations for utility-scale energy or comparable infrastructure projects.
  3. Demonstrated experience in undertaking geotechnical investigations for at least minimum two (2) utility scale projects in Sub- Saharan Africa.
