data.notice_text:
Government of the People’s Republic of Bangladesh

Ministry of Social Welfare

Department of Social Services

ISO Component 05: Socio-economic Development of the Host Community

and FDMN through Capacity Enhancement Project

21/1 & 21/2 Bir Uttam A.N.M. Nuruzzaman Sarak,

Shyamoli Square (9th Floor), Shyamoli, Dhaka-1207.

 

 Memo no. 41.01.0000.124.07.029.2026-1208                                                                                      Date:  14 October 2026

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (REOI)

(SELECTION OF AN NGO)

Country: Bangladesh

Name of Project: ISO Component 05: Socio-economic Development of the Host Community and FDMN through Capacity Enhancement Project, (Credit No: IDA-7546-BD & E326-BD)

Assignment Title: Selection of an NGO for Monitoring, Evaluation and Operational Review (Spot Checks) for both Host Community and FDMN activities.

Reference No.: SD-16

The Government of Bangladesh is implementing the Inclusive Services and Opportunities for Host Communities and Displaced Rohingya Population (ISO) Project with World Bank financing. The Project Development Objective is to improve access to human capital services for vulnerable host communities and displaced Rohingya populations. Component 3, implemented by the Department of Social Services (DSS) under the Ministry of Social Welfare (MoSW), supports social care, child protection, and economic empowerment interventions for the Host Communities and Forcibly Displaced Myanmar Nationals (FDMN) in Chattogram Division. Under this assignment, DSS intends to conduct independent Monitoring, Evaluation, and Operational Reviews (Spot Checks) to assess whether child protection and economic empowerment interventions under the ISO Project are being implemented in accordance with approved guidelines / procedures and agreed protocols. The assignment will verify operational performance, beneficiary targeting, service delivery quality, use of systems among others and assess progress toward intended outputs and outcomes.

Purpose

The Monitoring, Evaluation and Operational Review (Spot Checks) will be conducted in a representative sample of locations where ISO Project interventions are being implemented for both Host Community (Chattogram Division) and FDMN populations (Camps in Cox’s Bazar and Bhasan Char). The assignment will cover both Child Protection and Economic Empowerment interventions. The NGO will be responsible for conducting independent monitoring, evaluation and operational reviews to assess operational performance, beneficiary targeting, use of digital systems, adequacy and capacity of human resources, quality of service delivery Relevant indicators will be drawn from the ISO Project Results Framework, as applicable. The assignment will be implemented over Eighteen (18) months.

Objectives

The objective of this assignment is to conduct independent Monitoring, Evaluation, and Operational Reviews (Spot Checks) to assess whether child protection and economic empowerment interventions under the ISO Project are being implemented in accordance with approved guidelines / procedures and agreed protocols. The assignment will verify operational performance, beneficiary targeting, service delivery quality, use of systems among others and assess progress toward intended outputs and outcomes.

 

The assignment will also involve an outcome evaluation of the social care and economic empowerment interventions in terms of beneficiary households’ progress across a set of relevant socio-economic / welfare indicators. Findings from the operational reviews and outcome evaluation would also need to be analyzed from a gender and social inclusion perspective, identifying any differential experiences or gaps affecting women and vulnerable groups, and will provide practical recommendations to support corrective actions and continuous improvement.

The shortlisting criteria are:

The NGO shall meet the following minimum qualification and experience requirements:

  • At least 10 years of relevant experience in monitoring, evaluation, operational reviews, or spot checks of large-scale development programs, preferably in Bangladesh or the region.
  • Experience in applying participatory and verification-based approaches to beneficiary targeting and service delivery assessment.
  • Strong understanding of social protection, livelihoods, poverty reduction, and community-based programs in Bangladesh and similar socio-economic contexts, including experience with government led programs and demonstrated experience with World Bank- or development partner-financed projects.
  • Proven experience in designing and implementing digitally enabled quantitative and qualitative data collection (using CAPI devices configured with KOBO Toolbox, Survey CTO and other similar platforms etc.), including household surveys, focus group discussions, key informant interviews, and field observations.
  • Demonstrated capacity to configure and deploy Bangla-language digital instruments using CAPI / mobile platforms, offline data capture in low-connectivity locations, and routine data quality checks such as back-checks and spot re-interviews.
  • Capacity to maintain a secure database for storing, managing and analyzing all data collected under the assignment, with respondent-level unique identifiers and appropriate access, backup and confidentiality controls.
  • Strong analytical, conceptual, and reporting capacity, with demonstrated ability to produce clear, evidence based, and actionable reports.
  • Demonstrated capacity to analyze quantitative and qualitative data using standard analysis software (i.e., Stata, R, SPSS, Python etc.)
  • Adequate organizational capacity to manage multi location field operations and deploy digitally equipped field teams across multiple districts and camps.
  • Demonstrated experience in monitoring or evaluating child protection, social service workforce, case management, or gender-based violence prevention and response programs.
  • Demonstrated experience of field data collection in humanitarian or fragility, conflict and violence settings, preferably in the Rohingya camps in Cox's Bazar and Bhasan Char or similar refugee contexts.
  • Demonstrated commitment to safeguarding, with an established Code of Conduct and experience of implementing / adopting Sexual Exploitation and Abuse and Sexual Harassment (SEA/SH) prevention and response protocols in field-based programs.
  • The NGO shall also have documented data protection and confidentiality policies for personally identifiable and case-related data, including data relating to children and survivors.

NGOs should submit:

  1. NGOs should provide sufficient information demonstrating their qualifications and relevant experience, including a brief description of similar assignments, clients, implementation periods, contract values, and the NGO's role. Copies of contracts, completion certificates, and other supporting documents are required at this stage.  CVs of individual experts are not required and will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.; and
  2. The JV agreement or letter of intent to form a JV, if applicable.

NGOs may associate with other NGOs to enhance their qualifications and capacity and shall clearly indicate whether the association is in the form of a joint venture or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all members shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. The qualifications and experience of the joint venture members will be assessed collectively, taking into account their respective roles. The qualifications and experience of proposed subconsultants will not be considered in the evaluation of expressions of interest for shortlisting.

The attention of interested NGOs is drawn to Section VII, paragraphs 7.3, 7.21 and 7.29 of the World Bank’s ‘Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers’, Fifth Edition, September 2023 (‘Procurement Regulations’), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

An NGO will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours, i.e. 0900 to 1600 hours. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be downloaded from https://iso.dss.gov.bd website or can be obtained upon request from the address below either by e-mail or in person during the office hours (Local Time: 09:00 to 16:00 hours).

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, or by mail, or by e-mail- procurement.iso.dss.msw@gmail.com) by 12 November 2026 up to 1400 hours (UTC+ 6 hours).

The Procuring Entity (PE) reserves the right to accept or reject any or all EOIs without assigning any reason whatsoever.

  --

REQUEST FOR EXPRESS OF INTEREST
CONSULTANT TO PREPARE A LOCAL ROADS NETWORK FINANCING STRATEGY
REFERENCE NO. CRRCIP-IC-016

The Government of Lao Peoples Democratic Republic (GoL) has received financing support from the World Bank’s (WB) International Development Association (IDA) to implement the Lao PDR Climate Resilient Road Connectivity Improvement Project (CRRCIP), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The proposed of Climate Resilient Road Connectivity Improvement Project (CRRCIP) seeks to build about 300 km of District Roads and Rural Roads in the poor districts of Khammouan, Savannakhet, and Saravan provinces. The MPWT in consultation with the DPWT of these three provinces had identified a long list of proposed roads. About 100 km of roads in each of the provinces will be selected from the roads in this longlist through a prioritization exercise based on aspects which include: (i) passing through a poor district – based on poverty headcount, (ii) criticality of the link for climate resiliency of the network, (iii) connectivity to agricultural areas, (iv) population served by the road, (v) traffic level, (vi) not passing through environmentally sensitive areas, and (vii) no resettlement of more than 200 people (or 40 households) and/or more than 40 households severely affected with 10 percent of productive assets owned by individual household lost in all three target provinces. The proposed project provides connectivity to National Roads and access to the east-west economic corridor between Vietnam and Thailand thus increasing market linkages and contributing towards greater economic gains to the local communities.

The CRRCIP now intends to engage a part-time, suitably qualified and experienced individual Consultant to Prepare a Local Roads Network Financing Strategy. Specifically, the consultant is required to prepare a local road network financing strategy which will include (i) Road Sector Overview and Expenditure Needs, (ii) Review of current Road Sector Financing, (iii) Fiscal and Macro-economic context, (iv) exploring Financing Options and Reform Scenarios, (v) prepare the Road Sector Financing Strategy and Action Plan. This will be a part-time assignment and the Consultant will work intermittently in Lao PDR and home-based. During visits to Lao PDR, the consultant will be based in Vientiane Capital, MPWT. In the course of entire assignment, the Consultant will cooperate with MPWT and in particular with the Department of Roads (DoR) and the Department of Finance (DPF) as described in the Terms of Reference (ToR). The full ToR for the assignment can be found at the following website : https://ppmd.mof.gov.la/opportunities/com or it can be provided to interested candidates upon written request to the email address below.

This will be an output-based contract with part-time inputs, expected to start by February 2027. The Consultant is required to work in Vientiane for at least 50% of the finally agreed time input in person-days. The work plan shall be agreed during contract negotiations.

The CRRCIP now invites eligible individual consultants to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultant should provide information (CV, Expression of Interest, other supporting information, if any) demonstrating that s/he has the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. In order to qualify for this position, the candidates shall meet the following experience and competence requirements :

    At least a Master’s degree in transport economy, civil engineering, road/transport contract management, or related fields. 
    A minimum of 15 years of working experience in Road Sector institutional reforms and Road Sector financing. 
    Preparation / implementation / completion of at least 3 similar projects, including roads’ long-term operation & maintenance (O&M) funding & implementation frameworks and/or strategies.
    A minimum of 6 years of experience working with development partners funding the road sector, including WB, ADB or other international institutions. 
    Experience in Lao PDR or in other countries in South/ Southeast Asia region is an advantage. 
    Familiarity with the GoL road improvement projects and GoL’s administrative and other procedures is an advantage.
    Excellent speaking and writing English.
    Excellent communication skills.
    Ability to work independently.

The attention of interested consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” 4th edition of November 2020 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Competitive Selection of Individual Consultants method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person or by e-mail) on or before 13 November 2026, 17:00 o’clock Lao time (submissions via email are also acceptable). Only the shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

Georgia

Anaklia Rail Hinterland Connectivity Project

Assignment Title: Supervision of Design and Build of a Railway and Related Infrastructure Connecting to the Anaklia Deep-Sea Port

Reference No. GE-GR-577262-CS-QCBS

The Government of Georgia intends to apply for financing from the World Bank towards the cost of the Project, and JSC Georgian Railway intends to utilize part of the proceeds towards payments under the contract for “Design and Build of a Railway and Related Infrastructure Connecting to the Anaklia Deep-Sea Port”, as well as for consulting services (the Services).

 

The Services include “Supervision of Design and Build of a Railway and Related Infrastructure Connecting to the Anaklia Deep-Sea Port”. The Project envisages design and construction of a railway line with its supporting infrastructure, electrification, construction of overpasses and underpasses, drainage channels and pipes, construction of a new railway station “Anaklia”, construction of Khamiskuri junction, reconstruction of existing railway station “Khobi” and construction of service facilities. The Project territory is located between the village Khamiskuri and the Black Sea from East to West direction. From North it is bordered by the rivers Jumi and Enguri, from South – by the villages of Khobi municipality: Tsvane, Mogiri and Torsa. Eastern (about 4km) and Western (about 9km) parts of the territory are uninhabited. Its middle part (about 4km) is populated (the villages: Ergeta, Didi Nedzi and Orulu). The railway line starts at Khamiskuri and ends near the Port area in Anaklia. The total length of the line is approximately 17.74km.

 

The primary objectives of the Consulting Services are as follows: (i) review the Contractor’s detailed design and verify its compliance with the Employer’s Requirements; (ii) function as the Engineer in administering the works contract and execution of all rights and responsibilities of the Engineer in accordance with the “Conditions of Contract for Plant & Design-Build for Electrical & Mechanical Plant & for Building & Engineering Works Designed by the Contractor (“Yellow book”) Second edition 2017, reprinted 2022 with amendments”; (iii) comprehensive supervision of design activities and works carried out by the Contractor to ensure compliance with the drawings, technical specifications and various stipulations contained in the contract documents, with high standards of quality assurance in supervision and in the execution of works; (iv) advise the Client on all matters concerning the contract management and support the Client to have the works completed within the stipulated time for completion and budget.

Digital RMI Project

Assignment Title:  

Reference No.: MH-DIDA-576425-CS-INDV Digital Unit: Government Technical Support Specialist/s 

(Majuro based position) 

 

The Government of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (the Government) is undertaking a major investment program supported by the World Bank under the Digital RMI Project (Project).  The development objective includes establishing the critical foundations for digital government services and the digital economy. 

 

To support the development of digital government services and a digital economy the Government, with World Bank funding support, has established a Digital Unit reporting into the Office of the Chief Secretary.  

The Project is under implementation and closes in August 2028. The Digital Unit is based in Majuro and currently comprises two Technical Support Specialists, with the Director position under open competitive recruitment. Work currently underway includes the migration of government users to Microsoft 365, an Azure landing zone, consolidation of government onto the rmi.gov.mh domain, a new government web portal, electronic signature and workflow tooling, and the first e-Services and Digital ID releases. 

 

The Director of the Digital Unit is now seeking to recruit a third technical support specialist staff member who will help progress the Digital Unit work program and support the rollout of the Microsoft platform, and applications as approved in the RMI Future State Roadmap Report.  The role involves working closely with relevant Ministry(s) to provide technical support for the implementation of and migration to the Microsoft platform and associated applications. 

 

 A description of the Digital Unit’s functions is set out in the position description in terms of reference, and a copy of the Future State Roadmap Report can be provided on request. 

 

The role is based in Majuro.  This is a full-time position and is for a contracted period from 1 January 2027 to 31 August 2028 (with the possibility of an extension), with a 3-month probationary period.  It is expected that the role will commence on or about 1 January 2027.  The remuneration will reflect the fact that this is a contracted role and not a permanent public sector role.

data.notice_text:
Request for Expressions of Interest (REoI)
Individual Consultant Service as Gender and SEA/SH Expert (National)
Country                     : Bangladesh
Name of the Project : Sylhet-Charkhai-Sheola Highway Improvement Project under ACCESS PROGRAM 
Credit No                   : IDA Credit 7786-BD
Assignment Title       : Individual Consultant Service as Gender and SEA/SH Expert (National)
Reference No             : Package No: SP-9
 

1.    The Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh (GoB) has received a credit from the International Development Association (IDA) towards the cost of the Sylhet-Charkhai-Sheola Highway Improvement Project under ACCESS Program. The RHD, an implementing agency of the Project intends to apply a part of the proceeds of this credit to eligible payments under the contract for which this Request for Expressions of Interest is invited.

2.    The Objective of this assignment is to seek the services of an experienced Individual Consultant to work as the Gender and SEA/SH expert to, support the PIU to ensure equitable distribution of benefits across gender, recommend measures for mitigating and managing any adverse gender impacts, including potential impacts related to GBV and SEA/SH. The detailed scope of the consultancy service is mentioned in the ToR. Detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) and other information will be available upon request from the address provided below, either through email or in person. The TOR can also be found at ‘Sylhet-Sheola Project’ corner of the RHD website (rhd.portal.gov.bd).  

3.    The expected date for the commencement of services is January 2027. The assignment will have an input of Twenty-four (24) Man-Months, depending on the need of the Client and satisfactory performance of the Consultant. The Contract period shall be determined as per mutual agreement of both parties. The Contract period may be extended on mutually agreed terms if required as per rules and regulation of WB and GoB. 

4.    The Consultant will be selected using Individual Consultant Selection (ICS) Method (Open-National) following the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (7th Edition, September 2025). The selected Consultant shall sign the contract with Project Director, Sylhet-Charkhai-Sheola Highway Improvement Project, RHD. Interested Applicants are required to provide information demonstrating that they possess the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services. The selection criteria are –
•    Educational Qualifications: The consultant should have an appropriate post-graduate degree in Social Science/Social Work/Anthropology/Mass Communication/Gender Studies/Women studies or equivalent qualification in a related field. Formal training/course on gender planning/analysis/management is preferred.
•    Experience: At least 8 years of general work experience in the area of gender/social development/stakeholder management/grievance management etc., including 4 years of specific working experience on this type of management in development partner funded projects or reputed international organizations. The Gender expert should have specifically worked on preparation or implementation of social safeguards or gender assessments/management for at least 01 large scale Infrastructure development project. Familiarity with and demonstrated experience of applying tools for gender analysis or developing strategies for gender mainstreaming in development projects will be considered as added advantage.
Applicants are required to submit their Expressions of Interest (EoIs), comprising a CV (including employment history with duties and responsibilities) and a forwarding letter describing briefly the reasons that the applicant considers him/her-self best suited to perform the assignment.

5.    The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to the Section III, para 3.13, 3.15, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, Seventh Edition, September 2025 ("Procurement Regulations"), setting forth the World Bank's policy on conflict of interest.

6.    Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours (09:00 AM to 04:00 PM Bangladesh Standard Time).

7.    The authority reserves the right to accept or reject any or all of EOIs.

Expressions of Interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, or by mail, or by fax, or by e-mail) by 1:00 PM (Bangladesh Standard Time), November 25, 2026.

data.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST

 

 

Country:  MOZAMBIQUE

Project:  Mphanda Nkuwa Hydroelectric Project

Agreement: Preparation Advance No. -V522-MZ.

Assignment Title: Individual Consultancy Services to Provision Hydrologist Specialist Project Advisor for providing Project Advisory to undertaking the review of the hydrological studies of the planned Mphanda Nkuwa Hydropower Project.

 

Reference: MZ-GMNK-442364-CS-INDV

 

 

 

The Government of Mozambique (GoM) hereinafter referred to as “the Borrower” have received Advance funds from International Development Association (IDA) towards the costs of the Mphanda Nkuwa Hydroelectric Project, Preparation Phase. The funds have been channeled through the Mphanda Nkuwa Hydroelectric Project Office (GMNK) as the Project Implementation Agency, and GMNK intends to apply part of the proceeds for Consulting Services for providing Project Advisory for undertaking the review of the hydrological studies of the planned Mphanda Nkuwa Hydropower Project.

 

 

The GMNK now invites eligible Individual Consultant (“Consultants”) to express their interest in providing the Services. Interested Individual Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services. The shortlisting criteria are:

 

  1. qualification, experience and skills in providing Project advisory services for reviewing the hydrological studies of hydropower projects;
  2. a minimum of Post Graduate Degree in the relevant hydrological disciplines and must have at least 15 years of professional experience relevant to the assignment.
  3. description of similar assignments previously carried out - must have done at least two (2) similar assignments (hydrological of hydropower advisory services), and
  4. experience of working in Sub-Sahara Africa - at least one (1) of the assignments should be in Sub-Shara Africa - and other regions.

 

Evidence shall be attached as supporting documents for the Expression of Interest.

 

Objective

 

The Project is being prepared for seeking financial support of the World Bank (the “Bank”) and therefore must comply with the World Bank Safeguards Policies and Performance Standards (see the concept project information document stage at the WB website [1]).  Accordingly, the Mphanda Nkuwa Project needs to comply with the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) – Community Health and Safety (ESS4[2]). To this effect two panel of experts (PoEs) need to be formed: (i) Panel of Experts for Dam Safety (PoE-DS); and (ii) Panel of Experts for Environmental and Social Management (PoE-ESM).

Key Responsibilities/ Scope of Reviews

 

The hydrologist will:

 

  1. Review of the hydrological studies pertaining to the long-term inflow to the reservoirs, and spillway and diversion design floods with reference to international criteria. Assess the adequacy of spillway and diversion facilities, also considering increasing hydrological variability associated with global warming. Review of soil erosion data and estimate of sediment yield into the reservoirs, estimated reservoir sedimentation, and assessment of the long-term sustainable capacity that could be maintained by implementing appropriate management strategies. Review of layouts related to sediment management of the reservoirs including sediment flushing.
  2. Review of the design of spillway and tailrace facilities including flow conditions, energy dissipation and need for hydraulic modelling.
  3. Review of the designs of the diversion works, schedule and risk factors associated with diversion during construction and with the closure of diversion works at initial reservoir filling.

 

Expected Assignment Timeline

 

The assignment is for a period of six (6) years, covering project preparation, construction, and initial reservoir filling. The initial contract will be signed for a period of 2 years, with the potential for an extension to cover the full duration of preparation and implementation. The contract will be time-based, with an annual ceiling of 20 working days, subject to extension if needed.

 

Detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained at the address given below.

 

The attention of interest is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank՚s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” - September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting for the World Bank`s policy on conflict of interest.
